questions.stem: A 24-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after being thrown from his motorcycle onto asphalt. After his clothing is removed, a red, raw lesion is noted running along the lateral aspect of his left leg and forearm, which he calls "road rash." There is no deep bleeding, and only the most superficial layers of skin appear to have been scraped away. Which of the following best classifies this injury?

explanation.summary: An abrasion is removal of the superficial layers of skin by friction or compression.
explanation.whyCorrect: Abrasions remove the top layers of skin through friction or compression, as with a "skinned" area of road rash after being dragged across pavement. There is no deep hemorrhage or penetration, consistent with loss of only the superficial skin.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A contusion is hemorrhage into soft tissue from ruptured blood vessels (a bruise) with the surface typically intact, not a scraping away of skin.
whyWrongByChoice.C: An incised wound is a sharp cut or slash that is longer than it is deep, produced by a sharp edge rather than friction.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A laceration is a tearing of tissue by blunt shearing or crushing forces and classically shows tissue bridging, which is absent here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A stab wound is penetration by a pointed object with depth greater than width, not a superficial surface scrape.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 2 of 2: Physical Agents

questions.stem: A 20-year-old man collapses near the end of a marathon on a hot, humid afternoon. He is confused and combative. His rectal temperature is 41.5 C (106.7 F). Which of the following findings would be most specific for his diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Heat stroke reflects failure of thermoregulation, marked by profound mental status changes and cessation of sweating.
explanation.whyCorrect: In heat stroke the core temperature rises above 40 C (104 F) and thermoregulation ceases, so sweating stops. Combined with profound mental status changes, cessation of sweating is the finding most specific for thermoregulatory failure.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Cramping muscles occur with heat cramps from loss of electrolytes during sweating and are not specific for heat stroke.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Decreased blood volume from sweating-related hypovolemia characterizes heat exhaustion and can be seen in several heat illnesses, so it is not specific.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Erythema of the skin is a nonspecific finding that can be seen in many settings.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Shortness of breath is nonspecific and does not distinguish heat stroke from other conditions.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 2 of 2: Physical Agents

questions.stem: A 68-year-old farmer with decades of outdoor sun exposure develops a scaly, ulcerated lesion on his lower lip; biopsy shows squamous cell carcinoma. The ultraviolet B radiation responsible for this malignancy characteristically causes which of the following forms of DNA damage?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reactive oxygen species from radiolysis of water

explanation.summary: UVB, a nonionizing radiation, is carcinogenic through pyrimidine dimer formation in DNA.
explanation.whyCorrect: UVB exerts its carcinogenic effect by causing the formation of pyrimidine dimers, with covalent cross-linking of adjacent thymidine residues. This nonionizing mechanism underlies UV-associated skin cancers.

whyWrongByChoice.A: DNA-protein crosslinks result from ionizing radiation rather than ultraviolet exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Double-stranded DNA breaks are a form of direct damage caused by ionizing radiation, not UV light.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Reactive oxygen species generated by radiolysis of water are an indirect mechanism of ionizing radiation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Single-stranded DNA breaks are among the direct DNA injuries produced by ionizing radiation.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 2 of 2: Physical Agents

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman is evaluated after a house fire. One burn on her forearm appears pale, waxy, and mottled. It does not blanch with pressure, but she can perceive deep pressure and pin-prick sensation over the area. Which of the following best classifies this burn?

explanation.summary: Deep partial-thickness burns reach the reticular dermis and appear pale, waxy, and mottled with retained deep-pressure sensation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Deep partial-thickness burns extend into the reticular dermis, producing a pale, waxy, mottled appearance that does not blanch. Pressure or pin-prick sensation from intact deep Pacinian corpuscles may still be felt, exactly as described.

whyWrongByChoice.A: "Chemical burn" describes a cause of injury from a corrosive substance, not a depth of thermal injury.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Full-thickness burns extend into fat below the dermis and are painless with a leathery eschar, not a mottled dermis with retained sensation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Superficial (first-degree) burns are confined to the epidermis, are erythematous and painful, blanch to touch, and do not blister.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Superficial partial-thickness burns involve the papillary dermis and are red, blistering, painful, and blanch to touch.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 2 of 2: Physical Agents

questions.stem: A construction worker sustains a burn on his thigh from prolonged contact with a hot metal surface. The area is dry, leathery, and white, and he reports no pain when the wound is examined. Which of the following best explains the absence of pain in this burn?

choices.label: E
choices.text: The superficial location of the injury

explanation.summary: Full-thickness burns are painless because destruction of tissue extends deep enough to destroy nerves.
explanation.whyCorrect: A dry, leathery, white appearance with a firm eschar indicates a full-thickness (third-degree) burn extending into the fat below the dermis. These burns are painless due to destruction of the nerves within the injured tissue.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The epidermis is destroyed in a full-thickness burn, not intact.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Vasoconstriction of dermal vessels does not account for the loss of pain sensation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Endorphin release is not the mechanism the source attributes to painlessness in these burns.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The injury is deep, not superficial; superficial burns are in fact painful.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 2 of 2: Physical Agents

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man has a circumferential full-thickness burn encircling his entire right forearm. Over several hours the forearm becomes increasingly tense and firm, and the distal radial pulse weakens. Which of the following is the most appropriate intervention?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Application of a tourniquet proximal to the forearm

explanation.summary: A circumferential eschar can compromise limb circulation (compartment syndrome), treated by escharotomy.
explanation.whyCorrect: An eschar that encompasses the circumference of an extremity can compromise blood supply, causing increased soft tissue pressures, ischemia, and compartment syndrome. Escharotomy is the surgical opening of the wound to relieve pressure and restore blood flow.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A tourniquet would further reduce distal perfusion and worsen ischemia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A fasciotomy opens the fascia and is directed at the affected limb; a fasciotomy of the uninjured lower leg does not address the forearm eschar.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Amputation is not the appropriate first step for a threatened but salvageable limb with rising compartment pressure.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Anticoagulation does not relieve the mechanical constriction produced by a circumferential eschar.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 2 of 2: Physical Agents

questions.stem: A 35-year-old electrician grasps a live wire and is unable to release it because of sustained muscle contraction. He is found pulseless and unresponsive. Which of the following is a recognized principal mechanism of death from electrocution?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Crystallization of intracellular water in frozen tissue

choices.label: B
choices.text: Disruption of the cardiac conduction system

choices.label: C
choices.text: Excessive collagen deposition during wound healing

choices.label: D
choices.text: Formation of pyrimidine dimers in epidermal DNA

choices.label: E
choices.text: Radiolysis of intracellular water generating free radicals

explanation.summary: Electrocution kills through disruption of cardiac conduction, disruption of neuronal activity, or asphyxia from respiratory muscle paralysis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Electrical injury can produce ventricular fibrillation and cardiac arrest by disrupting the cardiac conduction system, one of the three principal mechanisms of death by electrocution. Alternating household current also causes muscle spasm that prevents release of the wire.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Crystallization of intracellular water mediates tissue damage in hypothermia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Excessive collagen deposition causes hypertrophic scarring after burns, not electrocution death.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pyrimidine dimer formation is the mechanism of UVB radiation injury, not electrocution.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Radiolysis of water generating reactive oxygen species is a mechanism of ionizing radiation.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 2 of 2: Physical Agents

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man treated months earlier with external-beam radiation therapy for a head and neck tumor develops progressive firmness of the irradiated tissue and reduced salivary flow. Histologic examination of the region shows narrowing of small blood vessels. Which of the following best explains this vascular change?

explanation.summary: Vessels are sensitive to radiation and undergo narrowing through fibrointimal thickening, with surrounding tissue fibrosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Radiation damage makes vessels undergo narrowing through fibrointimal thickening, and attempts at repair throughout affected tissues commonly result in widespread fibrosis. This accounts for both the vessel narrowing and the firm, poorly functioning irradiated gland.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amyloid deposition is not the radiation-associated mechanism of vessel narrowing.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Caseating granulomas are characteristic of infections such as tuberculosis, not radiation-induced vascular change.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fatty streaks are early atherosclerotic lesions unrelated to the fibrointimal response described after radiation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Neutrophilic vasculitis reflects an inflammatory vasculitis rather than the fibrosing vascular injury of radiation.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 2 of 2: Physical Agents

questions.stem: A 15-month-old child who recently began walking is brought to clinic after being noted to limp. Radiographs reveal a spiral fracture of the distal tibia. There is no other evidence of injury, and the history is consistent with an ordinary fall for a child of this age. Which of the following is the most likely explanation for this fracture?

explanation.summary: A toddler's fracture is a non-abusive spiral fracture of the distal tibia that may occur when a child is learning to walk.
explanation.whyCorrect: Not all pediatric spiral fractures are abusive. The toddler's fracture is a non-abusive spiral fracture of the distal tibia that occurs as a child learns to walk and may present without an inciting event beyond the common everyday falls of this age group.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Although spiral fractures can raise concern for abuse, an isolated distal tibial spiral fracture in a new walker with a consistent history and no other injuries favors a toddler's fracture.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Osteogenesis imperfecta typically produces multiple or recurrent fractures with other features such as blue sclerae, not described here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A pathologic fracture from malignancy would be expected to show an underlying bony lesion, which is not present.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Rickets causes bony deformities and metaphyseal changes rather than an isolated spiral fracture from a minor fall.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 2 of 2: Physical Agents

questions.stem: A forensic pathologist examines a scalp wound with irregular margins. Strands of intact tissue are seen crossing the depth of the wound. Which of the following types of injury is most consistent with this finding?

explanation.summary: Tissue bridging is a classic sign of a laceration (blunt tearing) and is not expected in a sharp injury.
explanation.whyCorrect: Tissue bridging, in which strands of tissue span the depth of the wound, is a classic sign of a laceration caused by blunt shearing or crushing forces. Distinguishing a laceration from an incised wound is important in a criminal investigation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An abrasion is a superficial removal of skin by friction, not a deep wound with bridging strands.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A contusion is hemorrhage into intact soft tissue (a bruise) rather than an open wound.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Incised wounds are produced by a sharp edge, are longer than they are deep, and show clean margins without tissue bridging.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Stab wounds are sharp penetrating injuries that are deeper than they are wide and do not exhibit tissue bridging.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 2 of 2: Physical Agents

questions.stem: A man experiencing homelessness is brought to the emergency department after a night spent outdoors in freezing weather. Several of his fingertips are hard, black, and shriveled with a mummified appearance. Which of the following best describes this finding?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Heat-related tissue necrosis from a burn

explanation.summary: Severe frostbite causes deep tissue necrosis manifesting as dry gangrene with black mummification.
explanation.whyCorrect: Frostbite is the freezing of tissue. Severe cases with deep injury result in necrosis, an example of dry gangrene that appears as black mummification of the affected part.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The injury results from freezing (cold), not heat.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hypertrophic scarring is an excessive collagen response seen in wound healing after burns, not cold injury.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Limited frostbite appears pale and waxy with development of bullae and blisters, not black mummified tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Paradoxical undressing is a behavior seen in hypothermia in which victims remove clothing before death, not a description of tissue appearance.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 2 of 2: Physical Agents

questions.stem: A 7-year-old boy with poorly controlled asthma lives in an older, poorly maintained home. On a home visit his physician notes visible mold on the walls and observes that the child's symptoms worsen indoors. Growth of this mold is most directly promoted by which of the following aspects of the indoor environment?

explanation.summary: Damp, humid indoor air promotes mold growth, a socioeconomic environmental factor linked to respiratory disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: Damp and humid indoor air contributes to mold growth, which is associated with a wide variety of respiratory symptoms, including asthma-related disease. Indoor environment is an important environmental factor with socioeconomic implications.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Carbon monoxide is a poisonous gas from incomplete combustion; it does not cause mold growth.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Excessive cold is not the factor that drives mold growth in the home.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Dryness inhibits rather than promotes mold growth.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Excessive heat is not associated with the mold growth described here; moisture is the key factor.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 2 of 2: Physical Agents

questions.stem: A 16-year-old boy is struck in the anterior thigh by a pitched baseball during a game. Two days later the area is tender and shows a purple discoloration. The overlying skin surface is intact, with no break in the epidermis. Which of the following best classifies this injury?

explanation.summary: A contusion (bruise) is an area of hemorrhage in soft tissue from rupture of blood vessels after blunt trauma.
explanation.whyCorrect: Blunt trauma is a forceful impact from an object lacking an edge or point. A purple bruise after being hit in the thigh with a baseball is the classic example of a contusion: hemorrhage in soft tissue due to rupture of blood vessels, with the skin surface intact. Contusions can involve the skin or internal organs.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An abrasion is removal of the superficial layers of skin by friction or compression, such as a skinned elbow; here the skin surface is intact.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A chop injury combines blunt and sharp trauma from a heavy object with a cutting edge, such as an axe or meat cleaver.
whyWrongByChoice.D: An incised wound (cut or slash) is inflicted by a sharp-edged object and is longer than it is deep; a baseball has no edge.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A laceration is tearing of tissue by shearing or crushing forces; there is no tear of skin or deeper tissue in this injury.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 2 of 2: Physical Agents

questions.stem: A 72-year-old man collapses at home, and family members perform chest compressions for 20 minutes before emergency services arrive. He does not survive. At autopsy the forensic pathologist finds fractures of the sternum and several anterior ribs, along with a tear through the capsule and parenchyma of the liver. Which of the following is the most likely explanation for the hepatic injury?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chop injury from a heavy edged object

choices.label: C
choices.text: Incised wound from a sharp-edged object

choices.label: E
choices.text: Stab wound from a pointed object

explanation.summary: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation can produce injuries to the sternum, ribs, and occasionally internal organs such as liver lacerations.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chest compressions during CPR, although potentially life-saving, are a form of blunt force that can fracture the sternum and ribs and occasionally lacerate internal organs. A liver laceration found at autopsy in a patient who received prolonged CPR is a recognized resuscitation-related injury; a laceration is tearing of tissue by shearing or crushing forces and can involve internal organs.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A chop injury requires a heavy object with a cutting edge such as an axe; there was no such instrument.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A contusion is hemorrhage in soft tissue from ruptured vessels, not a tear through the capsule and parenchyma of an organ.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Incised wounds are cuts or slashes made by a sharp-edged object; there is no history of sharp injury, and the accompanying sternal and rib fractures point to blunt force.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A stab wound is penetration by a pointed object with depth greater than width; nothing penetrated the skin in this patient.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 2 of 2: Physical Agents

questions.stem: A 3-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department by his mother's boyfriend, who states that the child "fell off the couch." Radiographs show a spiral fracture of the mid-shaft of the humerus. Examination also reveals several bruises of differing ages on the back and posterior thighs. Which of the following mechanisms best explains the fracture?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bone fragility from an inherited skeletal disorder

choices.label: B
choices.text: Direct impact at the fracture site during a short fall

choices.label: C
choices.text: Rotational stress that occurs while learning to walk

choices.label: D
choices.text: Severe muscle contraction from electrical current

choices.label: E
choices.text: Violent twisting or pulling of the limb

explanation.summary: Spiral fractures are rotation fractures that, in a pediatric patient with an unexplained injury, may result from violent twisting or pulling of the limb in child abuse.
explanation.whyCorrect: Unexplained bone fractures in a pediatric patient may be an important clue to child abuse. Spiral fractures are a type of rotation fracture produced by torsional (indirect) force, and they may occur from the violent twisting or pulling of a child's limb. A humeral spiral fracture with a history inconsistent with the injury and bruises of different ages strongly suggests inflicted trauma.

whyWrongByChoice.A: There is no evidence of an underlying skeletal disorder, and the pattern of bruising points to inflicted injury.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A direct force produces a fracture at the site of impact; a spiral fracture reflects an indirect torsional force rather than a direct blow, and a fall from a couch does not explain the pattern or the multiple bruises.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The non-abusive toddler's fracture is a spiral fracture of the distal tibia in a child learning to walk, not a humeral fracture in a 3-year-old with bruises of varying ages.
whyWrongByChoice.D: High-voltage electrical exposure can cause contractions severe enough to fracture bone, but there is no history of electrical contact.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 2 of 2: Physical Agents

questions.stem: A 28-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after an altercation. On the left flank there is a 1.5-cm skin wound; surgical exploration shows the wound track extends 8 cm into the abdominal cavity. Witnesses report the assailant used a screwdriver. Which of the following best classifies this injury?

explanation.summary: A stab wound is caused by penetration of a pointed object and is generally deeper than it is wide.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sharp injuries include stab wounds and incised wounds. Stab wounds are caused by the penetration of a pointed object, such as a knife or a screwdriver, and the depth of a stab wound is generally greater than the width. A 1.5-cm skin defect with an 8-cm track fits this definition.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An abrasion is removal of the superficial layers of skin by friction or compression, without penetration.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A contusion is hemorrhage into soft tissue with the surface intact, not a penetrating wound.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Incised wounds (cuts, slashes) are made by a sharp edge and are generally longer than they are deep, the opposite of this wound.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A laceration is tearing of tissue by blunt shearing or crushing forces and shows tissue bridging, not a narrow penetrating track from a pointed object.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 2 of 2: Physical Agents

questions.stem: A forensic pathologist examines a deep wound of the scalp inflicted with a hatchet. The skin edges of the wound are cleanly cut, but the underlying skull is fractured and crushed, and the adjacent soft tissue is bruised. Which of the following best classifies this injury?

explanation.summary: A chop injury combines blunt and sharp trauma and is produced by a heavy object with a cutting edge, such as an axe or meat cleaver.
explanation.whyCorrect: A chop injury represents a combination of blunt and sharp trauma and includes injuries caused by a heavy object with a cutting edge, such as an axe or meat cleaver. The cleanly cut skin edges reflect the sharp component, while the crushed bone and surrounding bruising reflect the blunt force of the heavy implement.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An abrasion is superficial removal of skin by friction and does not involve deep tissue or bone.
whyWrongByChoice.C: An incised wound is a pure sharp injury (cut or slash) that is longer than it is deep; it does not crush underlying bone.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A laceration is a pure blunt injury with tearing of tissue and tissue bridging; it would not have cleanly cut margins.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A stab wound is penetration by a pointed object with depth greater than width and lacks the crushing component.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 2 of 2: Physical Agents

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman spills boiling water on her forearm. Two hours later the area is red and moist with several intact blisters. It is very painful, and the redness blanches when pressed. Which of the following represents the deepest layer of skin involved by this burn?

explanation.summary: Superficial partial-thickness burns extend to the papillary dermis and are red, blistering, painful, and blanch to the touch.
explanation.whyCorrect: Partial-thickness (second-degree) burns involve the dermis and can be superficial or deep. Superficial partial-thickness burns extend to the papillary dermis and are red, blistering, painful, and blanch to the touch, exactly as described. The combination of blistering with preserved blanching distinguishes this depth.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Superficial (first-degree) burns are confined to the epidermis and are red, painful, and blanch, but they do not blister.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Deep partial-thickness burns reach the reticular dermis and have a pale, waxy, mottled appearance that does not blanch to touch.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Involvement of muscle lies beyond even a full-thickness burn and would not present as a blistering, blanching, painful lesion.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Full-thickness burns extend into the underlying fat and are painless with a leathery eschar.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 2 of 2: Physical Agents

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man sustains a pale, waxy, blistering burn of the dorsal hand in a workplace fire. He reports that he can still feel firm pressure applied over the burn even though light touch and pain over the area are lost. Which of the following structures most likely accounts for the retained sensation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Muscle spindles of the underlying muscle

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nerve fibers within the subcutaneous fat

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pacinian corpuscles of the reticular dermis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sensory receptors of the papillary dermis

explanation.summary: Deep pressure is sensed by Pacinian corpuscles in the reticular dermis, some of which may survive a deep partial-thickness burn.
explanation.whyCorrect: Deep pressure is sensed by Pacinian corpuscles, which are located in the reticular dermis of the skin. In a deep partial-thickness burn (pale, waxy, blistering), some of these Pacinian corpuscles may remain intact depending on the severity of the injury, so pressure or pin-prick sensation may be felt upon examination even when more superficial sensation is lost.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Muscle spindles sense muscle stretch and are not the cutaneous receptors responsible for pressure sensation over a burn.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The epidermis is destroyed in a burn that reaches the reticular dermis, so epidermal nerve endings cannot account for retained sensation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The deep pressure-sensing structures described are Pacinian corpuscles in the reticular dermis, not fibers in the subcutaneous fat.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The papillary dermis lies above the reticular dermis and is destroyed in a deep partial-thickness burn.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 2 of 2: Physical Agents

questions.stem: A 2-year-old girl and her 35-year-old father both sustain scald burns involving the entire head and neck. The burn team uses a different chart to estimate the total body surface area (TBSA) burned in the child than in the adult. Which of the following best explains the need for a separate pediatric method?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Children have a greater proportion of subcutaneous fat

choices.label: B
choices.text: Children have a smaller total skin surface area

choices.label: C
choices.text: Children have proportionally more surface area in the head and neck

choices.label: D
choices.text: Children have proportionally more surface area in the lower extremities

choices.label: E
choices.text: Children have proportionally more surface area on the trunk

explanation.summary: Children and infants have more body surface area in the head and neck and less in the lower extremities than adults, so separate TBSA methods are used.
explanation.whyCorrect: The percentage of body surface area involved by a burn is important to burn assessment, and clinical charts for estimating TBSA vary by clinical situation. Children and infants have more body surface area in the head and neck and less surface area in the lower extremities compared to adults, so a head-and-neck burn represents a larger fraction of TBSA in a child. For this reason, separate methods are used for assessing TBSA in children.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Subcutaneous fat content does not determine the surface-area proportions used in TBSA estimation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: TBSA is expressed as a percentage, so a smaller absolute skin area does not by itself require a different chart; the regional proportions differ.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The opposite is true: children have less surface area in the lower extremities than adults.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The difference described is in the head and neck versus the lower extremities, not the trunk.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 2 of 2: Physical Agents

questions.stem: A 25-year-old man sustained deep partial-thickness burns across the antecubital fossa 8 months ago. He now cannot fully extend the elbow, and the healed skin over the joint is thick, raised, and tight. Which of the following best describes the process limiting his movement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Compartment syndrome from a circumferential eschar

choices.label: B
choices.text: Contracture from an exaggerated healing response

choices.label: E
choices.text: Opportunistic infection of the healed wound

explanation.summary: A contracture is an exaggerated wound-healing response, commonly seen after serious burns, that compromises patient movement.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hypertrophic scarring from excessive collagen deposition after burns can result in cosmetic defects and physical impediments. A contracture is an exaggerated wound healing response that is commonly seen following serious burns and large wounds, and contractures compromise patient movement. Thick, tight scar over a joint that limits extension months after a deep burn is this process.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Compartment syndrome is an acute complication of a circumferential eschar that compromises blood supply during the burn itself, not a late healed-scar problem.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fibrointimal thickening of vessels is a change seen after ionizing radiation, not the mechanism of a burn contracture.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Vascular leakiness and fluid shifts occur acutely after a burn; they do not explain a tight scar 8 months later.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Burn victims are vulnerable to opportunistic infection during the acute period, but the healed, raised, tight skin described is scar, not infection.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 2 of 2: Physical Agents

questions.stem: A 40-year-old factory worker splashes a concentrated industrial cleaning solution across his forearm and chest, soaking through his shirt. He arrives at the occupational health clinic 5 minutes later with burning pain and erythema. Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate step?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Estimation of total body surface area

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neutralization of the chemical with a weak acid

choices.label: E
choices.text: Removal of clothing and irrigation with water

explanation.summary: Chemical burns are managed with prompt removal of clothing and generous irrigation with water to dilute and remove the chemical.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chemical burns result from contact with substances capable of direct tissue destruction, such as certain household cleaners and industrial products. Prompt removal of clothing and generous irrigation of water is recommended for dilution and removal of the chemical to prevent additional damage. Soaked clothing keeps the chemical in contact with the skin and must be removed.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An occlusive dressing would trap the chemical against the skin and prolong tissue destruction.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Escharotomy is indicated for a circumferential eschar compromising limb circulation, not for a fresh chemical exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.C: TBSA estimation is part of burn assessment but does not take priority over stopping ongoing chemical injury.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The recommended approach is dilution and removal with generous water irrigation, not chemical neutralization.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 2 of 2: Physical Agents

questions.stem: A 32-year-old utility lineman contacts a high-voltage power line while working from a bucket truck. Coworkers state that he did not fall and remained in the bucket. In the emergency department, radiographs show a fracture of the proximal humerus. Which of the following best explains the fracture?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Direct force at the fracture site from impact

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ischemia of bone from acute fluid shifts

choices.label: C
choices.text: Severe muscle contraction induced by the current

choices.label: D
choices.text: Thermal destruction of bone at the exit site

choices.label: E
choices.text: Torsional force applied during the rescue

explanation.summary: High-voltage electrical sources may cause muscle contractions so severe that they fracture bone.
explanation.whyCorrect: Electrical current causes muscle spasms; alternating current can prevent a victim from releasing a live wire and produces spasms of the chest wall muscles that inhibit breathing. High-voltage sources may cause such severe contractions as to cause bone fractures. A fracture without a fall after high-voltage contact is best explained by this current-induced contraction.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A direct-force fracture requires an impact at the fracture site, and witnesses confirm there was no fall or impact.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fluid shifts and vascular leakiness are systemic complications of burns and do not fracture bone.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Electrical burns occur where current enters and exits, but the brick attributes fractures in high-voltage injury to violent muscle contraction, not thermal bone destruction.
whyWrongByChoice.E: There is no history of the limb being twisted during rescue; the injury occurred at the time of electrical contact.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 2 of 2: Physical Agents

questions.stem: A 50-year-old man is found dead beside a faulty electrical appliance he had been repairing with his right hand while standing barefoot on a concrete floor. At autopsy, a burn is present on the right palm and a second small, depressed burn is present on the sole of the left foot. Which of the following best explains the plantar lesion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Abrasion from friction against the floor

choices.label: B
choices.text: Contact burn from a hot surface on the floor

choices.label: C
choices.text: Contusion from the fall at the time of death

choices.label: D
choices.text: Exit wound where the current left the body to ground

choices.label: E
choices.text: Fern-like pattern from a lightning discharge

explanation.summary: Electrical current takes the shortest route from the point of entry to the ground, often hand to foot, producing corresponding entry and exit burns.
explanation.whyCorrect: Upon contact with the body, the electrical current takes the shortest route from the point of entry to the ground, often from the hand to the foot, where corresponding burns can be seen. A palm burn on the hand that touched the appliance paired with a sole burn represents the entry and exit wounds documented at autopsy in electrocution.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An abrasion is superficial skin removal by friction and would not appear as a burn.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The floor was concrete and there is no hot surface described; the lesion location on the sole matches the current's path to ground.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A contusion is soft-tissue hemorrhage from blunt impact, not a burn.
whyWrongByChoice.E: An arborescent, fern-like skin pattern is characteristic of lightning strikes, not household electrical contact.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 2 of 2: Physical Agents

questions.stem: A 24-year-old hiker is found unresponsive on an exposed ridge after a summer thunderstorm. His shoes are lying several feet from his body. On the skin of his chest and shoulder there is a branching, fern-like reddish pattern. Which of the following is the most likely cause of death?

explanation.summary: Lightning strikes may produce an arborescent (fern-like) pattern on the skin, and shoes may be blown from the feet.
explanation.whyCorrect: In lightning strikes, an arborescent or fern-like pattern may be encountered in the skin. Examples of shoes being blown from the feet following a lightning strike have also been reported. The thunderstorm, exposed location, fern-like skin marking, and displaced shoes together point to a lightning strike, a high-voltage electrical injury.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Blunt trauma produces abrasions, contusions, lacerations, and fractures, not an arborescent pattern.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Frostbite is freezing of tissue with pale, waxy skin or black mummification, not a fern-like pattern.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Heat stroke causes profound mental status change and cessation of sweating, not branching skin markings.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hypothermia victims may show paradoxical undressing, but it does not produce a fern-like skin pattern, and the setting is a summer storm.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 2 of 2: Physical Agents

questions.stem: A 19-year-old football player practicing in August develops painful, involuntary contractions of his calf and hamstring muscles after several hours of drills. He is alert and oriented, sweating heavily, and his temperature is 37.8 C (100 F). Which of the following best explains his symptoms?

explanation.summary: Heat cramps are painful muscle contractions due to loss of electrolytes from sweating.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hyperthermia may result from increased ambient temperature or exercise, such as an ambitious workout on a hot August afternoon. Heat cramps are painful muscle contractions due to loss of electrolytes from sweating. This athlete is still sweating, has normal mental status, and is only mildly warm, so his cramps are the mildest heat-related illness.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cessation of sweating is a feature of heat stroke; this patient is sweating heavily.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Crystallization of intracellular water mediates tissue damage in hypothermia, not heat illness.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Failure of thermoregulation occurs in heat stroke with core temperature above 40 C and profound mental status changes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Generalized vasodilation and peripheral blood pooling decrease circulating volume in heat stroke, not in simple heat cramps.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 2 of 2: Physical Agents

questions.stem: A 55-year-old landscaper working outdoors on a hot afternoon develops headache and dizziness and then collapses. In the emergency department he is alert and oriented, his skin is moist with sweat, temperature is 39.4 C (102.9 F), pulse is 118/min, and blood pressure is 92/58 mm Hg. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Heat exhaustion is hyperthermia (usually 40 C or less) without significant neurological dysfunction, with headache, dizziness, and collapse from sweating-related hypovolemia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Heat exhaustion is hyperthermia, usually at or below 40 C (104 F), without significant neurological dysfunction. Headache and dizziness may occur, and a patient may collapse to help the cardiovascular system compensate for hypovolemia secondary to sweating. This patient's preserved mentation, continued sweating, temperature below 40 C, and hypotension with tachycardia fit heat exhaustion.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Heat cramps are painful muscle contractions from electrolyte loss, not collapse with hypotension.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Heat stroke is defined by profound mental status changes, cessation of sweating, and core temperature above 40 C; this patient is alert, sweating, and below that threshold.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hypothermia is an abnormally low body temperature.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Paradoxical undressing is a behavior of hypothermia victims, not a heat illness.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 2 of 2: Physical Agents

questions.stem: A 38-year-old man is found unresponsive on a park bench on a January morning after a night of heavy drinking; his clothing is soaked with rain. His core temperature is 31 C (87.8 F). Which of the following best explains how his alcohol use increased his susceptibility to this condition?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hallucinations of warmth that prompt undressing

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased shivering that depletes energy stores

choices.label: E
choices.text: Superficial vasodilation that increases heat loss

explanation.summary: Resistance to cold is reduced by superficial vasodilation secondary to alcohol use, as well as by wet clothes and high humidity.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hypothermia is an abnormally low body temperature. Resistance to cold can be negatively impacted by high humidity, wet clothes, and superficial vasodilation secondary to alcohol use. Loss of consciousness occurs as internal body temperature drops to 32.2 C (90 F), consistent with this patient's unresponsiveness at 31 C.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Crystallization of intracellular and extracellular water is the mechanism of tissue damage once hypothermia occurs, not the way alcohol lowers cold resistance.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Paradoxical undressing results from impaired thermoregulation in hypothermia itself; this patient remains clothed.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Shivering is a protective heat-generating response; the brick links vulnerability to diminished shivering (as in older adults), not to increased shivering from alcohol.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Increased blood viscosity is an indirect contributor to ischemic injury in hypothermia, not an effect of alcohol on heat loss.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 2 of 2: Physical Agents

questions.stem: A 70-year-old woman with dementia wanders from her home on a winter night and is found dead in a field the next morning. Her coat, sweater, and shoes are found removed and lying several yards from the body. There are no signs of assault or injury. Which of the following best explains the removal of her clothing?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Abnormal vasoconstriction and hallucinations of warmth

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cessation of sweating with core temperature above 40 C

choices.label: C
choices.text: Dulled thermoregulatory response to ambient heat

choices.label: E
choices.text: Muscle spasm induced by alternating current

explanation.summary: Paradoxical undressing in hypothermia is thought to result from abnormalities of vasoconstriction and hallucinations of warmth from impaired thermoregulation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Victims of hypothermia may exhibit paradoxical undressing, in which clothing is removed before death. This is thought to be due to abnormalities of vasoconstriction as well as hallucinations of warmth from impaired thermoregulation. An elderly patient with dementia exposed overnight in winter, found undressed without evidence of assault, is the classic presentation.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Cessation of sweating with core temperature above 40 C describes heat stroke, not a winter exposure death.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A dulled thermoregulatory response to heat explains older adults' vulnerability to heat-related illness, not undressing in the cold.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Generalized vasodilation with peripheral pooling is the circulatory derangement of heat stroke, not hypothermia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Alternating current causes muscle spasms that prevent release of a live wire; it has nothing to do with clothing removal in a cold field.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 2 of 2: Physical Agents

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man with burns involving 40% of his total body surface area develops hypotension, tachycardia, and generalized edema during the first 24 hours after injury despite the absence of any bleeding. Which of the following best explains his decreased intravascular volume?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Electrolyte and water loss from profuse sweating in heat illness

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fluid shift into interstitial compartments from vascular leak

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased caloric demand of the postburn hypermetabolic state

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ongoing hemorrhage from deep tissue lacerations of the limbs

choices.label: E
choices.text: Peripheral pooling of blood from generalized cutaneous vasodilation

explanation.summary: Burns disrupt fluid balance through shift of fluids into the interstitial compartments, vascular leakiness, and generalized edema.
explanation.whyCorrect: Among the factors affecting burn patients is disruption of fluid balance due to shift of fluids into the interstitial compartments, vascular leakiness, and generalized edema. Fluid that leaves the vessels for the interstitium is lost from the circulation, producing hypotension and tachycardia together with the edema seen in this patient.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Electrolyte loss from sweating causes heat cramps and hypovolemia in heat illness, not the edema of a burn patient.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The hypermetabolic state after burns drives nutritional needs; it does not itself produce hypovolemia and edema.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The stem specifies no bleeding, and burns are thermal rather than lacerating injuries.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Generalized vasodilation with peripheral blood pooling is the mechanism of decreased circulating volume in heat stroke, not in burns.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 2 of 2: Physical Agents

questions.stem: A 62-year-old woman with a malignant tumor receives external-beam radiation delivered in many small daily doses over several weeks rather than as a single large dose. Which of the following best explains the rationale for the recovery intervals between doses?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cancer cells repair DNA damage faster than normal cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Divided doses prevent fibrointimal thickening of vessels

choices.label: C
choices.text: Divided doses prevent radiolysis of water in normal tissue

choices.label: D
choices.text: Normal cells repair between doses; cancer cells often cannot

choices.label: E
choices.text: Quiescent cells grow more radiosensitive with each dose

explanation.summary: Recovery intervals between radiation doses allow normal cells to repair themselves, while cancer cells often have dysfunctional or impaired repair mechanisms.
explanation.whyCorrect: The rate of delivery and field size affect the biologic effects of therapeutic radiation. Recovery intervals between doses allow normal cells to repair themselves, while cancer cells often have dysfunctional or impaired repair mechanisms. This differential repair capacity, combined with the greater vulnerability of rapidly dividing cells to direct DNA damage, underlies the therapeutic advantage of radiation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This reverses the relationship: cancer cells often have impaired repair, which is why they are preferentially killed.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Vessel narrowing through fibrointimal thickening is a consequence of radiation on surviving tissue and is not prevented simply by dividing doses.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Radiolysis of water and reactive oxygen species generation occurs with each exposure to ionizing radiation; dividing the dose does not eliminate it.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Rapidly dividing cells, not quiescent cells, are the more vulnerable population, and the brick does not describe sensitization of quiescent cells over time.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 2 of 2: Physical Agents

questions.stem: A pathologist examines a biopsy of skin taken from within a field that was irradiated 2 years earlier. Surviving cells show nuclear enlargement with bizarre nuclear shapes, and the cytoplasm is swollen and expanded. Which of the following best accounts for the cytoplasmic change?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Covalent cross-linking of adjacent thymidine residues

choices.label: B
choices.text: Crystallization of intracellular and extracellular water

choices.label: C
choices.text: Distortion of mitochondria and endoplasmic reticulum

choices.label: D
choices.text: Excessive collagen deposition by dermal fibroblasts

choices.label: E
choices.text: Fibrointimal thickening of small dermal vessels

explanation.summary: In cells surviving radiation, cytoplasmic swelling and expansion result from mitochondrial distortion and alterations of the endoplasmic reticulum.
explanation.whyCorrect: Surviving radiation has repercussions for surviving cells. Radiation damage impacts the structures of chromosomes and nuclear material, manifesting as nuclear enlargement and abnormal nuclear morphologies. Cytoplasmic changes, including swelling and expansion, are a result of mitochondrial distortion and alterations of the endoplasmic reticulum.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Covalent cross-linking of adjacent thymidine residues (pyrimidine dimers) is the DNA lesion of UVB, not the cause of cytoplasmic swelling after ionizing radiation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Crystallization of water is the mechanism of tissue injury in hypothermia, not radiation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Excessive collagen deposition produces fibrosis and hypertrophic scarring; it does not swell the cytoplasm of individual cells.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Fibrointimal thickening narrows vessels in irradiated tissue but is a vascular change, not the cause of the cytoplasmic alteration in parenchymal cells.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 2 of 2: Physical Agents

questions.stem: A public health official is preparing for the health impacts of climate change in a low-income coastal region. After a severe storm disrupts the supply of clean water to several communities, which of the following diseases is most likely to increase as a direct result?

explanation.summary: Climate change-related disruptions of the clean-water supply may increase exposure to infectious diseases such as cholera.
explanation.whyCorrect: The WHO estimates 250,000 deaths annually from climate change within 10-20 years based on several factors, one of which is that disruptions of clean-water supply through environmental disturbances may result in increased exposure to infectious diseases, such as cholera. Other cited factors include exacerbation of cardiovascular and respiratory disease, shifting geographic distribution of malaria and dengue, and malnutrition from crop disruption.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Carbon monoxide poisoning is a chemical exposure and is not a consequence of a disrupted water supply.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Frostbite is freezing of tissue from cold exposure and is unrelated to water contamination.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Heat stroke results from increased ambient temperature and exercise, not from loss of clean water.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Squamous cell carcinoma of the skin is linked to UV light exposure, not to disruption of the water supply.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 2 of 2: Physical Agents

questions.stem: An 82-year-old woman who lives alone in a poorly insulated house with a broken furnace is found lethargic by a neighbor during a cold spell; her core temperature is 33 C (91.4 F). Compared with a younger adult in the same environment, which of the following best explains her increased vulnerability?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Greater surface area of the head and neck

explanation.summary: Older patients are vulnerable to hypothermia because of decreased ability to regulate body temperature in response to cold, including diminished shivering intensity.
explanation.whyCorrect: Environmental exposure to cold disproportionately affects those living in poorly insulated structures or homes without sufficient heating. Older patients are vulnerable to hypothermia due to decreased ability to regulate body temperature in response to cold, including diminished shivering intensity, so they generate less heat when exposed.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Proportionally greater head and neck surface area is a feature of children and infants relevant to burn TBSA estimation, not of older adults.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A higher metabolic rate would generate more heat and protect against hypothermia rather than increase vulnerability.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Superficial vasodilation is a mechanism by which alcohol reduces cold resistance, not an age-related change described by the brick.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sweating dissipates heat and is relevant to heat illness; it does not explain susceptibility to cold.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 2 of 2: Physical Agents

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman in a rural low-income region cooks daily over an open wood fire inside a small, poorly ventilated home. She develops chronic respiratory illness attributed to household air pollution. According to the World Health Organization, approximately how many people die prematurely each year from illness attributable to household air pollution from the inefficient use of solid fuels and kerosene cooking?

explanation.summary: The WHO attributes 3.8 million premature deaths per year to household air pollution from inefficient use of solid fuels and kerosene cooking.
explanation.whyCorrect: Indoor air quality has negative effects on health and disproportionately affects low-income individuals. Reliance on open fires and simple stoves fueled with kerosene, coal, wood, and animal or crop wastes diminishes air quality, and negative effects can be compounded by poor ventilation. According to the WHO, 3.8 million people die prematurely from illness attributable to household air pollution caused by the inefficient use of solid fuels and kerosene cooking.

whyWrongByChoice.B: 12 million overstates the WHO estimate by roughly threefold.
whyWrongByChoice.C: 50 million is more than an order of magnitude greater than the WHO estimate.
whyWrongByChoice.D: 250,000 is the WHO estimate of annual deaths from climate change within 10-20 years, not from household air pollution.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 800,000 is far lower than the WHO figure for household air pollution.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 2 of 2: Physical Agents

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man with known coronary artery disease shovels snow outdoors in -10 C (14 F) weather and develops crushing chest pain. In the emergency department a myocardial infarction is diagnosed. Which of the following best explains the contribution of the cold exposure to this event?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Disruption of the cardiac conduction system by current

choices.label: B
choices.text: Generalized vasodilation with peripheral blood pooling

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hypovolemia from electrolyte loss in sweat

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased blood viscosity from crystallization of water

explanation.summary: The vasoconstrictive response to cold can reduce blood flow and contribute to cardiovascular events such as myocardial and cerebral infarctions in medically vulnerable patients.
explanation.whyCorrect: Vasoconstrictive response to the cold can reduce blood flow and contribute to cardiovascular events, such as myocardial and cerebral infarctions, in medically vulnerable patients. A man with coronary artery disease exerting himself in freezing weather is exactly such a patient. Cold air can also inhibit circulation in the lungs and trigger asthma attacks and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Disruption of cardiac conduction by electrical current is a mechanism of death in electrocution, not cold exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Generalized vasodilation with peripheral pooling occurs in heat stroke; cold produces the opposite, vasoconstriction.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hypovolemia from sweating is the mechanism of heat exhaustion, not a cold-weather cardiac event.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Crystallization of water and increased viscosity are mechanisms of tissue damage in established hypothermia; this patient is not hypothermic.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 2 of 2: Physical Agents

questions.stem: A 64-year-old woman with newly diagnosed lung cancer undergoes a full staging workup. The report lists a 3-cm primary tumor, involvement of two regional lymph nodes, grade 3 (anaplastic) histology, and a solitary lesion in the liver consistent with tumor spread. Which of the following findings most strongly worsens her prognosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A tumor that is well vascularized

choices.label: B
choices.text: Involvement of two regional lymph nodes

choices.label: D
choices.text: The 3-cm size of the primary tumor

explanation.summary: Distant metastasis (the M in TNM) is the single most important component of staging and confers the worst prognosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Of the three TNM components, metastasis is the most important prognostic factor, and spread to a distant organ such as the liver carries the worst outlook. It outweighs tumor size, nodal spread, and grade.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Vascularity of the tumor is not one of the prognostic parameters emphasized in staging and grading.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Nodal involvement (N) ranks below metastasis in prognostic weight; two nodes is less severe than distant spread.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tumor size (T) is the least important of the three TNM components and is far less ominous than distant spread.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Grade is an important prognostic factor but is explicitly less important than stage, and metastasis dominates staging.

questions.topicName: Cancer Staging and Grading

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man completes chemotherapy for lymphoma. On follow-up, his physical exam, blood work, and imaging show no evidence of cancer, and the oncologist says he is in complete remission. Which of the following best describes what this means?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All signs and symptoms of the cancer have disappeared

choices.label: B
choices.text: Imaging shows no growth of the original tumor, though symptoms persist

choices.label: C
choices.text: Signs and symptoms are alleviated but not eliminated

choices.label: D
choices.text: The cancer has been definitively cured and cannot return

choices.label: E
choices.text: The tumor is at least 50% smaller than before treatment

explanation.summary: Complete remission means all evidence, signs, and symptoms of cancer have disappeared, but it is not the same as cure.
explanation.whyCorrect: Complete remission means no cancer is detectable on physical exam, blood work, or imaging. It is distinguished from cure because undetected cancer cells may still remain and could regrow.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Imaging showing no growth of the original tumor with residual disease describes partial remission, not complete remission.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Signs and symptoms alleviated but not eliminated defines partial remission.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Providers avoid the word cure because undetected cells may persist even in complete remission; complete remission is not a guarantee of cure.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A tumor at least 50% smaller but still present is a criterion for partial remission, not complete remission.

questions.topicName: Cancer Staging and Grading

questions.stem: A 47-year-old woman is diagnosed with breast cancer. Her oncologist tells her that, based on her diagnosis, 75% of patients with her cancer will not die as a result of their cancer within 5 years of diagnosis. Which parameter is the oncologist using to describe her prognosis?

choices.label: D
choices.text: 5-year relative survival versus a matched population

explanation.summary: Cancer-specific survival counts only deaths caused by the cancer itself over a set period after diagnosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cancer-specific survival is the percentage of patients with a specific type and stage who have not died as a result of that specific cancer in a given period after diagnosis. That is exactly what the oncologist described.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Disease-free survival is the percentage with no signs of cancer during a period after completing treatment, not deaths from the cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Overall survival counts patients who have not died from any cause, not just the cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Relative survival compares survival of patients with cancer to a matched cancer-free population.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The oncologist specified a 5-year window and death from the cancer, not a 10-year overall figure.

questions.topicName: Cancer Staging and Grading

questions.stem: A biopsy of a breast mass is reviewed by a pathologist. Which of the following histologic descriptions most likely corresponds to a high-grade cancer?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cells that form glands and resemble normal breast tissue

choices.label: C
choices.text: Extensive tumor infiltration into adjacent tissue and lymph nodes

choices.label: D
choices.text: Poorly differentiated cells with numerous mitoses

explanation.summary: Grade reflects histology; high-grade tumors are poorly differentiated or anaplastic with marked nuclear atypia and abundant mitoses.
explanation.whyCorrect: Grade describes the histologic appearance and number of mitoses. High-grade (poorly differentiated or anaplastic) cancers lack differentiation, show pleomorphic nuclei, and have numerous mitotic figures.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cells that form glands and resemble normal tissue describe a well-differentiated, low-grade tumor.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Serum tumor marker levels are not a component of grade, which is based on microscopic appearance.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Infiltration into adjacent tissue and lymph nodes reflects stage (extent of spread), not grade.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Well-differentiated cells with uniform nuclei describe a low-grade, not a high-grade, cancer.

questions.topicName: Cancer Staging and Grading

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man has an elevated serum CA19-9 detected during evaluation of abdominal pain and weight loss. An elevation of this tumor marker is most classically associated with which of the following cancers?

explanation.summary: CA19-9 is a tumor marker associated with colon and pancreatic cancer.
explanation.whyCorrect: CA19-9 is classically elevated in pancreatic cancer (and colon cancer). In a patient with abdominal pain and weight loss, a high CA19-9 points toward pancreatic cancer.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hepatocellular carcinoma is marked by alpha-fetoprotein (AFP), not CA19-9.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Neuroendocrine tumors are associated with chromogranin.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ovarian cancer is associated with CA-125.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Prostate cancer is associated with prostate-specific antigen (PSA).

questions.topicName: Cancer Staging and Grading

questions.stem: A 62-year-old man with non-small cell lung cancer is assigned a stage of T2 N1 M1. Which single feature of his cancer carries the greatest weight in determining his prognosis?

choices.label: C
choices.text: The moderate differentiation of the tumor

choices.label: D
choices.text: The N1 involvement of one lymph node

explanation.summary: Among the three TNM components, metastasis (M) is the most important prognostic factor.
explanation.whyCorrect: The M component describes distant spread and is the most important of the three TNM factors. M1 (metastasis present) therefore weighs most heavily on prognosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Tumor markers help track response and recurrence but are not the dominant prognostic component of TNM staging.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Grade (differentiation) is a prognostic factor but is less important than stage.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nodal involvement (N) is important and second to metastasis, but still ranks below M.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tumor size (T) is the least important of the three TNM components.

questions.topicName: Cancer Staging and Grading

questions.stem: A 68-year-old woman is diagnosed with stage 3B non-small cell lung cancer. Using the staging-based survival data, which of the following is closest to her expected 5-year survival rate?

explanation.summary: Higher stage means worse prognosis; stage 3B non-small cell lung cancer has roughly a 5% 5-year survival.
explanation.whyCorrect: The stage-specific survival table lists a 5-year survival of about 5% for stage 3B non-small cell lung cancer, illustrating how advancing stage sharply lowers survival.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 1% corresponds to stage 4 (metastatic) disease, worse than stage 3B.
whyWrongByChoice.C: 14% corresponds to stage 3A disease, one substage below 3B.
whyWrongByChoice.D: 31% corresponds to roughly stage 2B disease.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 49% corresponds to stage 1A disease, much earlier than stage 3B.

questions.topicName: Cancer Staging and Grading

questions.stem: A researcher reports that, for a particular cancer, a given statistic represents the percentage of patients with that cancer type and stage who have not died from any cause within 5 years of diagnosis. Which survival measure is being described?

explanation.summary: Overall survival counts patients who have not died from any cause during a set period after diagnosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Overall survival is the percentage of patients with a specific type and stage of cancer who have not died from any cause in a certain period after diagnosis, which matches the description exactly.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cancer-specific survival counts only deaths caused by the cancer, not deaths from any cause.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Disease-free survival tracks the absence of cancer signs after completing treatment, not death from any cause.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Progression-free interval is not one of the survival measures defined in the source.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Relative survival compares patients with cancer against a matched cancer-free population.

questions.topicName: Cancer Staging and Grading

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man treated for colorectal carcinoma had a carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) level that normalized after surgery. During surveillance, his CEA begins to rise steadily on serial measurements. Which of the following does this trend most likely suggest?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A normal age-related change in the marker

choices.label: B
choices.text: A positive response to ongoing treatment

choices.label: E
choices.text: That the patient is now cured

explanation.summary: After a baseline is established following treatment, a rising tumor marker suggests cancer recurrence.
explanation.whyCorrect: Tumor markers are useful for monitoring after treatment. Once a post-treatment baseline is set, a later increase in the marker suggests the cancer has returned.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The PSA example, not CEA, is the marker described as changing with age; a steady rise here reflects disease, not aging.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A decrease in a tumor marker, not an increase, signifies a positive treatment response.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Complete remission requires no detectable cancer; a rising marker indicates the opposite.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A rising marker argues against cure; providers are already reluctant to use the term cure.

questions.topicName: Cancer Staging and Grading

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man with advanced cancer has progressive weakness, loss of appetite, and marked muscle wasting with more than 5% loss of body weight despite adequate nutrition offered. This hypercatabolic state is thought to account for roughly 30% of cancer deaths. Which of the following mediators are most implicated in this process?

explanation.summary: Cancer cachexia is a hypercatabolic wasting state driven by inflammatory mediators such as TNF, IL-1, and IL-6.
explanation.whyCorrect: The picture describes cancer cachexia, a hypercatabolic state with loss of muscle mass that occurs in about half of cancer patients and contributes to roughly 30% of cancer deaths. Inflammatory mediators including TNF, IL-1, and IL-6 are implicated.

whyWrongByChoice.A: AFP and CEA are tumor markers, not cytokines driving cachexia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Estrogen and progesterone are hormones related to breast cancer biology, not drivers of cachexia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Insulin and glucagon regulate glucose metabolism and are not the implicated inflammatory mediators.
whyWrongByChoice.D: PSA and CA-125 are tumor markers, not mediators of the wasting process.

questions.topicName: Cancer Staging and Grading

questions.stem: A 50-year-old woman receives chemotherapy for cancer. Follow-up imaging shows her tumor burden has decreased by about 60% with no new lesions, but residual tumor is still present and blood tests remain mildly abnormal. Which of the following terms best describes her current status?

explanation.summary: Partial remission means the cancer responded to treatment and shrank, but signs of disease remain.
explanation.whyCorrect: Partial remission means signs and symptoms are alleviated but not eliminated; imaging showing tumors at least 50% smaller and not growing, with residual disease, fits partial remission.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cancer-specific survival is a population survival statistic, not a status for an individual's tumor response.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Complete remission requires that all evidence, signs, and symptoms have disappeared, but residual tumor remains here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cure means no trace of cancer at all, which is not the case with visible residual tumor.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Disease-free survival is a survival statistic measured after treatment completion, not a description of current tumor response.

questions.topicName: Cancer Staging and Grading

questions.stem: A 52-year-old woman is diagnosed with breast cancer, and molecular testing is performed to help refine her prognosis. Which of the following receptor profiles is associated with the most favorable prognosis?

choices.label: E
choices.text: Presence of both BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutations

explanation.summary: In breast cancer, estrogen receptor-positive and HER2/Neu-negative tumors carry a better prognosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Molecular characteristics influence prognosis: estrogen receptor-positive breast cancers carry a better prognosis than receptor-negative ones, and HER2/Neu-negative cancers carry a better prognosis than HER2/Neu-positive ones. The combination of both favorable features is the most favorable profile.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Estrogen receptor-negative removes the favorable receptor feature, worsening prognosis relative to receptor-positive disease.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Estrogen receptor-negative and HER2/Neu-positive combines two unfavorable features and has a worse prognosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: HER2/Neu-positive status is unfavorable and offsets the benefit of being receptor-positive.
whyWrongByChoice.E: BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutations are molecular features that can worsen prognosis and are not the favorable receptor profile described.

questions.topicName: Cancer Staging and Grading

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman completed chemotherapy and radiation for Hodgkin lymphoma 5 years ago. Her oncologist tells her that 90% of patients treated as she was show no signs of cancer during the 5 years after completing their treatment. Which survival parameter is the oncologist describing?

explanation.summary: Disease-free survival is the percentage of patients who have no signs of cancer during a certain period after completing treatment.
explanation.whyCorrect: The oncologist describes patients with no signs of cancer for a period measured from the completion of treatment. That is the definition of disease-free survival; it is anchored to the end of treatment rather than to diagnosis or to death.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cancer-specific survival counts patients who have not died from that cancer after diagnosis, and it does not require them to be cancer-free.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Overall survival counts patients who have not died from any cause after diagnosis, not those free of signs of cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Partial remission describes an individual patient's tumor response, not a population survival statistic.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Relative survival compares survival of patients with cancer to patients who do not have cancer.

questions.topicName: Cancer Staging and Grading

questions.stem: A 72-year-old man with prostate cancer reads that patients with his cancer survive for 5 years after diagnosis at nearly the same rate as men of the same age who do not have cancer. Which survival measure is being reported?

explanation.summary: Relative survival compares the survival of patients with cancer over a period after diagnosis to that of people who do not have cancer.
explanation.whyCorrect: Relative survival is the percentage of patients with cancer who have survived a certain period after diagnosis compared with patients who do not have cancer. A statement comparing cancer patients to a cancer-free group is by definition a relative survival figure.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cancer-specific survival counts deaths from that cancer only and involves no comparison group.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Disease-free survival measures absence of signs of cancer after completing treatment; it makes no comparison to a cancer-free population.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Disease-specific survival is simply another name for cancer-specific survival, which does not use a comparison group.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Overall survival counts deaths from any cause among cancer patients without reference to people who do not have cancer.

questions.topicName: Cancer Staging and Grading

questions.stem: A 56-year-old woman is told that the 5-year disease-specific survival for her type and stage of cancer is 80%. She asks whether this means that 80% of such patients are free of cancer at 5 years. Which of the following is the most accurate response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: No; it means 80% achieved complete remission with initial treatment

choices.label: B
choices.text: No; it means 80% have not died from any cause within 5 years of diagnosis

choices.label: C
choices.text: No; it means 80% have not died from that cancer, although some may still have disease

choices.label: D
choices.text: Yes; it means 80% have no detectable cancer 5 years after completing treatment

choices.label: E
choices.text: Yes; it means 80% survived relative to a matched population without cancer

explanation.summary: Disease-specific (cancer-specific) survival counts patients who have not died from that cancer; it does not mean those patients are cancer-free.
explanation.whyCorrect: Disease-specific survival is another name for cancer-specific survival: the percentage of patients with a specific type and stage of cancer who have not died from that cancer within a period after diagnosis. It explicitly does not mean all patients in the group are cancer-free, only that their disease has not resulted in death by the end point.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Complete remission is an individual treatment response, not what a disease-specific survival statistic measures.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Death from any cause is the basis of overall survival, not disease-specific survival.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Absence of signs of cancer after completing treatment describes disease-free survival, not disease-specific survival.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Comparison to a matched population without cancer defines relative survival.

questions.topicName: Cancer Staging and Grading

questions.stem: A 66-year-old man is newly diagnosed with lung cancer and asks what fraction of all patients with lung cancer, regardless of stage, are alive 5 years after diagnosis. Which of the following is closest to the 5-year overall survival rate for lung cancer?

explanation.summary: The type of cancer strongly affects prognosis; the 5-year overall survival rate for all patients with lung cancer is only 18%.
explanation.whyCorrect: Some cancers carry a much grimmer prognosis than others. The 5-year overall survival rate across all patients with lung cancer is about 18%, far below prostate cancer (98%), Hodgkin lymphoma (86%), and colorectal cancer (65%).

whyWrongByChoice.A: 2% is the 5-year survival for stage 4 small cell lung cancer specifically, not the overall rate across all lung cancer patients.
whyWrongByChoice.C: 65% is the 5-year overall survival rate for colorectal cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.D: 86% is the 5-year overall survival rate for Hodgkin lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 98% is the 5-year overall survival rate for prostate cancer.

questions.topicName: Cancer Staging and Grading

questions.stem: A 70-year-old woman is diagnosed with stage 4 small cell lung cancer. Her brother was diagnosed with stage 1 small cell lung cancer last year and was quoted a 5-year survival rate of 31%. Which of the following is closest to her expected 5-year survival rate?

explanation.summary: Stage is generally the most important prognostic factor; stage 4 small cell lung cancer has a 5-year survival of only 2% versus 31% for stage 1.
explanation.whyCorrect: Patients with stage 1 small cell lung cancer have a 5-year survival rate of 31%, while those with stage 4 disease have only a 2% 5-year survival rate. The same cancer type therefore spans a huge range of prognosis depending on stage.

whyWrongByChoice.B: 14% is the 5-year survival for stage 3A non-small cell lung cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.C: 18% is the 5-year overall survival across all lung cancer patients, not stage 4 small cell disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: 31% is the stage 1 small cell figure her brother was quoted, not the stage 4 figure.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 49% is the 5-year survival for stage 1A non-small cell lung cancer, not stage 4 small cell disease.

questions.topicName: Cancer Staging and Grading

questions.stem: A 61-year-old man with stage 3A non-small cell lung cancer learns that a friend has stage 2B disease of the same type. He asks whether his prognosis is better because his stage carries the letter A. Which of the following is the most accurate response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: His friend's prognosis is worse because the letter B indicates nodal spread

choices.label: B
choices.text: His prognosis is better because the letter A indicates less spread than B

choices.label: C
choices.text: His prognosis is worse because the stage number outweighs the letter

choices.label: D
choices.text: The letter indicates histologic grade, so the stages cannot be compared

choices.label: E
choices.text: Their prognoses are equivalent because both fall in the middle stages

explanation.summary: Letters stratify within a stage; a stage 3A cancer carries a worse prognosis than a stage 2B cancer of the same type.
explanation.whyCorrect: Stages are often written with a number and a letter, such as 2A or 3B, and the letters are simply a system for further stratifying within stages. A stage 3A cancer carries a worse prognosis than a stage 2B cancer of the same type; for non-small cell lung cancer the 5-year survival is 14% for 3A versus 31% for 2B.
