explanation.whyCorrect: TGF-beta attracts fibroblasts and drives extracellular matrix and collagen deposition while suppressing acute inflammation, making it central to fibrosis and later-stage wound healing.

whyWrongByChoice.A: EGF stimulates epithelial cell proliferation and migration, not collagen deposition with anti-inflammatory action.
whyWrongByChoice.B: PDGF is chemotactic for inflammatory cells, fibroblasts, and smooth muscle and helps stabilize new vessels; it does not suppress inflammation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: TGF-alpha stimulates epithelial cell proliferation (like EGF) and does not deposit collagen or dampen inflammation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: VEGF stimulates endothelial proliferation and vascular permeability (angiogenesis), not fibroblast collagen synthesis.

questions.topicName: Wound Healing and Tissue Repair

questions.stem: Granulation tissue forming in a healing wound requires the growth of new blood vessels, and these new vessels are notably leaky. Which of the following growth factors is most directly responsible for stimulating proliferation of the cells that line these new vessels during angiogenesis?

explanation.summary: VEGF drives angiogenesis by stimulating endothelial cell proliferation and increasing vascular permeability.
explanation.whyCorrect: VEGF, produced by mesenchymal cells, directly stimulates endothelial cell proliferation and increases vascular permeability, supplying the new vessels needed by regenerating granulation tissue.

whyWrongByChoice.A: EGF acts on epithelial cells, not on endothelial cells.
whyWrongByChoice.B: IL-6 is a cytokine that helps prime hepatocytes and coordinates inflammation; it does not directly stimulate endothelial proliferation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: PDGF recruits smooth muscle cells to stabilize newly formed vessels rather than directly driving endothelial proliferation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: TGF-beta suppresses endothelial proliferation and migration to stabilize vessels and instead promotes collagen/ECM synthesis.

questions.topicName: Wound Healing and Tissue Repair

questions.stem: A large traumatic skin wound with extensive tissue loss heals by secondary intention. Over about 6 weeks the wound margins are drawn together, substantially reducing the size of the defect. Which cell type is most directly responsible for this wound contraction?

explanation.summary: Myofibroblasts are contractile fibroblasts that pull wound edges together during healing by secondary intention.
explanation.whyCorrect: Myofibroblasts are a specialized type of fibroblast with contractile ability; they form a network within granulation tissue and slowly draw the wound margins together, closing large defects over weeks.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ordinary fibroblasts synthesize and deposit collagen but lack the contractile machinery to close the wound.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Keratinocytes are surface epithelial cells that re-cover the wound; they do not contract it.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Kupffer cells are liver macrophages that provide signals and phagocytose debris, not wound contraction.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Macrophages clear debris and secrete growth factors but do not physically contract the wound.

questions.topicName: Wound Healing and Tissue Repair

questions.stem: A 40-year-old woman sustains deep burns to both hands in a house fire. Several months later, the skin over her finger joints has become tight and taut, and she is unable to fully extend her fingers. Which wound-healing abnormality best explains her limited joint mobility?

explanation.summary: A contracture is an exaggerated healing response, common after severe burns, in which myofibroblasts tighten tissue across a joint and restrict movement.
explanation.whyCorrect: Contractures result from myofibroblasts contracting the healing tissue; when they occur over joints, especially after extensive burns, the skin becomes taut and leads to permanent limitation of joint mobility.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Dehiscence is the reopening of a closed surgical incision, not a burn-related tightening over joints.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A hypertrophic scar is excess collagen confined within the wound borders; it does not typically restrict joint motion the way a contracture does.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A keloid is exuberant scar extending beyond the wound margins, not a cause of restricted joint extension.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Venous ulceration is a chronic non-healing wound from venous hypertension, unrelated to burn-induced joint stiffness.

questions.topicName: Wound Healing and Tissue Repair

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman develops a firm, raised nodule at the site of an ear piercing. The lesion has grown well beyond the original margins of the piercing wound and has not regressed over the past year. Histology shows thick, brightly eosinophilic collagen bundles that are haphazardly arranged. Which of the following best describes this lesion?

explanation.summary: Keloids are exuberant scars whose thick, haphazard eosinophilic collagen extends beyond the original wound borders and does not regress.
explanation.whyCorrect: A keloid occurs when scarring extends beyond the boundaries of the original wound; microscopically it shows thick, brightly eosinophilic collagen arranged haphazardly, and unlike a hypertrophic scar it does not regress on its own and may require excision.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A contracture is tightening of healed tissue over a joint that limits motion, not a raised collagen nodule.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Granulation tissue is soft, pink, and temporary; a firm chronic collagenous nodule is not granulation tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A hypertrophic scar remains confined within the original wound margins and usually regresses over time, unlike this expanding lesion.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Dehiscence is the reopening of a closed incision, not an excess scar.

questions.topicName: Wound Healing and Tissue Repair

questions.stem: Five days after a skin injury, the wound bed is filled with soft, pink, granular tissue that bleeds easily when a scab is lifted. Microscopically it contains proliferating fibroblasts, delicate new capillaries, and macrophages within loose extracellular matrix. Which of the following best identifies this tissue?

explanation.summary: Granulation tissue is the weak, pink, intermediate repair tissue of fibroblasts, macrophages, and new vessels that later matures into scar.
explanation.whyCorrect: Granulation tissue represents the intermediate stage of connective tissue repair; it is structurally weak and named for its pink, granular appearance, with delicate new vessels that bleed easily and proliferating fibroblasts that later deposit collagen.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The basement membrane is a thin specialized ECM layer supporting epithelium, not a bed of proliferating vessels and fibroblasts.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Caseous necrosis is cheese-like dead tissue typical of granulomatous infection, not vascular reparative tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A keloid is an exuberant collagenous scar extending beyond wound margins, not early reparative tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A mature fibrotic scar is a firm, pale, dense collagen structure that is the end result of remodeling, not soft pink granular tissue.

questions.topicName: Wound Healing and Tissue Repair

questions.stem: On postoperative day 6 after abdominal surgery, a patient's closed midline surgical incision suddenly reopens along the suture line. Which of the following terms best describes this complication?

explanation.summary: Dehiscence is a surgical complication in which a closed incision reopens.
explanation.whyCorrect: Wound dehiscence is a postsurgical complication defined by the reopening of a previously closed incision, typically when the wound has not yet gained adequate tensile strength.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chronic ulceration is a non-healing wound lacking intact epithelium, usually from impaired perfusion, not acute incisional reopening.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A contracture is exaggerated healing that tightens tissue and limits joint motion, not a reopened incision.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hypertrophic scarring is excess collagen within the wound borders, not incisional separation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A keloid is exuberant scar extending beyond the wound margins, the opposite problem of a wound coming apart.

questions.topicName: Wound Healing and Tissue Repair

questions.stem: An elderly man whose diet lacks fresh fruits and vegetables presents with poorly healing wounds, bleeding gums, and perifollicular hemorrhages. His impaired wound healing is attributed to deficiency of a vitamin required for collagen synthesis and blood vessel maintenance. Which of the following vitamins is deficient?

explanation.summary: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is required for collagen synthesis; its deficiency causes scurvy with bleeding and impaired wound healing.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ascorbic acid is necessary for collagen synthesis and blood vessel maintenance; its deficiency produces scurvy, typified by bleeding (gums, perifollicular hemorrhages) and impaired wound healing, historically prevented by citrus consumption.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Vitamin A supports epithelial differentiation and immune function but is not the collagen-synthesis vitamin whose deficiency causes scurvy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Vitamin B12 deficiency causes megaloblastic anemia and neurologic disease, not a collagen/bleeding syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Vitamin D deficiency causes rickets/osteomalacia from impaired mineralization, not impaired collagen-based wound healing.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vitamin K deficiency causes a coagulation-factor bleeding disorder but does not impair collagen synthesis in wound repair.

questions.topicName: Wound Healing and Tissue Repair

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man sustains a deep laceration through the belly of his gastrocnemius muscle. On follow-up months later, the injured segment has been replaced largely by fibrous connective tissue rather than by new muscle fibers. Which of the following best explains this outcome?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Skeletal muscle is a labile tissue whose cells divide too rapidly to form organized fibers

choices.label: B
choices.text: Skeletal muscle is a stable tissue that requires IL-6 priming before myocytes can divide

choices.label: C
choices.text: Skeletal muscle is considered a permanent tissue with very limited regeneration from satellite cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Skeletal muscle lacks a basement membrane and therefore cannot support regenerating cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Skeletal muscle regenerates fully only when myofibroblasts first contract the defect

explanation.summary: Skeletal muscle is generally classified as a permanent tissue; its satellite cells give it only very limited regenerative capacity, so repair is dominated by scar formation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Although skeletal muscle contains satellite cells, their regenerative capacity is very limited, so skeletal muscle is grouped with the permanent (nondividing) tissues. After significant injury, its repair response is dominated by connective tissue replacement (scar) rather than by regeneration of functional muscle.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Labile tissues (gut epithelium, skin, bone marrow) divide continuously and regenerate well; skeletal muscle is not labile.
whyWrongByChoice.B: IL-6 priming of quiescent parenchymal cells describes liver (a stable tissue) regeneration, not skeletal muscle.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The limited regeneration reflects the tissue's intrinsic permanent classification, not an absence of basement membrane.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Myofibroblast contraction closes large skin wounds by secondary intention; it does not enable muscle regeneration.

questions.topicName: Wound Healing and Tissue Repair

questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman recovers from a severe bacterial pneumonia. Follow-up imaging weeks later shows the affected lung has returned to a normal appearance, reflecting regeneration by cells that are normally quiescent but were able to re-enter the cell cycle. Which of the following tissues shares this same regenerative classification?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hematopoietic cells of the bone marrow

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transitional epithelium of the urinary tract

explanation.summary: Alveolar cells of the lung, like hepatocytes, are stable (quiescent) tissue: normally not dividing but capable of regeneration when stimulated.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hepatocytes of the liver and alveolar cells of the lung are both examples of stable (quiescent) tissue. These cells sit in G0 and do not continuously divide, but they can be primed to proliferate after injury, allowing the tissue to regenerate.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The epithelium of the skin is labile tissue that divides continuously.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Oral cavity epithelium is labile (continuously dividing) tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hematopoietic cells of the bone marrow are labile tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Urinary tract epithelium is listed among the labile tissues, not the stable ones.

questions.topicName: Wound Healing and Tissue Repair

questions.stem: In a healing skin wound, activated macrophages release a growth factor that stimulates epithelial cells to proliferate and migrate across the defect and also promotes granulation tissue. Which of the following growth factors has these actions?

explanation.summary: EGF, produced by activated macrophages and epithelial cells, stimulates epithelial cell proliferation and migration and promotes granulation tissue.
explanation.whyCorrect: EGF is sourced from activated macrophages and epithelial cells. Its functions are to stimulate epithelial cell proliferation and migration and to promote granulation tissue, making it central to re-covering a wound with epithelium.

whyWrongByChoice.B: IL-6 is a cytokine released by Kupffer cells that primes hepatocytes; it is not an epithelial growth factor.
whyWrongByChoice.C: PDGF attracts neutrophils, macrophages, fibroblasts, and smooth muscle cells and stimulates fibroblast and endothelial proliferation, not epithelial migration.
whyWrongByChoice.D: TGF-beta attracts fibroblasts, drives ECM synthesis, and suppresses acute inflammation; it does not stimulate epithelial migration.
whyWrongByChoice.E: VEGF comes from mesenchymal cells and stimulates endothelial proliferation and vascular permeability, not epithelial migration.

questions.topicName: Wound Healing and Tissue Repair

questions.stem: Shortly after a skin incision, platelets within the clot release a growth factor that attracts neutrophils, macrophages, fibroblasts, and smooth muscle cells to the wound and stimulates fibroblast proliferation and extracellular matrix protein synthesis. Which of the following is this growth factor?

explanation.summary: PDGF, released by platelets and macrophages, is chemotactic for neutrophils, macrophages, fibroblasts, and smooth muscle cells and stimulates fibroblast/endothelial proliferation and ECM synthesis.
explanation.whyCorrect: PDGF is sourced from platelets and macrophages (among others). It attracts neutrophils, macrophages, fibroblasts, and smooth muscle cells and stimulates proliferation of fibroblasts and endothelial cells as well as ECM protein synthesis; its recruitment of smooth muscle cells later helps stabilize new vessels.

whyWrongByChoice.A: EGF stimulates epithelial proliferation and migration and promotes granulation tissue; it is not the platelet-derived chemoattractant described.
whyWrongByChoice.B: HGF is a signal that prepares hepatocytes to enter the cell cycle during liver regeneration.
whyWrongByChoice.D: TGF-alpha, from activated macrophages and epithelial cells, stimulates epithelial cell proliferation only.
whyWrongByChoice.E: VEGF is produced by mesenchymal cells and acts on endothelium (proliferation, permeability), not as a broad chemoattractant for inflammatory cells.

questions.topicName: Wound Healing and Tissue Repair

questions.stem: Within hours of a skin injury, damaged cells and resident immune cells release small signaling proteins that recruit and activate neutrophils, bringing them to the site of injury. Which of the following best describes these molecules?

explanation.summary: Chemokines are a type of cytokine released by damaged and immune cells that recruit and activate immune cells, especially neutrophils, to the site of injury.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cytokines are small proteins that function as signaling molecules coordinating the many cells of tissue repair. Chemokines are the subtype released by damaged and immune cells that recruit and activate other immune cells, particularly neutrophils, to the injured site.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Integrins are connector proteins linking the cytoskeleton to the ECM, not secreted chemoattractants.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Matrix metalloproteinases cleave collagen and ECM components during remodeling; they do not recruit neutrophils.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Proteoglycans are water-hydrated gel components of the ECM providing resilience and lubrication.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Transcription factors are intracellular proteins that regulate gene expression; they are not secreted recruiting signals.

questions.topicName: Wound Healing and Tissue Repair

questions.stem: During tissue repair, certain proteins act inside the nucleus to upregulate expression of genes needed for cellular mobilization, division, and differentiation. Which of the following best describes these proteins?

explanation.summary: Transcription factors regulate gene expression and, during repair, upregulate genes important for cellular mobilization, division, and differentiation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Transcription factors are proteins that regulate gene expression. In tissue repair they upregulate the expression of genes important for cellular mobilization, division, and differentiation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adhesive glycoproteins such as integrins connect ECM elements to cells; they are structural connectors, not nuclear regulators.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Chemokines are secreted cytokines that recruit immune cells; they do not directly act on gene transcription in the nucleus.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fibrous structural proteins (collagens, elastin) provide tensile strength and recoil in the ECM.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Growth factors are extracellular signals that stimulate survival, growth, and division; they act via receptors rather than directly regulating gene expression in the nucleus.

questions.topicName: Wound Healing and Tissue Repair

questions.stem: The extracellular matrix contains a component that forms water-hydrated gels, providing resilience and lubrication to tissues. Which of the following ECM constituents serves this function?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fibrillar collagens types I and III

explanation.summary: Proteoglycans and hyaluronan form the water-hydrated gels of the ECM that confer resilience and lubrication.
explanation.whyCorrect: The ECM components include fibrous structural proteins, water-hydrated gels, and adhesive glycoproteins. The water-hydrated gels, such as proteoglycans and hyaluronan, provide resilience and lubrication.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Elastin is a fibrous structural protein responsible for recoil.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Collagens are fibrous structural proteins providing tensile strength, not hydrated gels.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Integrins are adhesive glycoproteins that connect ECM elements and link the cytoskeleton to the matrix.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Laminin is a basement membrane component, not the hydrated gel of the matrix.

questions.topicName: Wound Healing and Tissue Repair

questions.stem: The basement membrane is a specialized extracellular matrix surface upon which epithelial, endothelial, and smooth muscle cells grow. Which type of collagen is characteristic of the basement membrane?

explanation.summary: Type IV collagen, together with laminin and proteoglycan, forms the basement membrane.
explanation.whyCorrect: The basement membrane is composed of type IV collagen, laminin, and proteoglycan. It is a specialized ECM surface supporting the growth of epithelial, endothelial, and smooth muscle cells.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Type I collagen is a fibrillar collagen of the interstitial matrix, not the basement membrane.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Type II collagen is not the basement membrane collagen; the basement membrane is characterized by type IV.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Type III collagen is a fibrillar interstitial collagen rather than a basement membrane component.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Type V collagen is not the collagen that characterizes the basement membrane.

questions.topicName: Wound Healing and Tissue Repair

questions.stem: Epithelial cells regenerating across a wound are anchored to the underlying matrix by transmembrane connector proteins that link the cell cytoskeleton to the extracellular matrix; signals through these proteins also promote cell proliferation. Which of the following are these proteins?

explanation.summary: Integrins are adhesive glycoproteins that link the cytoskeleton with the ECM, and integrin-associated signals promote cell proliferation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Integrins are connector proteins that link the cell cytoskeleton with the extracellular matrix. They are the adhesive glycoproteins of the ECM, and integrin-associated signaling also promotes cell proliferation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chemokines are secreted cytokines that recruit immune cells; they are not cell-matrix connectors.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fibrillar collagens are structural proteins of the interstitial matrix providing tensile strength, not transmembrane linkers.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hyaluronan is a hydrated gel component providing resilience and lubrication.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Matrix metalloproteinases degrade collagen and other ECM components during remodeling.

questions.topicName: Wound Healing and Tissue Repair

questions.stem: Following a partial hepatectomy, resident liver macrophages respond to damage and local inflammatory signals such as TNF by releasing a cytokine that prepares parenchymal liver cells to register and react to growth factors. Which of the following is this cytokine?

explanation.summary: In the priming stage of liver regeneration, Kupffer cells release IL-6, which prepares hepatocytes to respond to growth factors.
explanation.whyCorrect: Liver regeneration begins with the priming stage. Kupffer cells, the macrophages of the liver, respond to damage and local inflammatory signals such as TNF and release IL-6, a cytokine that prepares parenchymal liver cells to register and react to growth factors.

whyWrongByChoice.A: HGF acts after priming to move hepatocytes into the proliferative part of the cell cycle; it is a growth factor, not the Kupffer cell priming cytokine.
whyWrongByChoice.C: TGF-alpha is one of the growth factors (with HGF and EGF) that drives hepatocytes from G0 to G1 after priming.
whyWrongByChoice.D: TGF-beta acts at the end of regeneration as an anti-proliferative cytokine that returns the liver to quiescence.
whyWrongByChoice.E: VEGF stimulates endothelial proliferation and vascular permeability; it is not part of hepatocyte priming.

questions.topicName: Wound Healing and Tissue Repair

questions.stem: After the priming stage of liver regeneration, hepatocyte growth factor, EGF, and TGF-alpha act on hepatocytes. Which of the following cell cycle transitions do these signals produce in the hepatocytes?

explanation.summary: HGF, EGF, and TGF-alpha move primed hepatocytes from the quiescent G0 stage into the proliferating G1 stage.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hepatocytes are stable cells that normally rest in the quiescent G0 stage. After priming, HGF, EGF, TGF-alpha, and other signals prepare hepatocytes to enter the proliferative part of the cell cycle, moving them from G0 to the proliferating G1 stage.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Returning to G0 occurs when TGF-beta and other anti-proliferative cytokines end regeneration, not in response to HGF/EGF/TGF-alpha.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The G1 to S transition occurs later within the cycling cell; the growth factors are described as moving quiescent cells out of G0.
whyWrongByChoice.D: G2 to M is the entry into mitosis, not the initial exit from the quiescent state.
whyWrongByChoice.E: S to G2 is a later intracycle transition, not the exit from quiescence driven by these growth factors.

questions.topicName: Wound Healing and Tissue Repair

questions.stem: Several weeks after a living-donor liver resection, the donor's remnant liver has regenerated to an adequate mass and hepatocyte proliferation ceases, with the organ returning to a quiescent state. Which of the following signals is most responsible for ending the regenerative response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Epidermal growth factor (EGF) from the duodenum

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hepatocyte growth factor (HGF) from stellate cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tumor necrosis factor (TNF) from Kupffer cells

explanation.summary: Once the liver is adequately regenerated, TGF-beta and other anti-proliferative cytokines assuage the repair response and return the liver to a stable (quiescent) state.
explanation.whyCorrect: Liver regeneration is terminated when TGF-beta and other anti-proliferative cytokines suppress the proliferative response, allowing the liver to return to its stable, quiescent state.

whyWrongByChoice.A: EGF, with HGF and TGF-alpha, pushes hepatocytes into the proliferative cell cycle.
whyWrongByChoice.B: HGF drives hepatocytes from G0 into G1, promoting rather than ending proliferation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: IL-6 is released by Kupffer cells to prime hepatocytes to respond to growth factors, initiating rather than ending the response.
whyWrongByChoice.E: TNF is a local inflammatory signal that triggers Kupffer cells at the start of priming, not the termination of regeneration.

questions.topicName: Wound Healing and Tissue Repair

questions.stem: A 52-year-old man has a full-thickness burn of the forearm that destroys the epidermis, the underlying basement membrane, and much of the dermal extracellular matrix. Although epidermal keratinocytes are continuously dividing cells, the area heals with a scar rather than with restoration of normal skin architecture. Which of the following best explains this outcome?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Burn injury converts labile epithelium into stable tissue requiring priming

choices.label: B
choices.text: Chemokine release recruits neutrophils that prevent epithelial migration

choices.label: C
choices.text: Heat inactivates EGF so epithelial proliferation cannot be stimulated

choices.label: D
choices.text: Keratinocytes are permanent cells that cannot divide after severe injury

choices.label: E
choices.text: Loss of the ECM scaffold forces repair by connective tissue replacement

explanation.summary: Even labile tissues heal by scarring when the extracellular matrix scaffold is destroyed; the extent of damage to the ECM is a key determinant of regeneration versus fibrosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: The extent of tissue damage is a key determinant of healing. As long as the ECM is intact, continuously dividing and quiescent tissues can regenerate, but if the ECM is damaged the tissue will most likely repair via connective tissue replacement (scarring). Extensive injury destroys the interlocking supportive mesh that anchors functional tissue layers.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Injury does not convert labile tissue into stable tissue; the tissue categories are intrinsic.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Neutrophils are early responders that clear microbes and debris; they do not block epithelial regeneration in an intact-scaffold wound.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The problem is loss of the scaffold, not inactivation of EGF; growth factors are still produced by macrophages in the wound.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Keratinocytes remain labile (continuously dividing) cells; the scar results from loss of scaffold, not from a change in the cells' classification.

questions.topicName: Wound Healing and Tissue Repair

questions.stem: A clean surgical incision is closed with sutures and heals by first intention. On postoperative day 3, a biopsy of the wound edge is examined. Which of the following is the dominant inflammatory cell expected in the wound at this stage?

explanation.summary: By day 3 of first-intention healing, macrophages replace neutrophils as the dominant inflammatory cell, clearing debris and signaling angiogenesis and ECM deposition.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the first-intention timeline, neutrophils arrive within 24 hours, but by day 3 macrophages replace neutrophils as the dominant inflammatory cell. These histiocytes clear debris, fibrin, and foreign material and provide signals for angiogenesis and extracellular matrix deposition.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Myofibroblasts are contractile fibroblasts of secondary-intention healing, not the day-3 inflammatory cell of a sutured incision.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Neutrophils are the first responders in the first 24 hours; by day 3 they have been replaced by macrophages.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Platelets form the initial clot for hemostasis and provide early growth factors; they are not inflammatory cells dominating the wound at day 3.
whyWrongByChoice.E: T lymphocytes are listed as a source of TGF-beta but are not described as the dominant inflammatory cell at day 3.

questions.topicName: Wound Healing and Tissue Repair

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman has a small, superficial skin incision closed with adhesive strips. Approximately 36 hours after the injury, which of the following processes is expected to be occurring at the wound?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Epithelial cells migrating to thinly cover the wound

choices.label: B
choices.text: Formation of a mature collagenous fibrotic scar

choices.label: C
choices.text: Macrophages clearing fibrin as the dominant cell type

choices.label: D
choices.text: Myofibroblast contraction of the wound margins inward

choices.label: E
choices.text: Neovascularization of granulation tissue reaching its peak

explanation.summary: At hours 24-48 of first-intention healing, epithelial cells migrate and proliferate along the dermis to thinly cover the wound.
explanation.whyCorrect: In healing by first intention, neutrophils arrive within 24 hours, and during hours 24-48 epithelial cells migrate and proliferate along the dermis to thinly cover the wound. Healing by first intention relies principally on this epithelial regeneration.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A fibrotic scar constitutes the connective tissue at about month 1, not at 36 hours.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Macrophages replace neutrophils as the dominant cell at day 3, not at 36 hours.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Myofibroblast contraction is a feature of large wounds healing by secondary intention over about 6 weeks.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Neovascularization peaks around day 5, when granulation tissue fills the reparative space.

questions.topicName: Wound Healing and Tissue Repair

questions.stem: A sutured surgical incision is healing by first intention. On which of the following days after injury does neovascularization reach its peak while granulation tissue fills the reparative space?

explanation.summary: By day 5 of first-intention healing, granulation tissue fills the reparative space and neovascularization reaches its peak.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the first-intention timeline, day 5 is when granulation tissue fills the reparative space with fibroblast migration and proliferation, subsequent collagen synthesis and deposition, and neovascularization reaching its peak.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Within 24 hours, neutrophils are reaching the incision and migrating toward the clot.
whyWrongByChoice.B: On day 3, macrophages replace neutrophils and provide signals for angiogenesis; vessels are being signaled, not yet at their peak.
whyWrongByChoice.D: By week 2, collagen deposition continues while inflammation, edema, and vascularity diminish in prominence.
whyWrongByChoice.E: By month 1, a fibrotic scar constitutes the connective tissue and the epidermis is essentially normal.

questions.topicName: Wound Healing and Tissue Repair

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man has a large, open traumatic wound of the thigh with extensive tissue loss that is left to heal by secondary intention. Compared with a small incision healing by first intention, this wound carries a greater risk of which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Absence of granulation tissue formation in the wound bed

choices.label: B
choices.text: Conversion of the wound margins into permanently non-regenerative tissue

choices.label: C
choices.text: Failure of neutrophils to be recruited to the wound bed

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inflammation-mediated injury from a robust inflammatory response

choices.label: E
choices.text: Loss of vitamin C-dependent collagen synthesis in the scar

explanation.summary: Extensive wounds healing by secondary intention require a larger fibrin clot and a more robust inflammatory response, which raises the risk of inflammation-mediated injury.
explanation.whyCorrect: If the wound is extensive, a larger fibrin clot is needed, often accompanied by a more robust inflammatory response. This heightened inflammation raises the risk for inflammation-mediated injury to the healing tissue.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Granulation tissue is abundant in secondary intention, filling the large wound and serving as a scaffold for collagen.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Wound size does not change the regenerative classification of the tissue at the margins.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Neutrophils are recruited to both wound types; secondary intention involves more, not fewer, inflammatory cells.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vitamin C-dependent collagen synthesis relates to nutritional status, not to the size of the wound.

questions.topicName: Wound Healing and Tissue Repair

questions.stem: Weeks into the repair of a skin wound, granulation tissue is remodeled through a balance of protein synthesis and degradation until it is replaced by sturdy fibrillar collagen. Which of the following enzymes cleaves collagen fibers and other extracellular matrix components during this remodeling?

explanation.summary: Matrix metalloproteinases cleave collagen fibers and other ECM components as granulation tissue is remodeled into a stable fibrous scar.
explanation.whyCorrect: Granulation tissue is remodeled through a process of protein synthesis and degradation, including the use of matrix metalloproteinases that can cleave collagen fibers and other extracellular matrix components. Eventually the granulation tissue is replaced with sturdy fibrillar collagen until a stable fibrous scar forms.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Complement proteins from platelets help recruit neutrophils and macrophages early in repair; they do not remodel collagen.
whyWrongByChoice.B: HGF is a growth factor that primes hepatocytes to enter the cell cycle; it is not a matrix-degrading enzyme.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Integrins are connector proteins linking the cytoskeleton to the ECM, not proteolytic enzymes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Laminin is a structural component of the basement membrane, not an enzyme.

questions.topicName: Wound Healing and Tissue Repair

questions.stem: A child picks the dried, dark crust off a scraped knee and notices weeping of blood from the delicate tissue beneath. Which of the following terms describes the dried, necrotic surface of the wound that was removed?

explanation.summary: An eschar (scab) is the dried, necrotic surface of a wound; beneath it lies granulation tissue with delicate new vessels that bleed easily.
explanation.whyCorrect: A scab, or eschar, is the dried, necrotic surface of a wound. Pulling it from a skin wound exposes the underlying granulation tissue, whose delicate new vessels weep blood easily.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The basement membrane is a specialized ECM layer beneath epithelium, not a necrotic surface.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A contracture is an exaggerated healing response that limits joint movement.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Granulation tissue is the pink, vascular tissue beneath the crust, not the dried necrotic layer itself.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A keloid is exuberant scar extending beyond the wound borders, not a dried surface crust.

questions.topicName: Wound Healing and Tissue Repair

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man is seen 4 months after an appendectomy. The incision has healed with a raised, firm scar that remains entirely within the borders of the original incision. Histology, if obtained, would show excess collagen and fibroblasts. Which of the following is the most likely natural course of this lesion?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Progressive extension beyond the incision borders

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reopening of the incision along the suture line

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tightening across the joint with loss of mobility

explanation.summary: A hypertrophic scar is raised, stays within the confines of the original wound, and usually regresses over time, unlike a keloid.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hypertrophic scars are raised scars with excess collagen and fibroblasts that remain within the confines of the original wound. In contrast to keloids, hypertrophic scars usually regress over time.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Failure to regress with possible need for surgical excision characterizes keloids; hypertrophic scars regress spontaneously.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Extension beyond the wound boundaries is the defining feature of a keloid, not a hypertrophic scar.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Reopening of a closed incision is dehiscence, a postsurgical complication unrelated to scar maturation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tightening that limits joint movement describes a contracture, typically after severe burns over joints.

questions.topicName: Wound Healing and Tissue Repair

questions.stem: A 68-year-old woman with long-standing varicose veins and congestive heart failure develops a shallow, non-healing ulcer above the medial ankle. Which of the following is the most likely mechanism underlying this chronic wound?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Chronic venous hypertension with poor oxygen delivery

choices.label: D
choices.text: Prolonged compression over a bony prominence

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sensory neuropathy with repetitive unnoticed trauma

explanation.summary: Venous leg ulcers occur in chronic venous hypertension, varicose veins, or congestive heart failure, where decreased blood flow leads to poor oxygen delivery at the ulcer site.
explanation.whyCorrect: Venous leg ulcers occur in patients with chronic venous hypertension, varicose veins, or congestive heart failure, clinical scenarios with decreased blood flow. The lack of perfusion leads to poor oxygen delivery to the site of the chronic ulcer, preventing healing.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Arterial ulcers result from arterial insufficiency such as atherosclerosis; this patient's varicose veins and heart failure point to a venous cause.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Glucocorticoids impair healing by dampening TGF-beta and fibrosis but do not cause venous leg ulcers.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Prolonged compression produces pressure sores in bed-bound, immobile patients.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Neuropathy contributes to diabetic ulcers of the feet, not to a venous ulcer in a patient with varicose veins.

questions.topicName: Wound Healing and Tissue Repair

questions.stem: A 72-year-old man with a long smoking history and known atherosclerosis develops a painful, punched-out ulcer on the lateral lower leg that fails to heal. Which of the following categories of chronic wound best describes this lesion?

explanation.summary: Arterial ulcers result from inadequate perfusion due to arterial insufficiency, such as from atherosclerosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Arterial ulcers are chronic wounds that result from arterial insufficiency, such as from atherosclerosis, which deprives the tissue of the perfusion needed for repair. Tobacco smoke further impairs healing through decreased oxygen levels and vascular constriction.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Diabetic ulcers, typically of the feet and lower extremities, stem from diabetes-related poor blood flow, neuropathy, and infection risk; no diabetes is described here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A keloid is an exuberant scar extending beyond the wound, not a non-healing ulcer.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pressure sores result from prolonged compression in bed-bound patients with limited mobility.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Venous leg ulcers arise with chronic venous hypertension, varicose veins, or congestive heart failure rather than atherosclerotic arterial disease.

questions.topicName: Wound Healing and Tissue Repair

questions.stem: A 60-year-old woman on long-term high-dose prednisone for an autoimmune disease undergoes abdominal surgery. Her surgeon notes that her incision is forming noticeably less scar tissue than expected. Which of the following best explains the diminished fibrosis?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Impaired hydroxylation of collagen from ascorbic acid deficiency

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased recruitment of myofibroblasts to the incision

choices.label: D
choices.text: Loss of basement membrane type IV collagen scaffold

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reduced production of TGF-beta by inflammatory cells

explanation.summary: Glucocorticoids are anti-inflammatory and reduce key immune signals; inhibition of TGF-beta production diminishes fibrosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Glucocorticoids (steroids) are anti-inflammatory, reducing the influences of key immune responses on repair. In particular, inhibition of TGF-beta production can diminish fibrosis, because TGF-beta is the growth factor that attracts fibroblasts and stimulates collagen and ECM synthesis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Glucocorticoids suppress, rather than enhance, inflammatory cell recruitment and activation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ascorbic acid (vitamin C) deficiency impairs collagen synthesis in scurvy, but this patient's problem is steroid-related, not nutritional.
whyWrongByChoice.C: More myofibroblasts would increase contraction and scarring, not reduce fibrosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Loss of the ECM scaffold promotes scarring rather than reducing it, and it is not an effect of glucocorticoids.

questions.topicName: Wound Healing and Tissue Repair

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man who smokes two packs of cigarettes per day has delayed healing of a leg wound. Through which of the following mechanisms does tobacco smoke most directly impair his wound healing?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decreased oxygen levels and vascular constriction

choices.label: B
choices.text: Deficiency of ascorbic acid for collagen synthesis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Prolonged inflammation from reactive oxygen species

explanation.summary: Tobacco smoke negatively impacts wound healing through decreased oxygen levels and vascular constriction.
explanation.whyCorrect: Tobacco smoking is one of the factors that negatively influences tissue repair; it impairs healing through decreased oxygen levels and vascular constriction, reducing the perfusion and oxygen delivery that repair requires.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Ascorbic acid deficiency causes scurvy with impaired collagen synthesis; it is a nutritional factor, not the effect of smoking.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Neuropathy is one of the reasons diabetes mellitus impairs healing, not a direct effect of tobacco smoke.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Prolonged inflammation with reactive oxygen species generation is the mechanism by which infections impair healing.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Suppression of TGF-beta production is the mechanism of glucocorticoids diminishing fibrosis.

questions.topicName: Wound Healing and Tissue Repair

questions.stem: A 44-year-old man who works in a wood-preservation and pesticide facility presents with several weeks of abdominal cramping, diarrhea, and tingling and numbness in his hands and feet. On examination his breath has a garlic-like odor, and transverse white bands are noted across several fingernails. Which of the following toxins is most likely responsible for his presentation?

explanation.summary: Arsenic exposure classically causes garlic-odor breath, gastrointestinal symptoms, transverse white nail bands (Mees' lines), and sensorimotor neuropathy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Inorganic arsenic is found in soil and water and is used in herbicides, pesticides, and wood treatment and preservation. It inhibits sulfhydryl-containing enzymes and interferes with the electron transport chain. Clinical clues include garlicky breath, gastrointestinal symptoms, a transverse white band across the nail bed, and neurologic effects such as paresthesias that can appear weeks after exposure.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Carbon monoxide is a non-irritating, odorless gas that binds hemoglobin and causes hypoxia, not nail banding or garlic odor.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Lead poisoning produces microcytic anemia with basophilic stippling, wrist drop, and a blue gingival line rather than garlic breath and Mees' lines.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mercury exposure comes largely from contaminated fish and dental amalgam vapors and causes neuromotor and cognitive dysfunction, not garlicky breath.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Radon is a radioactive gas whose main consequence is lung cancer, not an acute garlic-breath and neuropathy syndrome.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 1 of 2: Chemicals and Substances

questions.stem: A 39-year-old painter who has spent several months renovating a house built in the 1950s presents with fatigue, abdominal pain, and difficulty extending both wrists. A peripheral blood smear shows a microcytic anemia with coarse basophilic stippling of red blood cells. Which of the following best explains the anemia in this patient?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Autoimmune destruction of red cell membranes

explanation.summary: Lead interferes with enzymes of heme synthesis, producing a microcytic anemia with basophilic stippling.
explanation.whyCorrect: Lead has high affinity for sulfhydryl groups and interferes with enzymes involved in heme synthesis, impairing hemoglobin production. The resulting microcytic anemia is accompanied by basophilic stippling, which represents aggregates of ribosomes and ribosomal RNA that precipitate because of the impairment. The wrist drop reflects lead-induced peripheral neuropathy in adults.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Alpha-particle DNA damage is a feature of radon exposure and is linked to lung cancer, not this anemia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: There is no autoimmune hemolysis here; the findings and old-paint exposure point to lead toxicity.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Carboxyhemoglobin formation is the mechanism of carbon monoxide toxicity and causes hypoxia, not a microcytic anemia with stippling.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Thiamine deficiency in alcoholism causes Wernicke encephalopathy, not microcytic anemia with basophilic stippling.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 1 of 2: Chemicals and Substances

questions.stem: A 2-year-old child living in an old home with peeling paint is brought in for irritability, developmental regression, and vomiting. Imaging demonstrates cerebral edema, and the child is diagnosed with lead encephalopathy. Compared with adults, why are pediatric patients particularly prone to central nervous system injury from lead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Their blood-brain barrier is more permeable

choices.label: B
choices.text: They eliminate lead more slowly through Phase II conjugation

choices.label: C
choices.text: They express more superoxide dismutase in neurons

choices.label: D
choices.text: They have higher hepatic cytochrome P-450 activity

choices.label: E
choices.text: They have increased carboxyhemoglobin binding capacity

explanation.summary: The pediatric blood-brain barrier is more permeable, facilitating lead entry into the CNS and increasing neurotoxicity.
explanation.whyCorrect: In addition to greater absorption of ingested lead, the blood-brain barrier is more permeable in pediatric patients, facilitating lead toxicity in the central nervous system. Lead poisoning in children can cause cerebral edema, demyelination of white matter, and necrosis, leading to learning disabilities and delayed psychomotor development; high doses can cause blindness, seizures, coma, and death.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Slower conjugation is not the described mechanism; the key factor is barrier permeability and increased absorption.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Superoxide dismutase handles reactive oxygen species and is not the reason children are more vulnerable to lead.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Higher P-450 activity would relate to xenobiotic metabolism, not to the enhanced CNS susceptibility that comes from a permeable barrier.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Carboxyhemoglobin binding pertains to carbon monoxide, not lead neurotoxicity.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 1 of 2: Chemicals and Substances

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man is found unconscious in his car inside a closed garage with the engine running. He is unresponsive, and examination reveals a cherry-red discoloration of his skin and mucous membranes. Which of the following best explains the tissue hypoxia in this patient?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Alpha particles generate free radicals in erythrocytes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Carbon monoxide binds hemoglobin and blocks oxygen transport

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reactive oxygen species peroxidize cell membranes

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sulfhydryl enzyme inhibition halts the electron transport chain

explanation.summary: Carbon monoxide has roughly 200-fold greater affinity for hemoglobin than oxygen, forming carboxyhemoglobin and preventing oxygen transport.
explanation.whyCorrect: Carbon monoxide is a non-irritating, colorless, odorless gas produced by incomplete oxidation of hydrocarbons. Hemoglobin has about a 200-fold greater affinity for CO than for oxygen, and CO binding forms carboxyhemoglobin, a stable form that prevents the binding and transport of oxygen. Acute exposure in an enclosed running car can cause coma within minutes, and cherry-red discoloration may be seen.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Alpha-particle free radical generation describes radon toxicity, not carbon monoxide poisoning.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Nicotine vasoconstriction impairs wound healing but does not produce carboxyhemoglobin or cherry-red skin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Membrane lipid peroxidation from ROS is a feature of alcohol and radiation injury, not the CO mechanism.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sulfhydryl enzyme inhibition of the electron transport chain describes arsenic, not carbon monoxide.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 1 of 2: Chemicals and Substances

questions.stem: A 58-year-old lifelong nonsmoker is diagnosed with lung cancer. His home was found to have elevated levels of a radioactive gas derived from uranium in the soil. Which of the following best describes how this exposure damaged his respiratory epithelium?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Alpha particles emitted during decay generate free radicals

choices.label: B
choices.text: It forms DNA adducts after activation by cytochrome P-450

choices.label: C
choices.text: It inhibits sulfhydryl-containing enzymes in the airway

choices.label: D
choices.text: Macrophages ingest the gas and release inflammatory mediators

choices.label: E
choices.text: The gas binds hemoglobin and starves cells of oxygen

explanation.summary: Radon decays into polonium and emits alpha particles that generate free radicals and reactive oxygen species, damaging DNA.
explanation.whyCorrect: Radon is a radioactive gas derived from uranium and is the number one cause of lung cancer among nonsmokers. It decays into polonium 214 and polonium 218, which cause ionizing radiation damage through the emission of alpha particles. Alpha particles release electrons that damage DNA, cells, and tissues through the generation of free radicals and reactive oxygen species.

whyWrongByChoice.B: P-450-activated DNA adduct formation describes tobacco smoke carcinogens rather than radon's ionizing radiation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sulfhydryl enzyme inhibition characterizes heavy metals such as arsenic, mercury, and lead.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Macrophage ingestion with inflammatory mediator release describes particulate matter, not a radioactive gas.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Hemoglobin binding and oxygen starvation describe carbon monoxide, not radon.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 1 of 2: Chemicals and Substances

questions.stem: A 62-year-old man who worked in coal mining for decades dies of unrelated causes. At autopsy, his lungs and hilar lymph nodes show accumulation of black carbon-containing pigment. Which of the following terms best describes this finding?

explanation.summary: Anthracosis is the accumulation of carbon-containing black pigment in the lungs and lymph nodes after exposure to exhaust, tobacco smoke, and coal mining.
explanation.whyCorrect: Particulate matter, or soot, is produced by coal- and oil-fired plants, fossil fuel burning, and diesel exhaust. Ultrafine particulate matter is ingested by macrophages, and its accumulation as black carbon pigment in the lungs and lymph nodes following exposure to exhaust, tobacco smoke, and coal mining is termed anthracosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Angiosarcoma is a vascular liver tumor linked to vinyl chloride, unrelated to lung pigment.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Emphysema is irreversible enlargement of airspaces from tissue destruction, not pigment deposition.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mesothelioma is a malignant tumor associated with asbestos exposure, not benign carbon pigment accumulation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Silicosis is lung scarring caused by silica dust, not carbon-pigment accumulation.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 1 of 2: Chemicals and Substances

questions.stem: During Phase I metabolism of xenobiotics, cytochrome P-450 enzymes can generate superoxide, a reactive oxygen species. Which of the following enzymes is directly responsible for converting superoxide to hydrogen peroxide?

explanation.summary: Superoxide dismutase converts superoxide, a reactive oxygen species, to hydrogen peroxide.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick specifies that superoxide dismutase is responsible for converting superoxide to hydrogen peroxide. Both catalase and glutathione peroxidase are then capable of further processing hydrogen peroxide to water, a key step in detoxifying the reactive oxygen species that arise during xenobiotic metabolism.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Alcohol dehydrogenase metabolizes ethanol and has no role in superoxide detoxification.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Catalase acts downstream, converting hydrogen peroxide to water, not superoxide to hydrogen peroxide.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cytochrome P-450 is a Phase I enzyme that can generate reactive oxygen species, not detoxify superoxide.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Glutathione peroxidase also processes hydrogen peroxide to water rather than converting superoxide.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 1 of 2: Chemicals and Substances

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man who spent 20 years working in a plant that synthesizes plastic resins develops a malignant liver tumor of vascular endothelial origin. Exposure to which of the following agents is most strongly associated with this tumor?

explanation.summary: Vinyl chloride, used to make polyvinyl chloride, is associated with hepatic angiosarcoma, a malignant tumor of vascular origin.
explanation.whyCorrect: Vinyl chloride is a chemical used in the synthesis of polyvinyl chloride resins used in packaging and building products. It is associated with angiosarcoma of the liver, a malignant tumor of vascular origin, which fits this worker's endothelial-origin hepatic malignancy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Asbestos is associated with mesothelioma and lung cancer, not hepatic angiosarcoma.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Carbon tetrachloride is a solvent causing acute CNS depression rather than hepatic angiosarcoma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Silica causes silicosis and is associated with lung disease and cancer, not liver angiosarcoma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Prolonged wood dust exposure is linked to nasal cancers, not a vascular liver tumor.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 1 of 2: Chemicals and Substances

questions.stem: A 50-year-old woman who smokes one pack of cigarettes daily is scheduled for an elective procedure. Her surgeon strongly recommends smoking cessation beforehand, explaining that one component of tobacco smoke exerts vasoconstrictive effects that could compromise blood flow to the healing wound. Which component is he referring to?

explanation.summary: Nicotine exerts vasoconstrictive effects that reduce blood flow and impair wound healing.
explanation.whyCorrect: Impaired wound healing in smokers is attributed to decreased oxygen availability and the vasoconstrictive effects of nicotine, which limits blood flow to a healing wound. This is why smoking cessation is advised before elective surgery.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Carbon monoxide reduces oxygen availability through carboxyhemoglobin but is not the vasoconstrictive component.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Nitrosamines are carcinogens implicated in cancer development, not vasoconstriction.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Polycyclic hydrocarbons are carcinogens implicated in cancer, not the vasoconstrictive agent.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Radon is an environmental radioactive gas and is not a component of tobacco smoke affecting wound perfusion.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 1 of 2: Chemicals and Substances

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man with a 40-year history of heavy cigarette smoking has chronic cough, phlegm, and progressive dyspnea. Autopsy of a similar patient shows irreversible enlargement of the airspaces due to destruction of lung parenchyma. Which of the following pathologic changes is most associated with tobacco use?

explanation.summary: Tobacco smoke destroys lung parenchyma, producing emphysema, the irreversible enlargement of airspaces.
explanation.whyCorrect: Emphysema is the irreversible enlargement of airspaces resulting from tissue destruction and is a component of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, which also includes chronic bronchitis. Tissue destruction by tobacco is driven by oxidative stress and pro-inflammatory effects, making emphysema the pathologic change most associated with smoking.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cherry-red discoloration of skin is characteristic of carbon monoxide poisoning, and would be unlikely in nonacute settings.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Gingival pigmentation (a blue gingival line) is seen in lead poisoning, not tobacco use.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hemorrhagic mammillary bodies occur in Wernicke encephalopathy from thiamine deficiency in alcoholism.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Macrosteatotic hepatocytes (fatty liver) are seen in alcohol use, not tobacco use.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 1 of 2: Chemicals and Substances

questions.stem: A 47-year-old man with chronic heavy alcohol use is found to have an enlarged, fatty liver on imaging, with hepatocytes distended by lipid. Which of the following metabolic changes from alcohol dehydrogenase activity best explains the accumulation of fat in his liver?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Deficiency of thiamine impairing the citric acid cycle

choices.label: B
choices.text: Depletion of hepatic cytochrome P-450 enzymes

choices.label: C
choices.text: Formation of DNA adducts by acetaldehyde

explanation.summary: Alcohol dehydrogenase consumes NAD and raises NADH, and the reduced NAD availability shifts metabolism toward fat accumulation in the liver.
explanation.whyCorrect: Processing of alcohol by alcohol dehydrogenase reduces the availability of NAD while increasing NADH. Because NAD is needed for fatty acid oxidation and for converting lactate to pyruvate, this shift leads to accumulation of fat in the liver as well as lactic acidosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Thiamine deficiency causes Wernicke encephalopathy, not hepatic steatosis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The MEOS pathway involves CYP2E1; alcohol does not simply deplete P-450 to cause steatosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Acetaldehyde-DNA adducts are linked to laryngeal and esophageal cancer, not the fatty liver mechanism.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vasoconstriction reducing blood flow is a nicotine effect on wound healing, not the cause of fatty liver.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 1 of 2: Chemicals and Substances

questions.stem: A newborn whose mother drank alcohol during pregnancy is noted to have a thin upper lip, a smooth philtrum, and short palpebral fissures, along with microcephaly and growth restriction. Which of the following mechanisms is most likely responsible for this clinical phenotype?

explanation.summary: Fetal alcohol spectrum disorder results from apoptosis of developing fetal cells triggered by reactive oxygen species during acetaldehyde metabolism.
explanation.whyCorrect: A proposed mechanism for the teratogenic effects of alcohol is damage from reactive oxygen species produced during the metabolism of acetaldehyde to acetic acid, which in turn induces apoptosis, or programmed cell death, in developing fetal cells. This underlies the facial phenotype of a thin upper lip, smooth philtrum, and short palpebral fissures with microcephaly and growth restriction.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Fetal alcohol spectrum disorder is an acquired teratogenic exposure, not an inherited single-gene disorder.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The mechanism is programmed cell death (apoptosis), not uncontrolled coagulative necrosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Calcium metabolism dysregulation is seen in pediatric lead poisoning, not fetal alcohol effects.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Carboxyhemoglobin hypoxia relates to carbon monoxide, not the teratogenic mechanism of alcohol.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 1 of 2: Chemicals and Substances

questions.stem: A pharmacology student is reviewing how the liver prepares an ingested xenobiotic for elimination. The compound first undergoes a reaction that yields a primary metabolite before any conjugation step takes place. Which of the following is an example of this first-step (Phase I) reaction?

explanation.summary: Phase I reactions are hydrolysis, oxidation, and reduction reactions that produce a primary metabolite.
explanation.whyCorrect: The body prepares xenobiotics for removal through Phase I and Phase II reactions. Phase I reactions include hydrolysis, oxidation, or reduction and produce a primary metabolite; the key enzyme group is the heme-containing cytochrome P-450 family located predominantly in hepatocytes. Phase II reactions then further metabolize that primary metabolite for elimination.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Conjugation is a Phase II reaction performed after the Phase I metabolite has been formed.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Glucuronidation is a Phase II reaction that acts on the primary metabolite to promote elimination.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Methylation is listed among the Phase II reactions that further metabolize the primary metabolite.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sulfation is a Phase II reaction, not a first-step reaction that generates the primary metabolite.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 1 of 2: Chemicals and Substances

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman ingests a lipid-soluble xenobiotic. After Phase I processing by cytochrome P-450 enzymes in her hepatocytes, the primary metabolite undergoes glucuronidation. Which of the following is the principal purpose of this second reaction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Convert superoxide to hydrogen peroxide within the hepatocyte

choices.label: B
choices.text: Generate a reactive metabolite that damages cellular DNA

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increase water solubility for elimination in urine, bile, or feces

choices.label: D
choices.text: Produce a primary metabolite through oxidation or reduction

choices.label: E
choices.text: Store the compound in adipose tissue for gradual release

explanation.summary: Phase II reactions such as glucuronidation make xenobiotic metabolites water soluble so they can be eliminated in urine, bile, or feces.
explanation.whyCorrect: Phase II reactions further metabolize the primary metabolite for elimination from the body, often with the purpose of making the substance water soluble. These reactions include glucuronidation, sulfation, methylation, and conjugation, and the xenobiotic is ideally eliminated by urine, bile, or feces.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Conversion of superoxide to hydrogen peroxide is the job of superoxide dismutase, not of glucuronidation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Reactive metabolites arise mainly from Phase I cytochrome P-450 activity, not as the goal of Phase II conjugation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Producing a primary metabolite by hydrolysis, oxidation, or reduction describes Phase I, not Phase II.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Phase II reactions promote elimination; accumulation in tissues is what happens when a xenobiotic is not eliminated.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 1 of 2: Chemicals and Substances

questions.stem: A 9-year-old boy with asthma lives beside a highway with heavy diesel truck traffic and near a coal-fired power plant. Over the past year he has had more frequent asthma attacks and two respiratory infections. Which of the following best describes the initial cellular event by which the responsible pollutant injures his airways?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Binding of hemoglobin with formation of a stable complex

choices.label: B
choices.text: Emission of alpha particles that release electrons

choices.label: C
choices.text: Formation of DNA adducts after cytochrome P-450 activation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ingestion by macrophages with release of inflammatory mediators

choices.label: E
choices.text: Inhibition of sulfhydryl-containing enzymes in bronchial epithelium

explanation.summary: Ultrafine particulate matter is ingested by macrophages, which release inflammatory mediators that irritate and inflame respiratory tissue.
explanation.whyCorrect: Particulate matter, or soot, is produced by coal- and oil-fired power plants, the burning of fossil fuels, and diesel exhaust. Ultrafine particulate matter is ingested by macrophages and releases inflammatory mediators, producing local damage, irritation, and pro-inflammatory actions. Particulate exposure is associated with increased respiratory infections in children, decreased lung function in patients with chronic lung or heart disease, and increased asthmatic attacks and mortality in patients with asthma.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hemoglobin binding describes carbon monoxide, which causes hypoxia rather than airway inflammation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Alpha-particle emission describes radon decay products, which cause ionizing radiation damage and lung cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cytochrome P-450-activated DNA adducts describe tobacco smoke carcinogens, not particulate matter.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sulfhydryl enzyme inhibition is the mechanism of heavy metals such as lead, mercury, and arsenic.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 1 of 2: Chemicals and Substances

questions.stem: A family of four presents in midwinter with several months of recurrent headaches, fatigue, and difficulty concentrating that improve whenever they are away from home. Their gas furnace is found to be malfunctioning. Skin and mucous membranes appear normal in color. Which of the following best characterizes the pathophysiology of their illness?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Inhibition of sulfhydryl-containing enzymes producing garlicky breath

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ionizing radiation injury to the respiratory epithelium

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lipid peroxidation of hepatocyte membranes by reactive oxygen species

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rapid onset of coma from carboxyhemoglobin formed within minutes

choices.label: E
choices.text: Slowly progressive hypoxia producing ischemic damage and neurologic sequelae

explanation.summary: Chronic carbon monoxide poisoning causes a slow progression of hypoxia over time, leading to ischemic damage and possible long-term neurologic sequelae.
explanation.whyCorrect: Carbon monoxide results from the incomplete oxidation of hydrocarbons, including the burning of carbon fuels in furnaces. Chronic poisoning by CO causes a slow progression of hypoxia over time, leading to ischemic damage and possible long-term neurologic sequelae. Cherry-red discoloration is seen with high carboxyhemoglobin levels in acute, often fatal cases and is more pertinent to death investigation than a reliable feature for ongoing patient care in chronic poisoning, so its absence does not exclude the diagnosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Sulfhydryl enzyme inhibition with garlicky breath describes arsenic poisoning, not a combustion-gas exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ionizing radiation injury describes radon, whose consequence is lung cancer rather than headaches and fatigue from a furnace.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Lipid peroxidation of hepatocyte membranes is a feature of alcohol metabolism through the MEOS pathway.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Coma within minutes describes acute high-level exposure, such as a running car in an enclosed garage, not months of low-level symptoms.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 1 of 2: Chemicals and Substances

questions.stem: A home inspector detects elevated levels of a radioactive gas seeping from the soil into a basement. The homeowner asks how a gas can damage lung tissue. The alpha particles responsible for the DNA damage are emitted primarily during the decay of which of the following?

explanation.summary: Radon decays into polonium 214 and polonium 218, which cause ionizing radiation damage through emission of alpha particles.
explanation.whyCorrect: Radon is a radioactive gas derived from uranium and is widely present in soil and sometimes in homes. It decays into polonium 214 and polonium 218, which cause ionizing radiation damage through the emission of alpha particles. These high-energy particles release electrons that damage DNA, cells, and tissues through free radicals and reactive oxygen species, explaining why radon is the leading cause of lung cancer among nonsmokers.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Arsenic is a toxic metal that inhibits sulfhydryl enzymes; it is not part of the radon decay chain described.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Beryllium is an inhaled mineral dust that causes pneumoconiosis, not a radioactive decay product.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Lead is a toxic metal deposited in bone, teeth, and gums; it is not the alpha-emitting product of radon decay.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Uranium is the source from which radon is derived, but the alpha-emitting decay products in the lung are polonium isotopes.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 1 of 2: Chemicals and Substances

questions.stem: A 3-year-old girl who lives in a home built in 1940 is evaluated for irritability and abdominal pain. A radiograph of the wrist shows bands of increased radiodensity at the ends of the radius and ulna. Which of the following best explains this radiographic finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Deposition of carbon-containing pigment in the bone marrow

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hemorrhage and necrosis within the growth plates

choices.label: C
choices.text: Impaired remodeling of calcified cartilage in the epiphyses

choices.label: D
choices.text: Osteolytic destruction by a tumor of vascular origin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Precipitation of ribosomal RNA aggregates within bone

explanation.summary: Lead interferes with calcium metabolism, deposits in bones and teeth, and impairs normal remodeling of calcified cartilage in the epiphyses of children, producing increased radiodensity.
explanation.whyCorrect: Lead interferes with calcium metabolism and deposits in bones and teeth, particularly in pediatric patients who demonstrate increased lead absorption compared with adults. Lead interferes with normal remodeling of calcified cartilage in the epiphyses of children, and the resulting increased radiodensity is visible on radiographs of pediatric patients with lead poisoning.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Carbon-containing black pigment accumulates in the lungs and lymph nodes (anthracosis), not in bone.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hemorrhage and necrosis describe the mammillary bodies in Wernicke encephalopathy, not epiphyseal lead deposition.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A malignant vascular tumor (angiosarcoma) is associated with vinyl chloride and arises in the liver, not the wrist.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Precipitated ribosomal RNA aggregates describe basophilic stippling in red blood cells, not a bone finding.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 1 of 2: Chemicals and Substances

questions.stem: A 46-year-old man who has worked for 20 years at a petroleum refinery presents with fatigue and colicky abdominal pain. Oral examination reveals a dark blue line along the gingival margin. Deposition of which of the following is responsible for this finding?

explanation.summary: A blue gingival line in lead poisoning results from deposition of lead sulfide.
explanation.whyCorrect: A blue gingival line, or gingival pigmentation, has been reported in lead poisoning due to the deposition of lead sulfide, and has been documented in patients who worked in a petroleum refinery. Lead poisoning is also responsible for gastrointestinal damage with severe abdominal pain and for kidney damage that can progress to renal failure.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Anthracotic (carbon) pigment accumulates in the lungs and lymph nodes, not along the gingiva.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Carboxyhemoglobin is the stable complex formed when carbon monoxide binds hemoglobin; it produces cherry-red discoloration, not a gum line.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Methyl mercury is lipid soluble and accumulates in the brain, producing neuromotor and cognitive dysfunction rather than gingival pigmentation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Polycyclic hydrocarbons are carcinogens implicated in lung and bladder cancer and do not deposit in the gums.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 1 of 2: Chemicals and Substances

questions.stem: A 52-year-old woman who eats large quantities of fish caught from a contaminated bay develops tremor, memory difficulties, and irritability over several months. Laboratory evaluation also shows renal impairment. Which of the following properties of the responsible toxin best explains its neurologic effects?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It emits alpha particles as it undergoes radioactive decay

choices.label: B
choices.text: It has a 200-fold greater affinity for hemoglobin than oxygen

choices.label: C
choices.text: It interferes with enzymes involved in heme synthesis

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is activated by cytochrome P-450 into DNA-damaging intermediates

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is lipid soluble and accumulates in the brain

explanation.summary: Methyl mercury is lipid soluble and accumulates in the brain, causing neuromotor, cognitive, and behavioral dysfunction.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mercury exposure may occur from eating contaminated fish or from mercury vapors released from certain dental amalgams. Mercury has a high affinity for sulfhydryl groups, inhibiting enzymes and altering proteins. One form, methyl mercury, is lipid soluble and accumulates in the brain, resulting in neuromotor, cognitive, and behavioral dysfunction. Mercury also damages the kidney and gastrointestinal system, accounting for her renal impairment.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Alpha-particle emission describes radon decay products, which cause lung cancer rather than tremor and cognitive change.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A 200-fold affinity for hemoglobin describes carbon monoxide, which is not acquired from contaminated fish.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Interference with heme synthesis describes lead and produces microcytic anemia with basophilic stippling.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cytochrome P-450 activation into DNA-damaging intermediates describes tobacco carcinogens, not mercury.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 1 of 2: Chemicals and Substances

questions.stem: A 41-year-old farmer recovers from an acute illness with vomiting and diarrhea that developed after he drank from a well later found to be contaminated with arsenic from agricultural runoff. Six weeks later he returns with tingling, numbness, and burning pain in both feet. Which of the following best explains his new symptoms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Accumulation of lipid-soluble organochlorines in nervous tissue

choices.label: B
choices.text: Arsenic sensorimotor neuropathy appearing weeks after the exposure

choices.label: C
choices.text: Demyelination of cerebral white matter from lead ingestion

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ischemic neurologic sequelae of chronic carbon monoxide exposure

choices.label: E
choices.text: Thiamine deficiency damaging the mammillary bodies and thalamus

explanation.summary: The neurologic effects of arsenic, including sensorimotor neuropathies with paresthesias, numbness, and pain, can manifest many weeks after exposure.
explanation.whyCorrect: Arsenic is tasteless and odorless, is absorbed by the gastrointestinal system, and is naturally found in soil and water as well as certain herbicides, pesticides, and agricultural products. Clinical presentations include gastrointestinal symptoms, and neurologic effects, including sensorimotor neuropathies with paresthesias (tingling sensations), numbness, and pain, can manifest many weeks after exposure. Heart arrhythmias may also occur.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Organochlorines are pesticides that damage nervous tissue, but his exposure was arsenic-contaminated water with a preceding gastrointestinal illness.
whyWrongByChoice.C: White matter demyelination is a central nervous system effect of lead in children; this adult had a documented arsenic exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Chronic carbon monoxide sequelae follow prolonged hypoxia from a combustion source, not a contaminated well.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Thiamine deficiency causes Wernicke encephalopathy with altered mental status, ophthalmoplegia, and ataxia, not a delayed distal neuropathy after arsenic ingestion.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 1 of 2: Chemicals and Substances

questions.stem: A 29-year-old man spends an afternoon stripping paint from cabinets in a small, unventilated bathroom using a commercial paint remover. He becomes dizzy and confused and is found by his roommate slumped on the floor. Which of the following agents is most likely responsible?

explanation.summary: Organic solvents such as chloroform and carbon tetrachloride, found in cleaning agents and paint removers, cause dizziness, confusion, and even coma at high levels.
explanation.whyCorrect: Occupational health risks in industry include solvents and chemicals. Organic solvents, such as chloroform and carbon tetrachloride, cause dizziness, confusion, and even coma at high levels, and these substances may be encountered in cleaning agents and paint removers. An unventilated space with a paint remover fits this acute central nervous system presentation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Beryllium is an inhaled mineral dust that damages the respiratory system as a pneumoconiosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Organochlorines are lipid-soluble pesticides that damage nervous tissue; they are not the active agents in paint removers.
