whyWrongByChoice.D: Polycyclic hydrocarbons are combustion products of coal and gas encountered in steel factories, tar, soot, and tobacco smoke, and are carcinogens rather than acute CNS depressants.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vinyl chloride is used in polyvinyl chloride synthesis and is associated with hepatic angiosarcoma, not acute dizziness from paint stripping.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 1 of 2: Chemicals and Substances

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man who spent 30 years working as a sandblaster develops progressive dyspnea. Examination of the lungs of a similar patient at autopsy shows discoloration and scarring of the upper lobes from inhaled silica. Non-neoplastic lung diseases caused by inhalation of mineral dusts are grouped under which of the following terms?

explanation.summary: Inhalation of mineral dusts causes non-neoplastic lung diseases grouped under the term pneumoconiosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Inhalation of mineral dusts causes non-neoplastic lung diseases, grouped under the term pneumoconiosis. Coal dust, silica, asbestos, and beryllium are all damaging to the respiratory system, and silicosis produces discoloration and scarring of the lung. Asbestos and silica are furthermore associated with cancer.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Angiosarcoma is a malignant vascular tumor of the liver associated with vinyl chloride, not a dust-induced lung disease.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Chronic bronchitis is airway inflammation causing chronic cough and phlegm, a component of COPD attributable to tobacco.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Emphysema is irreversible enlargement of airspaces from tissue damage, associated with tobacco smoke rather than mineral dust.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mesothelioma is a neoplasm associated with asbestos, whereas pneumoconiosis refers to the non-neoplastic dust diseases.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 1 of 2: Chemicals and Substances

questions.stem: A 67-year-old retired shipyard insulation worker presents with chest pain and a pleural effusion. Biopsy establishes a diagnosis of mesothelioma. Exposure to which of the following is most strongly associated with this tumor?

explanation.summary: Asbestos is an important cause of mesothelioma.
explanation.whyCorrect: Among the mineral dusts that cause pneumoconiosis, asbestos and silica are furthermore associated with cancer, and asbestos specifically is an important cause of mesothelioma. Insulation work in shipyards is a classic setting for asbestos exposure.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Beryllium is a mineral dust that damages the respiratory system but is not the exposure linked to mesothelioma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Coal dust causes non-neoplastic pneumoconiosis and anthracosis, not mesothelioma.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Organochlorines are lipid-soluble pesticides that damage nervous tissue and are not linked to mesothelioma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Prolonged wood dust exposure is associated with nasal cancers rather than pleural tumors.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 1 of 2: Chemicals and Substances

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man who has worked in a steel factory for 30 years presents with painless hematuria and is diagnosed with bladder cancer. He has never smoked. Exposure to which of the following at his workplace most likely contributed to this cancer?

explanation.summary: Polycyclic hydrocarbons, combustion products of coal and gas encountered in steel factories, are carcinogenic and implicated in lung and bladder cancer.
explanation.whyCorrect: Polycyclic hydrocarbons are combustion products of coal and gas and may be encountered in steel factories or through exposure to tar, soot, or tobacco smoke. They are carcinogenic and are implicated in lung and bladder cancer, making them the most likely occupational contributor in a nonsmoking steel worker with bladder cancer.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Asbestos is associated with mesothelioma and other lung disease, not bladder cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Carbon tetrachloride is an organic solvent that causes dizziness, confusion, and coma rather than bladder cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Vinyl chloride is used in polyvinyl chloride synthesis and is associated with angiosarcoma of the liver, not bladder cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Prolonged wood dust exposure is associated with nasal cancers, not bladder cancer.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 1 of 2: Chemicals and Substances

questions.stem: A 36-year-old agricultural worker develops paresthesias, tremors, confusion, and malaise after several weeks of applying an organochlorine pesticide without protective equipment. Which of the following properties of organochlorines best accounts for their effect on nervous tissue?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Interference with the electron transport chain

explanation.summary: Organochlorines are highly lipid-soluble pesticides that damage nervous tissue, producing paresthesia, tremors, confusion, and malaise.
explanation.whyCorrect: Organochlorines are used in certain pesticides, are highly lipid soluble, and can damage nervous tissue, including paresthesia, tremors, confusion, and malaise. Their central nervous system effects are attributed to this lipid solubility.

whyWrongByChoice.A: High affinity for sulfhydryl groups is the mechanism of the toxic metals lead, mercury, and arsenic, not organochlorines.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Interference with the electron transport chain describes inorganic arsenate.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Alpha-particle emission describes radon decay products, which cause lung cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vasoconstriction is the effect of nicotine that impairs wound healing, not a property of organochlorines.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 1 of 2: Chemicals and Substances

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man with a 35-pack-year smoking history develops lung cancer. His physician explains that cytochrome P-450 enzymes act on the polycyclic hydrocarbons and nitrosamines in tobacco smoke to increase their water solubility for elimination through the urinary system. Which of the following best explains why this detoxification process nonetheless contributes to carcinogenesis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Conjugated products are retained in macrophages as black pigment

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cytochrome P-450 depletes NAD, shifting metabolism toward fat accumulation

choices.label: C
choices.text: The enzymes deposit the carcinogens in bone and teeth

choices.label: D
choices.text: The reaction intermediates damage DNA, introducing oncogenic mutations

choices.label: E
choices.text: The water-soluble products bind hemoglobin and cause tissue hypoxia

explanation.summary: Although cytochrome P-450 enzymes increase the water solubility of tobacco carcinogens for elimination, the intermediates damage DNA and introduce potentially oncogenic mutations.
explanation.whyCorrect: Carcinogens contained in tobacco smoke, such as polycyclic hydrocarbons and nitrosamines, are substances capable of inducing neoplastic transformation. Cytochrome P-450 enzymes increase the water solubility of these carcinogens for elimination through the urinary system; however, the intermediates damage DNA, introducing potentially oncogenic (cancer-causing) mutations. Tobacco smoke contains at least 60 known carcinogens, and the relative risk for lung cancer increases with the number of cigarettes smoked per day.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Retention of black pigment in macrophages describes anthracosis from particulate matter, not DNA-damaging carcinogen intermediates.
whyWrongByChoice.B: NAD depletion with fat accumulation describes alcohol metabolism by alcohol dehydrogenase, not tobacco carcinogen activation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Deposition in bone and teeth describes lead, which interferes with calcium metabolism.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Hemoglobin binding and hypoxia describe carbon monoxide in smoke, not the mechanism by which activated carcinogens cause cancer.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 1 of 2: Chemicals and Substances

questions.stem: A 44-year-old baseball coach has used chewing tobacco daily for 25 years and has never smoked cigarettes. He asks whether his habit carries a cancer risk. Smokeless tobacco is most strongly associated with cancer at which of the following sites?

explanation.summary: Smokeless tobacco, such as snuff and chewing tobacco, is associated with oral cancer.
explanation.whyCorrect: Tobacco smoke risk is not limited to lung cancer; cigarette smoking is associated with cancers of the oral cavity, esophagus, pancreas, bladder, kidney, cervix, and bone marrow. Smokeless tobacco, such as snuff and chewing tobacco, is similarly associated with oral cancer and other health problems.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bone marrow cancer is listed among the cancers associated with cigarette smoking, not the site most linked to smokeless tobacco.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Liver cancer in this brick is linked to vinyl chloride (angiosarcoma) and to cirrhosis (hepatocellular carcinoma), not to chewing tobacco.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Nasal cancers are associated with prolonged wood dust exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pleural mesothelioma is associated with asbestos exposure.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 1 of 2: Chemicals and Substances

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman at 10 weeks' gestation smokes one pack of cigarettes daily and asks whether continuing to smoke could affect her pregnancy. She does not drink alcohol. Which of the following outcomes is she at increased risk for if she continues?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cerebral edema and white matter demyelination in the fetus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fetal facial anomalies with a smooth philtrum and thin upper lip

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fetal microcephaly from apoptosis of developing cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neonatal hemorrhage of the mammillary bodies

choices.label: E
choices.text: Spontaneous abortion and reduced intrauterine growth

explanation.summary: Maternal smoking increases the risk of spontaneous abortions, preterm births, and reduced birth weight and intrauterine growth.
explanation.whyCorrect: Among the non-neoplastic diseases and injuries associated with tobacco smoke is an increased risk of spontaneous abortions, preterm births, and reduced birth weight and intrauterine growth with maternal smoking. Tobacco use is also linked to increased myocardial oxygen demand and myocardial infarction, impaired wound healing, emphysema, and increased risk of type 2 diabetes, rheumatoid arthritis, age-related macular degeneration, ectopic pregnancy, and erectile dysfunction.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cerebral edema and white matter demyelination describe lead poisoning in children, not maternal smoking.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A smooth philtrum and thin upper lip are the facial phenotype of fetal alcohol spectrum disorder, and she does not drink.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Microcephaly from apoptosis of developing fetal cells is the proposed teratogenic mechanism of alcohol, not tobacco.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hemorrhage of the mammillary bodies is a finding of Wernicke encephalopathy from thiamine deficiency in chronic alcohol use.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 1 of 2: Chemicals and Substances

questions.stem: A 61-year-old man with a 30-year history of heavy alcohol use is evaluated for persistent memory problems. When asked about the previous day, he confidently describes a visit from a relative that never occurred. His deficits have not improved despite months of abstinence and supplementation. Which of the following best describes this condition?

explanation.summary: Korsakoff syndrome is the severe, usually irreversible manifestation of thiamine deficiency with memory disturbances and confabulation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Malnutrition in chronic alcohol use may result in thiamine (vitamin B1) deficiency. Korsakoff syndrome is the severe, usually irreversible, manifestation of thiamine deficiency in which patients demonstrate memory disturbances and confabulation, the telling of memories that never took place. His fabricated account of a visit and lack of recovery fit this syndrome.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Alcoholic hepatitis is inflammation of the liver and does not explain confabulated memories.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fetal alcohol spectrum disorder results from alcohol exposure during pregnancy and presents with microcephaly, growth restriction, and facial anomalies.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lead encephalopathy causes cerebral edema and demyelination, mainly in children, and is unrelated to his alcohol history.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Wernicke encephalopathy presents acutely with altered mental status, ophthalmoplegia, and ataxic gait and can be treated with thiamine; irreversible confabulation is the Korsakoff stage.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 1 of 2: Chemicals and Substances

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after binge drinking with a very high blood alcohol concentration. Under these conditions, a larger proportion of ethanol is metabolized by a pathway that generates reactive oxygen species and causes lipid peroxidation of hepatocyte membranes. Which of the following enzymes is responsible for this pathway?

explanation.summary: The microsomal ethanol-oxidizing system (MEOS), driven by CYP2E1, handles a greater share of ethanol at high blood alcohol concentrations and generates reactive oxygen species that peroxidize hepatocyte membranes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Most alcohol is metabolized by alcohol dehydrogenase to acetaldehyde. A small proportion, particularly in cases of high blood alcohol concentrations, is processed using the microsomal ethanol-oxidizing system (MEOS) with the help of CYP2E1, a member of the cytochrome P-450 enzyme family. The MEOS pathway generates damaging reactive oxygen species, which can cause lipid peroxidation of hepatocyte membranes. Both pathways produce the intermediate acetaldehyde.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Alcohol dehydrogenase handles the majority of ethanol and its main consequence is a shift in NAD/NADH balance, not ROS-driven lipid peroxidation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Aldehyde dehydrogenase converts acetaldehyde to acetic acid; it does not oxidize ethanol itself.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Glutathione peroxidase processes hydrogen peroxide to water and is a protective, not an ethanol-oxidizing, enzyme.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Superoxide dismutase detoxifies superoxide to hydrogen peroxide; it does not metabolize ethanol.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 1 of 2: Chemicals and Substances

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman of East Asian heritage develops facial flushing, nausea, and tachycardia within minutes of drinking a single glass of wine. Which of the following best explains her reaction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enhanced processing of acetaldehyde to acetyl CoA

choices.label: B
choices.text: Excess NADH generated by alcohol dehydrogenase depleting NAD

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased CYP2E1 activity generating reactive oxygen species

choices.label: D
choices.text: Low aldehyde dehydrogenase activity causing acetaldehyde accumulation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Thiamine deficiency impairing the tricarboxylic acid cycle

explanation.summary: Low aldehyde dehydrogenase activity, from a lysine-for-glutamine substitution common in many people of Asian heritage, impairs oxidation of acetaldehyde and causes alcohol intolerance with flushing, nausea, and tachycardia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Acetaldehyde is usually short-lived because aldehyde dehydrogenase further processes it to acetic acid (acetate). Patients with low aldehyde dehydrogenase activity have difficulty oxidizing acetaldehyde, resulting in intolerance to alcohol with nausea, flushing, and tachycardia following ingestion. Some populations, including many of Asian heritage, have low-functioning aldehyde dehydrogenase due to a substitution of lysine for glutamine.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Enhanced processing of acetaldehyde would lower, not raise, acetaldehyde levels and would not produce intolerance.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The NADH/NAD shift from alcohol dehydrogenase leads to fatty liver and lactic acidosis, not immediate flushing and tachycardia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: CYP2E1 activity through the MEOS pathway causes lipid peroxidation of hepatocyte membranes, not an acute flushing reaction.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Thiamine deficiency produces Wernicke encephalopathy after chronic malnutrition, not symptoms minutes after one drink.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 1 of 2: Chemicals and Substances

questions.stem: A 39-year-old man with chronic heavy alcohol use presents after a weekend of continuous drinking. Laboratory studies show a metabolic acidosis with an elevated serum lactate. Which of the following best explains the elevated lactate?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decreased NAD availability impairing conversion of lactate to pyruvate

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased acetyl CoA driving fatty acid synthesis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Portal hypertension shunting blood away from the liver

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reactive oxygen species from acetaldehyde metabolism inducing apoptosis

explanation.summary: Alcohol dehydrogenase consumes NAD, and because NAD is needed to convert lactate to pyruvate, alcohol use leads to lactic acidosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: The processing of alcohol by alcohol dehydrogenase reduces the availability of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD) while increasing NADH. Since NAD is needed for fatty acid oxidation and conversion of lactate to pyruvate, the shift in the availability of NAD leads to the accumulation of fat in the liver of alcoholics as well as lactic acidosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acetaldehyde-DNA adducts are linked to laryngeal and esophageal cancer, not to lactate accumulation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Some acetaldehyde is processed to acetyl CoA for fatty acid synthesis, but this does not explain impaired lactate clearance.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Portal hypertension is a consequence of cirrhosis that produces esophageal varices; it is not the mechanism of alcohol-related lactic acidosis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Reactive oxygen species inducing apoptosis is the proposed mechanism of fetal alcohol teratogenesis, not lactic acidosis.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 1 of 2: Chemicals and Substances

questions.stem: A 54-year-old man with alcoholic cirrhosis presents with massive hematemesis. Endoscopy reveals dilated, tortuous veins in the distal esophagus that are actively bleeding. Which of the following best explains the development of these veins?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acetaldehyde-DNA adducts in the esophageal epithelium

choices.label: B
choices.text: Direct injury of the esophageal mucosa by alcohol

choices.label: C
choices.text: Portal hypertension from impaired hepatic blood flow

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vasoconstriction of esophageal vessels by nicotine

explanation.summary: Esophageal varices are dilated esophageal veins caused by portal hypertension, a consequence of cirrhosis, and may rupture and hemorrhage.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chronic alcoholism causes alcoholic hepatitis, and continued damage leads to cirrhosis, or fibrosis of the liver. Cirrhosis can impair blood flow through the liver, producing portal hypertension. Esophageal varices are dilated veins in the esophagus due to portal hypertension, a consequence of liver cirrhosis that can occur secondary to chronic alcohol use, and these varices may rupture and hemorrhage. Cirrhosis is further associated with risk for hepatocellular carcinoma.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acetaldehyde-DNA adducts are linked to laryngeal and esophageal cancer, not to varices.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Direct injury by alcohol causes gastritis, ulcers, and hemorrhage in the gastrointestinal tract, but does not create dilated esophageal veins.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Reduced NAD availability explains fatty liver and lactic acidosis, not the venous dilation of portal hypertension.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Nicotine vasoconstriction impairs wound healing in smokers and does not produce venous dilation.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 1 of 2: Chemicals and Substances

questions.stem: A 49-year-old woman with chronic alcohol use and poor nutrition is brought in with confusion, ophthalmoplegia, and a broad-based ataxic gait. Her symptoms improve after administration of a vitamin. The vitamin she lacked normally functions as a coenzyme in which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Conversion of superoxide to hydrogen peroxide

choices.label: D
choices.text: Synthesis of fatty acids from acetyl CoA

explanation.summary: Thiamine is a coenzyme in the tricarboxylic acid cycle; its deficiency in chronic alcohol use causes Wernicke encephalopathy, which is treated with thiamine.
explanation.whyCorrect: Malnutrition in chronic alcohol use may result in thiamine (vitamin B1) deficiency. Thiamine is needed as a coenzyme in the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle (Krebs cycle), and its lack results in metabolic derangements that damage neurons, particularly in the mammillary bodies and thalamus. This is Wernicke encephalopathy, which presents with altered mental status, ophthalmoplegia, and an ataxic, broad-based gait and can be treated with thiamine. Hemorrhage and necrosis of the mammillary bodies is a classic autopsy finding.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Conversion of superoxide to hydrogen peroxide is performed by superoxide dismutase and does not depend on thiamine.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ethanol oxidation to acetaldehyde is carried out by alcohol dehydrogenase and the MEOS pathway, not by a thiamine-dependent enzyme.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Glucuronidation is a Phase II xenobiotic reaction, not a thiamine-dependent pathway.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Fatty acid synthesis from acetyl CoA is a downstream fate of acetaldehyde metabolism and is not the thiamine-dependent step described.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 1 of 2: Chemicals and Substances

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman who is planning a pregnancy asks how much alcohol she can safely drink during pregnancy and when the fetus is most vulnerable. Which of the following is the most accurate response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A small daily amount is considered safe throughout pregnancy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Alcohol becomes safe once the second trimester has begun

choices.label: C
choices.text: Alcohol is harmful to the fetus only during the third trimester

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fetal risk exists only if she also smokes cigarettes during pregnancy

choices.label: E
choices.text: No safe amount is known, and the first trimester is particularly harmful

explanation.summary: A safe, minimal amount of alcohol during pregnancy is unknown, and first-trimester consumption is thought to be particularly harmful.
explanation.whyCorrect: Fetal alcohol spectrum disorders present as microcephaly and intrauterine growth restriction, with mental deficits in childhood and a facial phenotype of thin upper lip, smooth philtrum, and short palpebral fissures. A safe, minimal amount of alcohol consumption is unknown during pregnancy, and consumption during the first trimester is thought to be particularly harmful.

whyWrongByChoice.A: No safe, minimal amount of alcohol in pregnancy has been established.
whyWrongByChoice.B: No trimester is known to be safe; the danger is greatest early rather than resolving after the first trimester.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The first trimester, not the third, is thought to be the particularly harmful period.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Alcohol is teratogenic on its own through reactive oxygen species and apoptosis of fetal cells; smoking is a separate risk for spontaneous abortion and growth restriction.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease Part 1 of 2: Chemicals and Substances

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man is brought to the morgue after a fatal assault. The medical examiner notes a wound on the scalp that has irregular, ragged margins with strands of intact tissue seen bridging the depths of the wound. There is surrounding abrasion and contusion of the skin. Which of the following terms best describes this wound?

explanation.summary: Blunt-force tearing of skin produces a laceration with jagged edges and characteristic tissue bridging.
explanation.whyCorrect: A laceration results when blunt force overstretches and tears the skin. Because the tissue is torn rather than cut, the wound has irregular jagged margins and, diagnostically, intact strands of tissue (nerves, vessels) bridge the depths. Surrounding abrasion and contusion are common because the same blunt impact injures adjacent tissue.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An abrasion is a superficial graze that removes only epidermis; it does not have bridging strands.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A contusion is bleeding into tissue beneath intact skin, not an open wound with torn margins.
whyWrongByChoice.C: An incised wound is made by a sharp edge and has clean, straight margins with no tissue bridging.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A puncture wound is narrow and deeper than it is wide, produced by a pointed instrument, not a tearing force.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease: Physical and Environmental Injury

questions.stem: A 3-year-old girl is evaluated for possible abuse. Examination reveals several areas of skin discoloration over the back and buttocks that range from bluish-purple to yellow-green. The overlying skin is intact. Which of the following processes best explains these findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A clean cut produced by a sharp edge

choices.label: B
choices.text: Coagulative necrosis from a thermal source

choices.label: C
choices.text: Removal of the superficial epidermis by friction

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rupture of small vessels with hemorrhage

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tearing of skin by an overstretching blunt force

explanation.summary: A contusion is hemorrhage into tissue from ruptured vessels beneath skin that remains intact.
explanation.whyCorrect: A contusion (bruise) is produced by blunt force that ruptures small blood vessels while leaving the skin surface intact. Extravasated blood is progressively broken down, so the discoloration evolves through characteristic colors; the range of colors here indicates lesions of differing ages, which raises concern for repeated injury.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A clean cut by a sharp edge is an incised wound, not an area of discoloration under intact skin.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Coagulative necrosis from heat describes a thermal burn, which produces blistering or eschar, not evolving bruises.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Friction removal of epidermis describes an abrasion, which is an open superficial graze rather than subsurface bleeding.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tearing by blunt force describes a laceration, an open wound with jagged bridged margins.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease: Physical and Environmental Injury

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man dies of a gunshot wound. On external examination, the medical examiner finds a round skin defect on the chest that is surrounded by a rim of abraded skin and a zone of surrounding soot deposition and punctate powder tattooing. Compared with the wound found on the back, this wound is smaller and more regular. Which of the following best characterizes this finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A blast injury from an explosion

choices.label: C
choices.text: A distant entrance wound with no residue

choices.label: D
choices.text: A puncture wound from a knife

choices.label: E
choices.text: An exit wound produced at long range

explanation.summary: Gunshot entrance wounds are round with an abrasion collar; soot and stippling indicate a close firing range.
explanation.whyCorrect: A bullet entrance wound is typically smaller and rounder than the exit wound and is ringed by an abrasion collar where the projectile scrapes the skin. Deposition of soot and stippling (powder tattooing) around the defect indicates the muzzle was close to the skin, because these residues travel only a short distance.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A blast injury produces widespread irregular fragmentation and burns, not a single round collared defect.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A distant entrance wound would still have an abrasion collar but would lack the soot and stippling seen here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A knife produces a sharp-edged stab wound without an abrasion collar or powder tattooing.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Exit wounds are usually larger and more irregular than entrance wounds and lack an abrasion collar or powder residue.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease: Physical and Environmental Injury

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man is pulled from a house fire. On the anterior chest and abdomen the skin is dry, white, and leathery in texture, and the affected areas are notably insensate to pinprick, whereas adjacent reddened blistered areas are exquisitely painful. Which of the following best describes the white, insensate regions?

explanation.summary: Full-thickness (third-degree) burns destroy the entire dermis and its nerves, producing painless, leathery, white eschar.
explanation.whyCorrect: A third-degree (full-thickness) burn destroys the entire epidermis and dermis, including cutaneous nerve endings, so the burn is painless (anesthetic). The devitalized tissue appears white to charred and leathery (eschar), and because the dermal appendages that regenerate skin are gone, these areas require grafting.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A contusion is subsurface bleeding under intact skin and is unrelated to thermal eschar.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A deep partial-thickness burn still spares part of the dermis and retains some sensation; it is not fully leathery and anesthetic.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A first-degree burn involves only the epidermis and appears red and dry but remains painful with intact skin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A superficial partial-thickness burn is moist, red, and blistered and is very painful, not white and insensate.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease: Physical and Environmental Injury

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman is hospitalized with full-thickness burns over 40% of her body surface area. On the fourth day she develops hematemesis and melena. Endoscopy reveals multiple superficial gastric and duodenal ulcerations. Which of the following complications of severe burns does this represent?

explanation.summary: Severe burns predispose to acute stress ulcers of the stomach and duodenum, classically called Curling ulcers.
explanation.whyCorrect: Extensive burns cause splanchnic hypoperfusion and mucosal ischemia that lead to acute stress ulceration of the stomach and proximal duodenum, known as Curling ulcers. These superficial erosions can bleed, presenting as hematemesis and melena, as in this patient.

whyWrongByChoice.A: There is no history of NSAID use, and the ulcers here are the classic stress ulceration of severe burns.
whyWrongByChoice.C: H. pylori causes chronic gastritis and peptic ulcers over time, not acute ulcers appearing days after a burn.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A Mallory-Weiss tear is a mucosal laceration at the gastroesophageal junction from retching, not diffuse stress ulcers.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Zollinger-Ellison syndrome is caused by a gastrin-secreting tumor with markedly elevated gastrin, not by burn-related ischemia.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease: Physical and Environmental Injury

questions.stem: A 32-year-old man is recovering in the burn unit with extensive full-thickness burns. On hospital day 6 he becomes febrile and hypotensive. Examination of the burn eschar shows greenish discoloration with a fruity odor, and blood cultures grow a gram-negative rod. Infection with which of the following organisms is the most likely cause?

explanation.summary: Burn wounds are classically colonized and invaded by Pseudomonas aeruginosa, a leading cause of burn sepsis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Loss of the skin barrier and the moist, protein-rich eschar make burn wounds highly susceptible to infection, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a characteristic pathogen. It is a gram-negative rod that produces pigments giving a greenish, sometimes fruity-smelling wound and can invade the bloodstream to cause life-threatening sepsis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Candida is a fungus, not a gram-negative rod, and typically causes later fungal superinfection.
whyWrongByChoice.B: E. coli is a gram-negative rod but is not the characteristic organism of invasive burn-wound sepsis and lacks the greenish pigment.
whyWrongByChoice.D: S. aureus is a gram-positive coccus and does not produce the green pigment or fruity odor described.
whyWrongByChoice.E: S. pyogenes is a gram-positive coccus causing cellulitis but does not match a gram-negative rod with green discoloration.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease: Physical and Environmental Injury

questions.stem: A 19-year-old football player collapses during practice on a hot, humid day. He is confused and combative. His skin is hot, and his rectal temperature is 41.2 C (106.2 F). Laboratory studies later show elevated creatine kinase and evidence of disseminated intravascular coagulation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Heat stroke is failure of thermoregulation with core temperature above 40 C, CNS dysfunction, and multiorgan injury.
explanation.whyCorrect: Heat stroke occurs when thermoregulatory mechanisms fail and the core temperature rises above 40 C. It presents with CNS dysfunction (confusion, combativeness) and can cause rhabdomyolysis (elevated CK) and DIC. It is a medical emergency requiring rapid cooling.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Heat cramps are painful muscle cramps from electrolyte loss with a normal core temperature and intact mental status.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Heat exhaustion causes fatigue and dizziness with a temperature below 40 C and preserved mentation, without DIC.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Malignant hyperthermia is triggered by inhaled anesthetics or succinylcholine during anesthesia, not by exertion in the heat.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome follows exposure to antipsychotic (dopamine-blocking) drugs, which this patient did not receive.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease: Physical and Environmental Injury

questions.stem: A 20-year-old man undergoes general anesthesia with an inhaled halogenated agent and succinylcholine. Minutes later he develops generalized muscle rigidity, a rapidly rising temperature, and a markedly elevated end-tidal CO2. Which of the following underlying defects best explains this reaction?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Loss-of-function mutation in the CFTR chloride channel

explanation.summary: Malignant hyperthermia results from RYR1 (ryanodine receptor) mutations that trigger massive Ca2+ release after certain anesthetics.
explanation.whyCorrect: Malignant hyperthermia is an inherited disorder, most often due to mutation of the skeletal muscle ryanodine receptor (RYR1). Exposure to inhaled halogenated anesthetics or succinylcholine causes uncontrolled Ca2+ release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum, producing sustained muscle contraction (rigidity), heat generation with hyperthermia, and increased CO2 production. Treatment is dantrolene.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Anti-acetylcholine-receptor antibodies cause myasthenia gravis (weakness), not hypermetabolic rigidity and hyperthermia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Pseudocholinesterase deficiency prolongs succinylcholine-induced paralysis (apnea) but does not cause rigidity or hyperthermia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hypothalamic injury alters temperature set point but does not produce this acute anesthetic-triggered hypermetabolic crisis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: CFTR mutations cause cystic fibrosis, unrelated to anesthetic-induced hyperthermia.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease: Physical and Environmental Injury

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man is found after being stranded outdoors overnight in freezing temperatures. His fingers and toes are hard, white, and insensate. Over the following days these digits become dusky and demarcate into blackened, mummified tissue. Which of the following best explains the initial cellular injury?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Coagulative necrosis from a thermal (heat) source

explanation.summary: Frostbite injures tissue through ice-crystal formation and freezing-induced vascular damage, leading to distal gangrene.
explanation.whyCorrect: Frostbite occurs when tissue freezes: intracellular and extracellular ice crystals form and injure cells directly, while freezing and vasoconstriction damage the local microvasculature and cause ischemia. The poorly perfused, most exposed distal parts (fingers, toes) undergo necrosis and can progress to dry gangrene with demarcation and mummification.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Autonomic denervation does not cause the acute freezing necrosis seen after cold exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.B: There is no infection preceding the injury; exotoxin-mediated necrosis does not explain freezing of exposed digits.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Coagulative necrosis from heat describes a burn, the opposite thermal extreme, not a freezing injury.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Immune-complex vasculitis is an immunologic process unrelated to environmental cold exposure.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease: Physical and Environmental Injury

questions.stem: A 40-year-old worker is accidentally exposed to a high dose of whole-body ionizing radiation. Two to three weeks later he develops fever, mucosal bleeding, and a serious bacterial infection. A complete blood count shows profound leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, and anemia. Injury to which of the following cell populations best accounts for these findings?

explanation.summary: Ionizing radiation preferentially kills rapidly dividing cells; loss of marrow progenitors produces the hematopoietic syndrome.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ionizing radiation is most toxic to rapidly proliferating cells. The bone marrow hematopoietic progenitors are highly radiosensitive, so their loss produces the hematopoietic (bone marrow) syndrome: pancytopenia that manifests over 1-3 weeks as infection (leukopenia), bleeding (thrombocytopenia), and anemia.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Hepatocytes divide slowly and are relatively radioresistant compared with marrow precursors.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cardiac myocytes are terminally differentiated and relatively radioresistant; they do not explain acute pancytopenia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Peripheral neurons are non-dividing and relatively resistant; their injury would not cause cytopenias.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Skeletal muscle fibers are non-proliferating and radioresistant, so they are not the source of these blood findings.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease: Physical and Environmental Injury

questions.stem: A cohort of survivors who received significant whole-body ionizing radiation exposure is followed for decades. Compared with the general population, these individuals have a substantially increased incidence of leukemia and various solid tumors appearing years after the exposure. Which of the following mechanisms best explains this delayed effect?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chronic hypersensitivity reaction to residual radioisotopes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Depletion of intestinal crypt stem cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: DNA double-strand breaks and mutations in surviving cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Immune tolerance to tumor antigens caused by radiation

explanation.summary: Radiation is carcinogenic because it causes DNA damage and mutations that, in surviving cells, can drive malignant transformation years later.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ionizing radiation damages DNA, characteristically causing double-strand breaks. Cells that survive with unrepaired or misrepaired mutations may accumulate oncogenic changes, so radiation is a well-established carcinogen. Malignancies such as leukemia and solid tumors arise after a long latency of years to decades.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Delayed cancer is due to mutagenesis, not a hypersensitivity (allergic) reaction to isotopes.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Crypt stem cell depletion causes the acute gastrointestinal syndrome, not delayed carcinogenesis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Thermal coagulation is an acute effect of heat, not the mechanism of late radiation-induced cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Radiation does not induce tumor-specific immune tolerance; its carcinogenicity stems from DNA mutation.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease: Physical and Environmental Injury

questions.stem: During winter, a family living in a poorly ventilated home with a faulty gas furnace develops headache, dizziness, nausea, and confusion. Several are found unconscious. Their skin and mucous membranes appear cherry-red, and pulse oximetry reads falsely normal. Which of the following best explains their condition?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cyanide inhibition of the electron transport chain from smoke

explanation.summary: Indoor combustion produces carbon monoxide, which binds hemoglobin with high affinity and causes hypoxic injury with cherry-red skin.
explanation.whyCorrect: Carbon monoxide, a common indoor air pollutant from faulty heaters and incomplete combustion, binds hemoglobin with roughly 200 times the affinity of oxygen, forming carboxyhemoglobin and impairing oxygen carriage and delivery. This causes systemic hypoxia (headache, confusion, loss of consciousness), the classic cherry-red skin, and a falsely normal pulse oximetry reading because the device cannot distinguish carboxyhemoglobin from oxyhemoglobin.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Cyanide poisoning is chiefly from combustion of certain materials in fires, and this scenario points to CO from a gas furnace with the classic cherry-red hue.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis is an immunologic lung disease with cough and dyspnea, not acute cherry-red hypoxia in the whole family.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Methemoglobinemia causes chocolate-brown blood and cyanosis, not cherry-red skin, and follows oxidizing agents rather than furnace fumes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Radon is a radioactive gas that raises long-term lung cancer risk; it does not cause acute cherry-red carbon monoxide-type poisoning.

questions.topicName: Environmental Disease: Physical and Environmental Injury

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after being shot in the abdomen. Despite resuscitation he dies of massive hemorrhage. At autopsy, the gunshot wound to the abdomen is documented as the event that resulted in his death. This gunshot wound is best classified as which of the following?

explanation.summary: The cause of death is the injury or disease that resulted in death.
explanation.whyCorrect: The cause of death is defined as the injury or disease that resulted in death. A gunshot wound that kills a patient is the classic example given in the brick, so it represents the cause of death.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The final anatomic diagnosis is a section of the autopsy report that lists pathologic findings, not a category of death.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The manner of death is the medicolegal category (natural, homicide, suicide, accident, or undetermined) into which the death is placed, not the injury.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The mechanism of death is the physiologic derangement produced by the cause; here that would be the exsanguination, not the wound itself.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The preliminary autopsy diagnosis is an early autopsy report released within two working days, not a description of the fatal injury.

questions.topicName: Autopsy

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man collapses and dies. At autopsy, severe atherosclerotic coronary artery disease is found to have caused inadequate blood flow to the myocardium, producing lethal cardiac ischemia. Which of the following is the mechanism of death in this case?

explanation.summary: The mechanism of death is the physiologic derangement produced by the cause of death.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cardiac ischemia, the lack of blood flow to the heart, is a physiologic derangement rather than a specific disease, so it is the mechanism of death. The brick uses this exact example to contrast mechanism with cause and manner.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Atherosclerotic coronary artery disease is the underlying disease process that led to death, making it the cause of death, not the mechanism.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Homicide is a manner of death and does not fit a death from intrinsic coronary disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Natural is a manner of death, the medicolegal classification; it is not a physiologic derangement.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Undetermined is a manner of death used when the category cannot be established, which does not apply to a clear ischemic cardiac death.

questions.topicName: Autopsy

questions.stem: A 26-year-old man slips on a dock, is knocked unconscious, and falls into a lake, where he drowns. After a thorough autopsy the pathologist concludes that the death occurred as an accident. This conclusion that the death was an accident represents which of the following aspects of the death?

explanation.summary: The manner of death classifies how the death occurred into one of five medicolegal categories.
explanation.whyCorrect: The manner of death explains how the cause of death occurred and is divided into natural, homicide, suicide, accident, and undetermined. Classifying this death as an accident is a determination of the manner of death.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The cause of death would be the injury or disease that killed him (e.g., drowning/head injury), not the label 'accident.'
whyWrongByChoice.B: The clinical summary is a section of the autopsy report summarizing clinical information, not a category of manner.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Gross findings are the macroscopic descriptions recorded in the report, not the manner of death.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The mechanism of death would be the physiologic derangement, such as cerebral hypoxia from drowning.

questions.topicName: Autopsy

questions.stem: A hospital pathologist is asked to review several deaths to decide which is most appropriate for a medical (clinical) autopsy rather than a forensic investigation. Which of the following cases would most likely qualify as a medical autopsy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A 29-year-old who died in an unwitnessed motor vehicle collision

choices.label: B
choices.text: A 33-year-old found dead following a drug overdose

choices.label: C
choices.text: A 44-year-old found dead at a construction site

choices.label: D
choices.text: A 55-year-old who died of a gunshot wound

choices.label: E
choices.text: A 66-year-old who died of longstanding alcoholic cardiomyopathy

explanation.summary: Medical autopsies investigate natural disease, whereas violent, unexpected, or traumatic deaths fall under forensic jurisdiction.
explanation.whyCorrect: The medical autopsy documents and investigates a natural disease. Death from longstanding alcoholic cardiomyopathy is a natural death and is well suited to a medical autopsy to characterize the disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An unwitnessed motor vehicle collision is a violent/unexpected death subject to medicolegal investigation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A drug overdose is an unnatural death that would likely require medicolegal (forensic) review.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A death found at a construction site suggests an industrial accident, a forensic case.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A gunshot wound is a violent death that qualifies for forensic autopsy.

questions.topicName: Autopsy

questions.stem: A hospitalist is reviewing several deaths to determine which is least likely to fall under medical examiner or coroner jurisdiction. Which of the following deaths is least likely to require medicolegal investigation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A 19-year-old found unconscious and pulseless in a public park

choices.label: B
choices.text: A 3-month-old found unresponsive in a crib

choices.label: C
choices.text: A 76-year-old with widely metastatic prostate cancer

choices.label: D
choices.text: A previously healthy adult who dies suddenly and unexpectedly

choices.label: E
choices.text: A stillborn fetus delivered to a mother with a suspected history of domestic abuse

explanation.summary: Expected deaths from known natural disease are least likely to require medicolegal investigation.
explanation.whyCorrect: A death from widely metastatic prostate cancer is an expected natural death; it may undergo a medical autopsy but would be unlikely to fall under medical examiner or coroner jurisdiction.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An unwitnessed, unexpected death of a young person in a park would earn medicolegal investigation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: An unexpected death of an otherwise healthy infant in a crib warrants medicolegal investigation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A sudden, unexpected death in a previously healthy person is a reportable, medicolegal event.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A stillbirth in the context of possible maternal trauma or abuse may require medicolegal investigation.

questions.topicName: Autopsy

questions.stem: A medical student is comparing the coroner system with the medical examiner system in the United States. Which of the following statements most accurately describes a coroner?

choices.label: B
choices.text: A federal official who oversees organ donation registries

choices.label: C
choices.text: A hospital physician who signs consent for medical autopsies

choices.label: D
choices.text: A pathologist who performs all medicolegal autopsies for a state

choices.label: E
choices.text: An appointed physician who is a trained forensic pathologist

explanation.summary: A coroner is typically an elected lay official who investigates death but usually cannot perform autopsies.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the most common coroner system the coroner is elected to the position and is not required to be a physician or medical expert; coroners are typically not qualified to perform autopsies but do assign cause and manner of death.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Organ donation is handled by separate donation registries, not by coroners.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Signing consent for a medical autopsy is done by the decedent's next of kin, not the coroner.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Performing medicolegal autopsies is the role of the medical examiner or a forensic pathologist, not a lay coroner.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This describes a medical examiner, who is appointed and trained as a forensic pathologist.

questions.topicName: Autopsy

questions.stem: A patient dies in the hospital of a suspected neurodegenerative disease, and the care team wishes to obtain a medical autopsy. The patient is survived by a spouse, an adult son, both parents, and a sister. From whom should the team first seek legal consent for the autopsy?

explanation.summary: Consent for autopsy follows a next-of-kin priority list, with the spouse ranked highest.
explanation.whyCorrect: The legal next of kin authorized to give consent follows a priority order from highest to lowest: spouse, then adult son or daughter, then parent or guardian, then brother or sister. The spouse is highest and should be approached first.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A cousin is near the bottom of the next-of-kin priority list.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A parent ranks below both the spouse and adult children.
whyWrongByChoice.C: An adult child ranks below the spouse on the consent priority list.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A sibling ranks below the spouse, children, and parents.

questions.topicName: Autopsy

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man dies unexpectedly in police custody at a county jail, and the case is accepted by the medical examiner for a forensic autopsy. The decedent's family objects and refuses to sign an autopsy consent form. Which of the following is the most accurate statement regarding consent in this situation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Consent must be obtained from the treating clinician instead

choices.label: B
choices.text: The medical examiner may perform only a partial autopsy without consent

choices.label: C
choices.text: The autopsy cannot proceed without the spouse's written consent

choices.label: D
choices.text: The family may authorize only a brain-only examination

choices.label: E
choices.text: The medical examiner may perform the autopsy without family consent

explanation.summary: Medical examiner and coroner cases do not require family consent for autopsy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Deaths under medicolegal jurisdiction, such as a death at a jail, are reportable and become medical examiner cases, which do not require consent from the family for the autopsy to proceed.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A treating clinician cannot authorize consent, and no consent is needed for a medicolegal case.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The full/partial distinction applies to consented medical autopsies, not to medicolegal cases.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Family consent, including that of a spouse, is required for medical autopsies, not for medical examiner cases.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A brain-only examination is an example of a family-restricted partial medical autopsy, which is irrelevant when no consent is required.

questions.topicName: Autopsy

questions.stem: A hospital quality officer is identifying which in-hospital deaths must be reported to the medical examiner's office. Which of the following deaths is required to be reported?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A patient who dies 6 hours after admission for an unexplained illness

choices.label: B
choices.text: A patient who dies after a 3-week hospitalization for pneumonia

choices.label: C
choices.text: A patient who dies of a documented, expected metastatic cancer

choices.label: D
choices.text: A patient who dies of a known chronic obstructive pulmonary disease exacerbation

choices.label: E
choices.text: A patient who dies of end-stage heart failure after a long chronic course

explanation.summary: Sudden or unexpected deaths, including deaths within 24 hours of admission, are reportable to the medical examiner.
explanation.whyCorrect: Reportable deaths include those that are sudden or unexplained and those occurring less than 24 hours after admission to a hospital. A patient dying 6 hours after admission for an unexplained illness meets both criteria.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A death after a 3-week hospitalization for a known infection is an expected natural death occurring well beyond 24 hours of admission.
whyWrongByChoice.C: An expected death from documented metastatic cancer is a natural death and not reportable.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A death from a known chronic disease following its expected course is not a reportable event.
whyWrongByChoice.E: An expected death from a long chronic course of heart failure is a natural, non-reportable death.

questions.topicName: Autopsy

questions.stem: A pathologist is preparing an autopsy report and needs to record that the heart weighed 490 grams and the liver appeared cirrhotic. In which section of a standard medical autopsy report should these macroscopic observations be documented?

explanation.summary: Gross findings capture the macroscopic descriptions and organ weights of an autopsy.
explanation.whyCorrect: The gross findings section records the macroscopic information, such as organ weights and appearance (for example, a cirrhotic liver), and may include photographs and radiographs.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The case discussion gives the pathologist's integrated opinion on the case, not the gross descriptions.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The clinical summary provides pertinent clinical information from the medical record.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The final anatomic diagnosis lists the diagnoses and pathologic findings, typically organized by organ system, rather than the raw macroscopic descriptions.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Microscopic findings describe histologic observations made under the microscope, not organ weights.

questions.topicName: Autopsy

questions.stem: A patient's family calls the clinic after receiving an autopsy report noting 90% stenosis of the left anterior descending artery. They ask whether this finding was the cause of death. In which section of the report would the pathologist most likely provide an opinion on the significance of this stenosis within the clinical context?

explanation.summary: The case discussion integrates clinical and pathologic findings and offers the pathologist's opinion on their significance.
explanation.whyCorrect: The case discussion, or clinicopathologic correlation, is where the pathologist gives an opinion on the case and comments on the relevance of a finding, such as the significance of coronary stenosis, within the clinical context.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Additional findings cover ancillary studies such as toxicology and laboratory results.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The final anatomic diagnosis would list the stenosis as a diagnosis but does not interpret its significance.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Gross findings would describe the artery macroscopically but would not offer an interpretive opinion.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Microscopic findings report histologic observations, not the clinical significance of a lesion.

questions.topicName: Autopsy

questions.stem: A treating clinician is completing a death certificate and must record the specific cause of death rather than a nonspecific terminal event. Which of the following would be least appropriate to list as the cause of death on the certificate?

explanation.summary: Death certificates should record the specific cause, not nonspecific terminal events such as asystole or multiorgan failure.
explanation.whyCorrect: A critical role of the death certificate is documenting the specific cause of death. In general, terminal events such as asystole (lack of a heartbeat) and nonspecific physiologic derangements such as multiorgan failure are not included; the specific cause and contributing conditions are recorded instead.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acquired immunodeficiency syndrome is a specific contributing condition that can be listed as an underlying cause.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Disseminated aspergillosis is a specific disease and an appropriate immediate cause of death, as shown in the brick's example.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Disseminated fungal disease is a specific disease process appropriate for recording as a cause of death.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Human immunodeficiency virus infection is a specific underlying cause that can appear in the causal sequence.

questions.topicName: Autopsy

questions.stem: A 62-year-old woman dies in the hospital after a 4-day admission for pneumonia. During the family meeting, her adult daughter states that she believes the patient was slowly poisoned by an ex-spouse over the preceding months and asks the team to arrange a hospital autopsy to look for poison. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Communicate the concern to the local medical examiner or coroner

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decline any autopsy because the death occurred from natural disease

choices.label: C
choices.text: Have the treating clinician sign the autopsy consent on the family's behalf

choices.label: D
choices.text: Obtain the daughter's signed consent for a full medical autopsy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Order a brain-only partial autopsy with postmortem toxicology

explanation.summary: A family concern about poisoning has medicolegal implications and belongs with the medical examiner or coroner, not a hospital medical autopsy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Before explaining the autopsy process, it is helpful to learn why the autopsy is wanted and whether a medical autopsy can answer the question. A suspicion of poisoning by an ex-spouse is not an appropriate question for a medical autopsy because it has medicolegal implications, and some hospital centers do not perform toxicology, so a poison in the bloodstream could not be investigated. The family's concern should be communicated to the local medical examiner or coroner so a forensic autopsy can be considered.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Suspected poisoning is a potential unnatural death that warrants medicolegal review rather than dismissal.
whyWrongByChoice.C: An unrelated clinician cannot consent for an autopsy, and no medical autopsy should be pursued here in any case.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A medical autopsy investigates natural disease; it is not the appropriate vehicle for a question with medicolegal implications such as suspected poisoning.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A partial brain-only examination would not address the concern, and hospital toxicology may not even be available; the question belongs in the forensic setting.

questions.topicName: Autopsy

questions.stem: An 81-year-old man dies in a nursing home. He had been comatose for three years after sustaining a traumatic head injury in a fall down a flight of stairs, and the nursing staff note that his death was expected. The attending physician plans to sign the death certificate as a natural death and offer the family a medical autopsy. Which of the following best describes how this death should be handled?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It falls under medicolegal investigation because the inciting injury was trauma

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is a natural death; a medical autopsy may proceed with family consent

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is exempt from review because more than one year elapsed since the injury

choices.label: D
choices.text: It requires consent from both the spouse and the nursing home administrator

choices.label: E
choices.text: It should proceed as a partial autopsy limited to the brain

explanation.summary: Long delays between an initial injury and eventual death may still qualify for medicolegal evaluation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Even though the patient died of what looks like natural causes in a nursing home, the case falls under the purview of medicolegal investigation because the inciting injury three years earlier was trauma. Such a trauma could have been the result of an accident, an attack, or a suicide attempt, so the death must be evaluated by the medical examiner or coroner rather than treated as an ordinary natural death.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The death is not simply natural; the causal chain began with trauma, which makes the case medicolegal.
whyWrongByChoice.C: There is no time limit that exempts a trauma-initiated death from medicolegal review; long delays may still qualify.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A nursing home administrator has no role in autopsy consent, and medicolegal cases do not require family consent at all.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The scope of examination is not the issue; the case belongs to the medicolegal system, where family-restricted partial autopsies do not apply.

questions.topicName: Autopsy

questions.stem: In a rural county, an elected coroner who is not a physician investigates the unwitnessed death of a 45-year-old man found in his garage and determines that a forensic autopsy is necessary. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step for the coroner's office?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Obtain the family's written consent for the autopsy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Perform the autopsy at the county coroner's office

choices.label: C
choices.text: Refer the body to a hospital pathologist for a medical autopsy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Release the body to the funeral home pending toxicology

choices.label: E
choices.text: Send the body to the closest medical examiner's office

explanation.summary: Coroners investigate deaths but typically cannot perform autopsies, so the body is sent to a medical examiner's office for postmortem examination.
explanation.whyCorrect: Coroners are responsible for investigating deaths in their jurisdiction but typically are not qualified to perform autopsies. Thus, a coroner's office must send the body to the closest medical examiner's office for postmortem examination, and the coroner then works with the forensic pathologist who performs the autopsy to assign a cause and manner of death.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Medical examiner and coroner cases do not require consent from the family.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A lay coroner cannot perform autopsies, so the examination cannot be done at the coroner's office.
whyWrongByChoice.C: An unwitnessed, unexpected death is a medicolegal case for forensic autopsy, not a hospital medical autopsy of natural disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Releasing the body before the postmortem examination would forgo the forensic autopsy the coroner deemed necessary.

questions.topicName: Autopsy

questions.stem: A medical student rotating in a state's death investigation system learns that every county has an elected coroner who reviews the circumstances of reported deaths, and that when a forensic autopsy is deemed necessary the body is transported to a single state medical examiner's office housed within the state crime laboratory, which serves as the referral facility for all 75 counties. This arrangement is best described as which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A centralized medical examiner system without coroners

choices.label: B
choices.text: A county-level medical examiner system with multiple offices

choices.label: D
choices.text: A pure coroner system in which coroners perform autopsies

choices.label: E
choices.text: A regional medical examiner system with urban appointees only

explanation.summary: A state with elected county coroners plus a single state medical examiner's office is a mixed coroner-medical examiner system.
explanation.whyCorrect: Arkansas is the example given of a mixed coroner-medical examiner system: each county has an elected coroner, but there is also a state medical examiner's office. Local coroners investigate and review the circumstances of a reported death, and when a forensic autopsy is deemed necessary the body is transported to Little Rock, where the State Medical Examiner's Office within the State Crime Laboratory serves as the referral office and facility for 75 counties.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The presence of elected county coroners means the system is not a medical-examiner-only model.
whyWrongByChoice.B: In a county or regional medical examiner model, multiple medical examiner offices operate simultaneously; here there is a single state office.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Coroners cannot perform autopsies; the autopsies are done at the state medical examiner's office.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The urban-appointee model describes states such as Georgia and Texas that appoint medical examiners in major cities while keeping rural coroners; this arrangement instead has a single statewide referral office.

questions.topicName: Autopsy

questions.stem: A forensic pathology fellow compares death investigation models across several states. In one state, regional investigators conduct the local investigation of reported deaths, and all bodies requiring autopsy are then sent to one office that oversees death investigation for the entire state. Which of the following medical examiner models does this describe?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A state medical examiner in a centralized office

choices.label: B
choices.text: County medical examiners appointed in each county

choices.label: C
choices.text: Elected coroners referring cases to a hospital pathologist

choices.label: D
choices.text: Regional medical examiners with multiple operational offices

choices.label: E
choices.text: Urban medical examiners with coroners in rural locales

explanation.summary: Some states employ a single state medical examiner in a centralized office, with regional investigators conducting local investigations and sending bodies to the central office.
explanation.whyCorrect: Medical examiner models vary by state. In the centralized model, a state medical examiner in a centralized office oversees death investigation for the entire state; regional investigators conduct local investigations, and then bodies are sent to the state medical examiner office for autopsy.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A county-level model likewise has multiple offices operating simultaneously rather than a single statewide office.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Coroners do not refer forensic cases to hospital pathologists for medical autopsy; forensic autopsies are performed at medical examiner offices.
whyWrongByChoice.D: In the regional model, medical examiners work at a regional level such that multiple offices are operational in the state at the same time, rather than one central office.
whyWrongByChoice.E: States like Georgia and Texas appoint medical examiners in major urban centers but retain coroners for rural death investigation; that is a dual system, not a single centralized office.

questions.topicName: Autopsy

questions.stem: A hospital administrator is drafting a policy on reporting deaths to the local death investigation authority and wants to describe what a coroner and a medical examiner have in common. Which of the following responsibilities is shared by both a typical elected coroner and an appointed medical examiner?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Completing the hospital death certificate for inpatient deaths

choices.label: B
choices.text: Holding board certification in forensic pathology

choices.label: C
choices.text: Investigating deaths and assigning a cause and manner of death

choices.label: D
choices.text: Obtaining next-of-kin consent before any autopsy

explanation.summary: Both coroners and medical examiners investigate deaths in their jurisdiction and assign a cause and manner of death; only the medical examiner can also perform autopsies.
explanation.whyCorrect: Like coroners, medical examiners are in charge of death investigation for their assigned jurisdiction, including determination of a cause and manner of death. The duties differ in that a coroner investigates death but cannot perform autopsies, whereas a medical examiner investigates death and can perform autopsies.

whyWrongByChoice.A: In the hospital setting, death certificates are filled out by the treating clinician, not by the coroner or medical examiner.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The medical examiner is commonly a trained forensic pathologist; the typical coroner is an elected lay official who need not be a physician.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Medical examiner and coroner cases do not require family consent for autopsy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Only the medical examiner (a forensic pathologist) can perform autopsies; the coroner must send the body to a medical examiner's office.

questions.topicName: Autopsy

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man with a long history of coronary artery disease is admitted with chest pain and dies 10 hours later. Because the death occurred within 24 hours of admission, the resident reports it to the medical examiner's office. After reviewing the circumstances, the medical examiner declines to accept the case. The family would like to know the extent of his heart disease. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cancel the autopsy because the case was declined by the medical examiner

choices.label: B
choices.text: Offer a medical autopsy and obtain consent from the legal next of kin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Proceed with a medical autopsy without family consent

choices.label: D
choices.text: Refer the case to the county coroner to perform the autopsy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Report the death a second time to the state crime laboratory

explanation.summary: A reportable death is not automatically accepted by the medical examiner; if jurisdiction is declined, a medical autopsy can proceed with next-of-kin consent.
explanation.whyCorrect: Before proceeding with a medical autopsy it is important to consider whether the death is reportable, and a death within less than 24 hours of hospital admission must be reported. However, just because a death is reportable does not mean the medical examiner or coroner will accept jurisdiction; every case is considered on its own merit and circumstances. Once the medical examiner declines, the case returns to the hospital pathway, and a medical autopsy investigating the natural disease requires signed consent from the legal next of kin.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Declining jurisdiction does not preclude an autopsy; it means the death can be handled as a medical autopsy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Outside of forensic cases, medical autopsies require approval and consent from the decedent's family.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Coroners cannot perform autopsies, and the medicolegal system has already declined the case.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The reporting obligation has been satisfied; the medical examiner has already reviewed and declined the case.

questions.topicName: Autopsy

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man with no living relatives dies in the hospital of suspected amyloidosis. His care team would like a medical autopsy to confirm the diagnosis. He is survived only by a long-time friend who has been charged by law with responsibility for his burial. The attending physician, who has known the patient for 10 years, offers to sign the consent. Which of the following is the most accurate statement regarding consent in this case?

choices.label: A
choices.text: No autopsy can be performed because there is no blood relative

choices.label: B
choices.text: The attending physician may consent because he knew the patient well

choices.label: C
choices.text: The friend responsible for the burial may give consent

choices.label: D
choices.text: The hospital ethics committee must consent in place of the family

choices.label: E
choices.text: The medical examiner must be asked to authorize the autopsy

explanation.summary: A friend or person charged by law with responsibility for the burial is the lowest tier on the consent priority list, and an unrelated clinician cannot consent.
explanation.whyCorrect: The priority list for autopsy consent, from highest to lowest, ends with a friend or person charged by law with responsibility for the burial. With no spouse, children, parents, siblings, extended family, or other next of kin, that friend is the person authorized to give consent. An unrelated clinician cannot consent for an autopsy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The consent list extends beyond relatives to the person charged with responsibility for the burial, so an autopsy remains possible.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Of note, an unrelated clinician cannot consent for an autopsy regardless of the length of the relationship.
whyWrongByChoice.D: An ethics committee is not on the list of persons authorized to give autopsy consent.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This is an expected natural death and not a medicolegal case; the medical examiner does not authorize medical autopsies.

questions.topicName: Autopsy

questions.stem: A 34-year-old unmarried woman with no children dies in the hospital of fulminant hepatic failure of uncertain cause, and the team requests a medical autopsy. Both of her parents are deceased, and she had no siblings. She is survived by a maternal aunt, a first cousin, and a close friend who has offered to handle the funeral. From whom should consent for the autopsy first be sought?

explanation.summary: Grandparents, grandchildren, uncles, aunts, nieces, and nephews outrank cousins and friends on the consent priority list.
explanation.whyCorrect: The consent priority list, from highest to lowest, is spouse; adult son or daughter; parent or guardian; brother or sister; grandparent, grandchild, uncle, aunt, niece, or nephew; any other next of kin (cousin); and finally a friend or person charged by law with responsibility for the burial. With no relatives in the first four tiers, the aunt occupies the highest remaining tier and should be approached first.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An unrelated clinician cannot consent for an autopsy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A friend or person responsible for the burial is the lowest tier and is approached only if no next of kin exists.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A cousin falls under 'any other next of kin,' which ranks below the aunt-uncle-grandparent tier.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hospital administrators are not on the list of persons authorized to give autopsy consent.

questions.topicName: Autopsy

questions.stem: The family of a 79-year-old woman who died with progressive dementia consents to an autopsy but asks that only the brain be examined so that the rest of the body is left untouched. The pathologist explains the potential drawback of this request. Which of the following best summarizes the pathologist's concern?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A restricted autopsy must be approved by the medical examiner

choices.label: B
choices.text: Brain-only examinations are prohibited under most state consent laws

choices.label: C
choices.text: Formalin fixation cannot be performed on an isolated brain

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neurodegenerative disease cannot be diagnosed at autopsy

explanation.summary: Consent may be for a full or partial autopsy, but most practitioners advise against partial autopsies because they give partial answers.
explanation.whyCorrect: Consent can be for a full autopsy with no restrictions or for a partial autopsy, such as a brain-only examination for neurodegenerative disease. However, most autopsy practitioners advise against partial autopsies, citing the old adage that partial autopsies give partial answers, because findings outside the examined region will be missed.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A consented medical autopsy of natural disease does not involve the medical examiner.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A brain-only examination is explicitly an allowable form of partial consent, not a prohibited one.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The brain is routinely fixed in formalin for at least a week before examination; fixation is not the limitation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Determining the underlying diagnosis in a dementia case is a classic indication for medical autopsy.

questions.topicName: Autopsy

questions.stem: A pathology resident is preparing to perform a consented medical autopsy on a 68-year-old man who died after a prolonged intensive care unit course. Before making any incision or examining the body, which of the following should the resident do first?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Document the presence of therapeutic devices on the body

choices.label: C
choices.text: Make a Y-shaped incision to open the body cavity

choices.label: D
choices.text: Place the brain in formalin for fixation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Thoroughly review the available medical records

explanation.summary: The autopsy process begins with a thorough review of the medical records before the external examination.
explanation.whyCorrect: Before beginning the autopsy, the pathologist thoroughly reviews the available medical records. Only then does the autopsy itself begin with the external examination, followed by the internal examination.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Documenting therapeutic devices such as PICC lines is part of the external examination, which begins after the records review.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The preliminary autopsy diagnosis is issued within 2 working days after the autopsy, not before it.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The Y-shaped incision starts the internal examination, which follows both the records review and the external examination.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Brain fixation occurs after the organs are removed during the internal examination.

questions.topicName: Autopsy
