questions.stem: Five days after a medical autopsy, a neurologist calls the pathology department asking why the brain findings are not yet available even though the preliminary autopsy diagnosis has already been released. Which of the following best explains the delay?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Brain examination requires separate consent from the medical examiner

choices.label: B
choices.text: Neuropathology can only be assessed on microscopic sections

choices.label: C
choices.text: The brain is examined only after the final report is issued

choices.label: D
choices.text: The brain is fixed in formalin for at least a week before examination

choices.label: E
choices.text: The brain must be released to the funeral home before sectioning

explanation.summary: The brain is typically fixed in formalin for at least a week before the 'brain cutting' examination.
explanation.whyCorrect: Unlike the other organs, which are examined, weighed, and dissected at the time of autopsy, the brain is typically fixed in formalin for at least a week before examination, a process colloquially referred to as the 'brain cutting.' Because the preliminary autopsy diagnosis is released within 2 working days, it precedes the brain examination, and its information is limited and subject to change.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A consented medical autopsy does not involve the medical examiner; the family's consent covers the examination.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The 'brain cutting' is a gross examination of the fixed brain; the delay is for fixation, not for histology.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The brain is examined before the final report is issued, since the final report incorporates all gross and microscopic findings.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Whether organs are returned to the body depends on the institution or special request; the brain is not released for examination elsewhere.

questions.topicName: Autopsy

questions.stem: The daughter of a 74-year-old man who died in the hospital is considering consenting to a medical autopsy but is worried that it will postpone the funeral, which is planned for 3 days later. Which of the following is the most accurate information to give her?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The body goes to the funeral home after the autopsy without significant delay

choices.label: B
choices.text: The body is held until the final autopsy report is complete

choices.label: C
choices.text: The body is released only after the preliminary autopsy diagnosis is issued

choices.label: D
choices.text: The family should postpone the funeral until the 60-day report is issued

choices.label: E
choices.text: The funeral must be postponed at least one week to allow brain fixation

explanation.summary: The body is released to the funeral home following the autopsy, so an autopsy should not significantly delay funeral services in most situations.
explanation.whyCorrect: The body is released to the funeral home following the autopsy. As such, autopsy should not cause a significant delay for funeral services in most situations. Retained organs, such as the brain undergoing fixation, do not hold up release of the body; whether organs are returned to the body depends on the hospital, institution, or special request.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The final report may take weeks to months, but the body is released right after the autopsy, not after the report.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Release of the body to the funeral home is not tied to the timing of the preliminary autopsy diagnosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The report timeline is irrelevant to the funeral; the body goes to the funeral home after the autopsy itself.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The brain is fixed for at least a week, but this occurs separately and does not delay release of the body.

questions.topicName: Autopsy

questions.stem: A medical autopsy is performed on a 52-year-old woman who died of an unclear febrile illness. Two days later, the treating team receives a brief document listing the pathologist's initial impressions. Which of the following best characterizes the report they received?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The case discussion, which integrates clinical history with the pathologic findings

choices.label: B
choices.text: The death certificate, which the pathologist files with the state registrar

choices.label: C
choices.text: The final anatomic diagnosis, which is legally binding on the treating team

choices.label: D
choices.text: The final autopsy report, which must be complete within 2 days of death

choices.label: E
choices.text: The preliminary autopsy diagnosis, whose content is limited and subject to change

explanation.summary: The preliminary autopsy diagnosis (PAD) is released within 2 working days but contains limited information that may change.
explanation.whyCorrect: A preliminary report known as the preliminary autopsy diagnosis (PAD) is released within 2 working days of the autopsy date. The information available in the PAD is limited and subject to change, because microscopic examination, brain examination, and ancillary studies are not yet complete.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The case discussion is the clinicopathologic correlation in the final report, not an early preliminary document.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Death certificates are filled out by the treating clinician, not the pathologist.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The final anatomic diagnosis is a section of the final report, which comes weeks to months later, and it is not described as legally binding.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The final autopsy report takes weeks to months; national standards call for it within 90 days for complex cases.

questions.topicName: Autopsy

questions.stem: A quality officer is auditing turnaround times for a hospital autopsy service. A complex case involving multiple organ systems, extensive microscopic review, and ancillary molecular testing has been open for 10 weeks. According to national standards, within what time frame after the autopsy should the final report for a complex case be available?

explanation.summary: National standards call for final autopsy reports to be available within 90 days for complex cases.
explanation.whyCorrect: In accordance with national standards, final autopsy reports should be available within 90 days for complex cases. A case open for 10 weeks is still within this window, though the report is typically issued on the order of 30 to 60 days after the autopsy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: One week is roughly the minimum formalin fixation time for the brain, not a reporting standard.
whyWrongByChoice.B: One year far exceeds the national standard for final report availability.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Two working days is the time frame for the preliminary autopsy diagnosis, not the final report.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Six months exceeds the 90-day standard for complex cases.

questions.topicName: Autopsy

questions.stem: A pathologist writing the report for a 66-year-old man with long-standing hypertension lists left ventricular hypertrophy, hypertensive nephrosclerosis, and hypertensive retinal changes together under a single heading, then lists all findings related to his diabetes mellitus under a second heading, rather than proceeding organ by organ. This organizational approach is an alternative way of writing which section of the autopsy report?

explanation.summary: The final anatomic diagnosis is commonly organized by organ system, but may alternatively group findings along pathologic themes such as hypertension.
explanation.whyCorrect: The final anatomic diagnosis (FAD) lists diagnoses and relevant pathologic findings drawn from both gross and microscopic observations. Commonly the FAD is organized by organ system, with all heart abnormalities listed together, then all lung abnormalities, and so on. Alternative approaches include grouping findings along pathologic themes, such as grouping all findings throughout the body related to hypertension before moving to another clinical disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Additional findings cover imaging, toxicology, microbiology, molecular testing, and other laboratory results.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The clinical summary summarizes pertinent clinical information from healthcare records; it does not list pathologic diagnoses.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Gross findings record macroscopic descriptions such as organ weights and appearance, not a synthesized diagnostic list.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Microscopic findings describe histologic observations rather than thematically grouped diagnoses.

questions.topicName: Autopsy

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man with leukemia dies after chemotherapy. At autopsy, histologic sections of the lung show invasive septate hyphae within the pulmonary vessels. In which section of the standard medical autopsy report is this observation documented?

explanation.summary: The microscopic findings section describes histologic observations such as the identification of invasive fungal organisms.
explanation.whyCorrect: The microscopic findings section provides a description of the histologic findings, such as the identification of invasive fungal organisms or the light-microscopic correlates of a myocardial infarct. Hyphae seen on histologic sections of lung belong here.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Additional findings house ancillary results such as microbiology cultures, imaging, and toxicology, not histologic descriptions.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The clinical summary contains pertinent clinical information from the healthcare records, not autopsy observations.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The final anatomic diagnosis would list the resulting diagnosis (e.g., invasive fungal infection), not the raw histologic description.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Gross findings are macroscopic; hyphae are seen only under the microscope.

questions.topicName: Autopsy

questions.stem: During the autopsy of a 29-year-old woman who died unexpectedly during a hospital admission for sepsis, postmortem blood cultures are obtained, vitreous fluid is sent for chemistry, and a molecular panel for cardiac channelopathies is submitted. In which section of the autopsy report would the results of these studies be recorded?

explanation.summary: Ancillary results such as toxicology, microbiology, molecular testing, imaging, and other laboratory studies are reported under additional findings.
explanation.whyCorrect: The additional findings section of the autopsy report is where information from imaging, toxicology, microbiology, molecular testing, or other laboratory results may be included. Postmortem cultures, vitreous chemistry, and a molecular channelopathy panel are all ancillary laboratory studies that belong in this section.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The clinical summary reflects pertinent antemortem clinical information from the medical record.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Gross findings record macroscopic observations such as organ weights and appearance.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Microscopic findings describe histology, not culture, chemistry, or molecular results.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The preliminary autopsy diagnosis is an early, limited report issued within 2 working days, before most ancillary results return.

questions.topicName: Autopsy

questions.stem: A pathology resident drafts the clinicopathologic correlation for a medical autopsy and writes: 'Pt w/ hx CAD s/p CABG, EF 25%, developed AKI and MOF c/w cardiogenic shock.' The attending asks the resident to revise this section. Which of the following is the most appropriate reason for the revision?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ejection fraction cannot be cited in an autopsy report

choices.label: B
choices.text: Jargon and medical abbreviations are discouraged in this section

choices.label: C
choices.text: The cause of death must be omitted from the case discussion

choices.label: D
choices.text: The clinicopathologic correlation should contain only microscopic descriptions

choices.label: E
choices.text: The sentence should be moved to the gross findings section

explanation.summary: Use of jargon and medical abbreviations is discouraged in the clinicopathologic correlation and clinical history because families must be able to understand the report.
explanation.whyCorrect: Autopsy reports are highly detailed, technical, and contain content that can be difficult to understand, even for medical professionals. For that reason, the use of jargon and medical abbreviations is discouraged in the clinicopathologic correlation (case discussion) and the clinical history, which are the parts of the report families are most likely to read.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Pertinent clinical data such as cardiac function may be cited; the problem is the abbreviated, jargon-laden format.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The case discussion usually includes a comment pertaining to the cause and mechanism of death.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The case discussion integrates clinical and pathologic findings and gives the pathologist's opinion; microscopic descriptions belong in the microscopic findings section.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Gross findings record macroscopic observations at autopsy, not the clinical narrative.

questions.topicName: Autopsy

questions.stem: Two months after her husband's death, a widow receives the final autopsy report and notices that the cause of death listed on the death certificate she received a few days after his death differs from the pathologist's conclusion. Which of the following best explains this discrepancy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Death certificates are required to list terminal events rather than specific causes

choices.label: B
choices.text: The death certificate records only the manner of death, not the cause of death

choices.label: C
choices.text: The medical examiner overrode the hospital pathologist's stated cause of death

choices.label: D
choices.text: The pathologist filed the death certificate before the results of the autopsy were known

choices.label: E
choices.text: The treating clinician completed the death certificate before autopsy results were known

explanation.summary: In the hospital, death certificates are completed by the treating clinician within a few days of death, whereas the autopsy report comes weeks to months later, which may produce discrepancies.
explanation.whyCorrect: In a hospital setting, death certificates are usually filled out by the treating clinician (not the pathologist) within a few days of death. The autopsy report does not come out for several weeks to months later, which may result in discrepancies between the two documents when the autopsy reveals information unavailable at the time of certification.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Terminal events such as asystole are specifically excluded; the certificate should list the most immediate, specific cause of death.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A critical aspect of the death certificate is documenting the cause of death, not merely the manner.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This was a consented hospital autopsy of natural disease; the medical examiner was not involved.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The pathologist does not fill out the hospital death certificate; the treating clinician does.

questions.topicName: Autopsy

questions.stem: A 41-year-old man with human immunodeficiency virus infection diagnosed 6 years ago progressed to acquired immunodeficiency syndrome 4 years ago and died after a 2-week course of disseminated aspergillosis. The treating clinician is completing the cause-of-death section of the death certificate, which is structured as a sequence of conditions each 'due to, or as a consequence of' the next. Which condition should be entered on the first line (line a)?

explanation.summary: The death certificate lists the most immediate, specific cause of death first, followed by the events leading up to it in causal sequence.
explanation.whyCorrect: The cause-of-death statement begins with the most immediate, specific cause of death and is followed by other specific events leading up to or contributing to death. In the example of a patient who died from disseminated fungal disease, line a is disseminated aspergillosis (interval 2 weeks), due to acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (4 years), due to human immunodeficiency virus infection (6 years).

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acquired immunodeficiency syndrome is the intermediate condition on line b, with an approximate interval of 4 years.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Human immunodeficiency virus infection is the underlying condition on line c, with an interval of 6 years.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Non-specific physiologic derangements such as multiorgan failure are not included on the death certificate.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Terminal events such as respiratory arrest or asystole are excluded in favor of the specific cause of death.

questions.topicName: Autopsy

questions.stem: A 23-year-old woman dies after an intracerebral hemorrhage from a ruptured arteriovenous malformation. Her family has authorized donation of her corneas, skin, and bone through the organ donation registry and also consents to a medical autopsy to characterize the vascular malformation. Which of the following best describes the relationship between the tissue procurement and the autopsy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Consent for the autopsy automatically authorizes the tissue donation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Donation cancels the autopsy because the body has been surgically altered

choices.label: C
choices.text: Procurement is a separate surgical procedure usually performed before the autopsy

choices.label: D
choices.text: The pathologist harvests the donated tissues during the autopsy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tissue procurement is deferred until after the final autopsy report has been issued

explanation.summary: Tissue and organ procurement is a separate surgical procedure, not part of the autopsy, and is usually performed before the autopsy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Tissue and organ procurement donation is not part of the autopsy process but rather a separate surgical procedure, authorized by the family through organ donation registries. If an autopsy is requested for a person undergoing organ donation, the procurement of consented tissues such as bone, skin, corneas, and certain organs is usually performed before the autopsy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Donation is authorized separately by families contacting organ donation registries; autopsy consent does not cover it.
whyWrongByChoice.B: An autopsy can still be performed after procurement; the two are compatible and sequenced.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Procurement is a separate surgical procedure and is not performed by the pathologist as part of the autopsy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Procurement precedes the autopsy; waiting for the final report would come far too late for viable tissues.

questions.topicName: Autopsy

questions.stem: After the death of an 85-year-old retired teacher, her son tells the pathology team at the time of the autopsy that his mother always wanted her body used for cadaveric dissection by medical students, and he asks whether the hospital can pay the family and transfer her body to the medical school's anatomy laboratory. Which of the following is the most accurate response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Body donation can be substituted for the autopsy if the family prefers that arrangement

choices.label: B
choices.text: Such donations are arranged by the patient with an Anatomical Gift Program before death, and payment is prohibited

choices.label: C
choices.text: The hospital may compensate the family for the body donation at a rate set by state regulation

choices.label: D
choices.text: The organ donation registry will arrange the whole-body donation to the medical school's anatomy program

choices.label: E
choices.text: The pathologist can transfer the body directly to the medical school's anatomy laboratory once the autopsy is complete

explanation.summary: Whole-body donation for medical education is arranged by the patient with an Anatomical Gift Program prior to death, not at the time of autopsy, and state laws prohibit payment for body donations.
explanation.whyCorrect: Some patients want to donate their body for medical education, such as cadaveric dissection in medical schools. This is not done at the time of autopsy; such donations would be arranged by the patient with Anatomical Gift Programs prior to death. Of note, state laws throughout the United States prohibit payment for body donations.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Body donation is a separate arrangement made before death; it is not an alternative offered in place of an autopsy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: State laws throughout the United States prohibit payment for body donations.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Organ donation registries handle organ and tissue procurement; whole-body donation for education goes through Anatomical Gift Programs.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Body donation for education is not done at the time of autopsy and is not arranged through the pathologist.

questions.topicName: Autopsy

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man is found dead with multiple stab wounds, and the case is accepted by the medical examiner as a homicide investigation. His family objects to the autopsy on religious grounds, stating that their faith requires burial without delay and without disfigurement of the body. Which of the following is the most appropriate response by the forensic pathologist?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cancel the autopsy because religious objections take precedence in forensic cases

choices.label: B
choices.text: Delay the autopsy until a court order specifically overrides the objection

choices.label: C
choices.text: Proceed with the autopsy, communicating thoughtfully and modifying aspects where possible

choices.label: D
choices.text: Require the family to sign a consent form before the examination proceeds

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transfer the case to a hospital pathologist for a consented partial autopsy

explanation.summary: In a forensic setting, medicolegal and public health concerns may override religious or cultural objections, but the pathologist should communicate thoughtfully and may modify aspects of the autopsy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Certain cultures and religions hold beliefs that shape perceptions of autopsy; for example, some sects of Islam discourage or forbid autopsies due to delay of burial and disfigurement. In a forensic setting, however, medicolegal and public health concerns may override such objections. Thoughtful communication is necessary in these cases, and forensic pathologists may be able to modify aspects of the autopsy, such as returning organs to anatomic positions or utilizing minimally invasive approaches.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Religious objections may be overridden by medicolegal concerns in a forensic case such as a homicide.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The medical examiner already has jurisdiction; medicolegal concerns override the objection without a separate court process, and delay would compound the family's burial concern.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Medical examiner cases do not require family consent for autopsy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A homicide is a medicolegal case and cannot be converted into a family-restricted hospital autopsy.

questions.topicName: Autopsy

questions.stem: A 50-year-old man with liver cirrhosis secondary to alcohol use disorder presents for follow-up. On examination he has a large, protuberant abdomen, and he reports that his doctors told him there is fluid in his belly. Which of the following terms best describes this collection of fluid?

explanation.summary: Ascites is the accumulation of fluid within the abdominal cavity and is a classic finding in liver cirrhosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick defines an effusion as accumulation of fluid within a body cavity and names the fluid that collects in the abdominal cavity as ascites. Cirrhosis produces ascites through both portal hypertension and reduced albumin synthesis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Anasarca is severe generalized edema of subcutaneous tissue, not a cavity fluid collection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Edema is the general term for accumulation of fluid within tissues, not fluid within a body cavity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A pericardial effusion is fluid within the pericardial sac around the heart, not the abdomen.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A pleural effusion is fluid within the pleural cavity around the lungs, not the abdomen.

questions.topicName: Hemodynamics and Shock: Foundations and Frameworks

questions.stem: A 65-year-old man with a history of nephrotic syndrome presents with periorbital and lower extremity swelling. Laboratory studies show heavy proteinuria and a markedly low serum albumin. Which pathophysiologic category of edema best explains his findings?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lymphatic obstruction by tumor or fibrosis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sodium and water retention by the kidney

explanation.summary: Loss of albumin lowers plasma colloid osmotic pressure, allowing fluid to leave the vasculature and produce edema.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that albumin, which makes up about 50% of total plasma protein, is the predominant contributor to osmotic pressure. In nephrotic syndrome, protein-losing glomerulopathy causes massive urinary loss of albumin, reducing the oncotic pull that keeps fluid in the vessel.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Increased hydrostatic pressure results from disorders that impair venous return, such as heart failure or cirrhosis, not from urinary protein loss.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Increased vascular permeability is driven by inflammatory cytokines during inflammation, not by loss of plasma albumin.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Lymphatic obstruction is caused by trauma, tumors, fibrosis, or filariasis blocking lymphatic drainage, not by proteinuria.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sodium and water retention causes edema through intravascular volume expansion; the primary defect here is albumin loss lowering oncotic pressure.

questions.topicName: Hemodynamics and Shock: Foundations and Frameworks

questions.stem: A 72-year-old woman with longstanding congestive heart failure develops progressive bilateral lower extremity edema. Which of the following mechanisms is the most direct cause of her edema?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blockage of lymphatic channels by a tumor

choices.label: E
choices.text: Loss of albumin in the urine

explanation.summary: Disorders that impair venous return raise capillary hydrostatic pressure and push fluid into the interstitium.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick lists congestive heart failure among the disorders that increase hydrostatic pressure by impairing venous return. The resulting rise in capillary pressure drives fluid out of the vessel into the tissues, producing edema.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Leaky angiogenic vessels contribute to increased vascular permeability, not to hydrostatic edema from impaired venous return.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Tumor blockage of lymphatics is a lymphatic obstruction mechanism, unrelated to venous congestion from heart failure.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Inflammatory cytokines increasing permeability is the mechanism of inflammatory edema, not of heart-failure edema.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Urinary albumin loss lowers colloid osmotic pressure and is the mechanism in nephrotic syndrome, not in heart failure.

questions.topicName: Hemodynamics and Shock: Foundations and Frameworks

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man from a region where filarial disease is endemic develops massive, chronic swelling and thickening of one leg, progressing over years to elephantiasis. Which mechanism of edema best explains this presentation?

explanation.summary: Blocked lymphatic drainage of interstitial fluid produces lymphedema, which filariasis can advance to elephantiasis.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that movement of fluid from the interstitial space into lymphatic vessels can be blocked by conditions including trauma, fibrosis, invasive tumors, and filariasis from the Filarioidea roundworm, and it shows massive edema and elephantiasis of the leg as an example.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Increased hydrostatic pressure arises from impaired venous return, whereas here the lymphatic drainage is obstructed.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Increased vascular permeability is inflammatory and mediated by cytokines, not by parasitic blockage of lymphatics.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Reduced colloid osmotic pressure results from albumin loss and typically causes more generalized edema, not a filarial limb.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sodium and water retention expands intravascular volume via renal mechanisms, not via lymphatic blockage.

questions.topicName: Hemodynamics and Shock: Foundations and Frameworks

questions.stem: A 40-year-old woman undergoes thoracentesis for a pleural effusion. Analysis of the fluid shows a high protein content, high cellularity with numerous white cells, and a high specific gravity. Cultures grow bacteria. Which of the following best characterizes this fluid?

choices.label: D
choices.text: An exudate from an inflammatory process

choices.label: E
choices.text: An ultrafiltrate of plasma with low protein

explanation.summary: Protein-rich, highly cellular fluid with high specific gravity arising from infection or inflammation is an exudate.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick defines exudates as inflammatory fluid collections that arise from increases in vascular permeability caused by inflammatory mediators; they are protein-rich with higher cellularity and specific gravity, and common causes include infections such as pneumonia and tuberculosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A transudate from heart failure has low protein and low cellularity, the opposite of the described fluid.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A transudate from hypoalbuminemia is a low-protein ultrafiltrate, not a protein-rich, cellular fluid.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A transudate from renal disease is non-inflammatory with low protein and specific gravity, unlike this fluid.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A low-protein ultrafiltrate of plasma is by definition a transudate, not this protein-rich cellular fluid.

questions.topicName: Hemodynamics and Shock: Foundations and Frameworks

questions.stem: A pathologist reviews pleural fluid removed from a patient and must decide whether it is a transudate or an exudate. Which of the following findings is most compatible with a transudate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A background of underlying bacterial infection

choices.label: C
choices.text: High cellularity with abundant white cells

explanation.summary: Transudates are non-inflammatory, low-protein ultrafiltrates of plasma that occur in disorders such as heart failure.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that transudates are non-inflammatory fluid collections common in disorders such as heart failure, liver failure, renal disease, and malnutrition, and that they have low levels of protein, cellularity, and specific gravity.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An underlying bacterial infection points to an inflammatory exudate, not a transudate.
whyWrongByChoice.C: High cellularity is a feature of exudates; transudates have low cellularity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: High protein content characterizes exudates; transudates have low protein.
whyWrongByChoice.E: High specific gravity is typical of exudates; transudates have low specific gravity.

questions.topicName: Hemodynamics and Shock: Foundations and Frameworks

questions.stem: A 48-year-old man develops a blood clot in his right popliteal vein. Over the next day his right lower leg becomes swollen and takes on a dusky, blue-red discoloration. Which of the following best describes the change in blood volume in his leg?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An exudative effusion in the leg

explanation.summary: Congestion is a passive increase in blood volume from reduced venous outflow and gives tissue a cyanotic appearance.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick defines congestion as a passive process resulting from reduced venous outflow from a tissue, which can be localized as in isolated venous obstruction. Congested tissues take on a cyanotic, reddish-blue appearance from accumulation of deoxygenated hemoglobin, matching this venous clot.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An exudative effusion is an inflammatory fluid collection in a cavity, not a change in blood volume within the leg.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hyperemia from inflammation produces red erythema from oxygenated blood, not the blue-red hue of venous obstruction.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hyperemia is an active process of arteriolar dilation increasing inflow, whereas a venous clot obstructs outflow.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Increased arterial inflow from exercise describes hyperemia, the opposite mechanism of this venous outflow obstruction.

questions.topicName: Hemodynamics and Shock: Foundations and Frameworks

questions.stem: During a soccer match, a 28-year-old man exerts himself and his skin becomes flushed and red as blood flow to his muscles and skin increases. Which of the following statements about this process is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is a passive process caused by reduced venous outflow from the tissue

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is characteristically associated with systemic or local cardiac failure

choices.label: C
choices.text: It leads directly to ischemic tissue injury and fibrosis of the tissue over time

choices.label: D
choices.text: It typically produces a cyanotic, blue-red discoloration of the skin

choices.label: E
choices.text: The tissue is red because of an active increase in oxygenated arterial inflow

explanation.summary: Hyperemia is an active increase in blood volume from arteriolar dilation that turns tissue red with oxygenated blood.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick describes hyperemia as an active process in which arteriolar dilation increases blood flow, and affected tissues turn red because of an influx of oxygenated blood. It arises at sites of inflammation, during exercise, and with other stimuli.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A passive process from reduced venous outflow describes congestion, not hyperemia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Association with systemic cardiac failure describes congestion, whereas hyperemia is seen with exercise and inflammation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Chronic congestion, not hyperemia, is what can lead to ischemic tissue injury and fibrosis over time.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A cyanotic blue-red discoloration is characteristic of congestion from deoxygenated hemoglobin.

questions.topicName: Hemodynamics and Shock: Foundations and Frameworks

questions.stem: A 25-year-old hiker is attacked by a mountain lion and sustains large, bleeding wounds to her arms and legs. In the emergency department her skin is cool and clammy, her heart rate is 140/min, and her blood pressure is 100/60 mmHg. Which type of shock is she most likely experiencing?

explanation.summary: Massive hemorrhage lowers blood volume and cardiac output, producing hypovolemic shock.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that hypovolemic shock results from low cardiac output due to low blood volume, as in massive hemorrhage or fluid loss from severe burns. Her bleeding wounds, weak rapid pulse, and cool clammy skin fit this picture.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Anaphylactic shock is an IgE-mediated hypersensitivity reaction to an allergen, not a response to blood loss.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cardiogenic shock results from heart pump failure such as myocardial infarction, not from hemorrhage.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Neurogenic shock follows spinal cord injury with acute vasodilation, which is not described here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Septic shock results from systemic inflammation due to infection and often produces warm, flushed skin, unlike her cool clammy skin.

questions.topicName: Hemodynamics and Shock: Foundations and Frameworks

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man is admitted with a large anterior myocardial infarction. Despite normal blood volume, his blood pressure falls to 80/50 mmHg, his pulse is weak and rapid, and his skin is cool and clammy. Which type of shock best explains his presentation?

explanation.summary: Cardiogenic shock results from low cardiac output due to failure of the heart as a pump.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick defines cardiogenic shock as resulting from low cardiac output due to heart pump failure, giving myocardial infarction and arrhythmias as examples. Because volume is adequate but the infarcted heart cannot pump, he develops hypotension with a weak pulse and cool clammy skin.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Anaphylactic shock is an IgE-mediated allergic reaction, not a consequence of a myocardial infarction.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hypovolemic shock is caused by low blood volume from hemorrhage or burns, but his volume is normal.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Neurogenic shock follows spinal cord injury with vasodilation, which is not present here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Septic shock arises from systemic inflammation due to infection and tends to cause warm, flushed skin.

questions.topicName: Hemodynamics and Shock: Foundations and Frameworks

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man with severe necrotizing pancreatitis becomes hypotensive. Unlike a patient in hemorrhagic shock, his skin is warm and flushed rather than cool and clammy. Which type of shock and mechanism best account for these findings?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neurogenic shock from spinal cord injury

explanation.summary: Septic shock arises from systemic inflammation and often produces warm, flushed skin from peripheral vasodilation.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that septic shock results from states of systemic inflammation, including pancreatitis, and its clinical correlation notes that patients with septic shock may have warm and flushed skin due to peripheral vasodilation, in contrast to the cool skin of hypovolemic or cardiogenic shock.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Anaphylactic shock is an IgE-mediated reaction to an allergen, not a response to systemic inflammation from pancreatitis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cardiogenic shock is due to pump failure and, like hypovolemic shock, presents with cool clammy skin.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hypovolemic shock from fluid loss causes cool clammy skin, not the warm flushed skin described.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Neurogenic shock follows spinal cord injury, which this patient with pancreatitis does not have.

questions.topicName: Hemodynamics and Shock: Foundations and Frameworks

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man is stung by a bee and within minutes develops diffuse hives, wheezing, and a blood pressure of 75/40 mmHg from widespread vasodilation. Which type of shock is he experiencing?

explanation.summary: Anaphylactic shock is an IgE-mediated hypersensitivity reaction to an allergen causing acute vasodilation and hypotension.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick defines anaphylactic shock as an IgE-mediated hypersensitivity reaction to an allergen in which acute vasodilation leads to hypotension and tissue hypoperfusion. A bee sting triggering hives, wheezing, and profound hypotension is the classic example.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Cardiogenic shock arises from heart pump failure, which is not the mechanism in an allergic reaction.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hypovolemic shock is due to loss of blood volume, whereas this patient's volume is intact and vessels are dilated.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Neurogenic shock is caused by spinal cord injury, not by an allergic reaction to a sting.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Septic shock results from systemic inflammation due to infection, not from an IgE-mediated allergen response.

questions.topicName: Hemodynamics and Shock: Foundations and Frameworks

questions.stem: A physiology instructor describes the opposing Starling forces acting across a capillary wall. Which of the following forces tends to pull fluid from the interstitium back into the blood vessel?

explanation.summary: Hydrostatic pressure pushes fluid out of the vessel, while plasma colloid osmotic pressure pulls fluid into it.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick describes the body's fluid distribution as governed by a balance of opposing Starling forces: hydrostatic pressure, which tends to push fluid out of the blood vessel, and plasma colloid osmotic pressure, which tends to pull fluid into the vessel. Plasma proteins, chiefly albumin, generate this inward osmotic pull.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Arteriolar dilation increases blood flow into a tissue in hyperemia; it is not a Starling force that draws fluid into the capillary.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Capillary hydrostatic pressure is the force that pushes fluid out of the vessel, the opposite direction.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Increased interstitial fluid pressure is shown in Figure 1 as a consequence of fluid leaving the vessel, not the force that returns it to the blood.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lymphatics drain the small net excess of interstitial fluid, but this is not the osmotic force that pulls fluid into the capillary.

questions.topicName: Hemodynamics and Shock: Foundations and Frameworks

questions.stem: Under normal conditions there is a small net movement of fluid out of capillaries into the interstitial space. Which of the following best describes the normal fate of this fluid?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It accumulates gradually in the tissues as physiologic dependent edema

choices.label: B
choices.text: It collects within the pleural and pericardial cavities as a normal effusion

choices.label: C
choices.text: It drains into lymphatic vessels and returns to the bloodstream via the thoracic duct

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is excreted by the kidney as part of normal sodium and water balance

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is reabsorbed at the arterial end of the same capillary bed by plasma oncotic pressure

explanation.summary: The small net efflux of interstitial fluid normally drains into lymphatics and ultimately returns to the bloodstream.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that there is usually a small net movement of fluid into the interstitial space, but this typically drains into the lymphatic vessels and ultimately returns to the bloodstream. Figure 1 shows the lymphatics carrying this fluid to the thoracic duct and eventually to the left subclavian vein.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Under normal conditions edema does not accumulate, because lymphatic drainage removes the excess.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fluid within body cavities is an effusion, which is abnormal, not the normal route of interstitial fluid return.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The kidney regulates sodium and water, but interstitial fluid returns to the circulation through lymphatics, not by direct renal excretion.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The arterial end is where hydrostatic pressure pushes fluid out; the fluid is not reabsorbed there.

questions.topicName: Hemodynamics and Shock: Foundations and Frameworks

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman with systemic lupus erythematosus develops chest discomfort. Echocardiography shows fluid accumulated within the sac surrounding her heart. Which of the following terms best describes this finding?

explanation.summary: An effusion is fluid within a body cavity, and fluid within the pericardial sac is a pericardial effusion.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick defines an effusion as accumulation of fluid within a body cavity and lists the named effusions by location: pleural cavity is a pleural effusion, pericardial sac is a pericardial effusion, and abdominal cavity is ascites.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ascites is fluid within the abdominal cavity, not around the heart.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Anasarca is generalized edema of the tissues, not a fluid collection in a body cavity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lymphedema is tissue edema resulting from lymphatic obstruction, not fluid within a cavity.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A pleural effusion is fluid within the pleural cavity around the lungs, not the pericardial sac.

questions.topicName: Hemodynamics and Shock: Foundations and Frameworks

questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman with an invasive pelvic tumor develops progressive, persistent swelling of her left leg. Imaging shows the tumor encasing the lymphatic vessels draining that limb. Which of the following terms best describes her leg swelling?

explanation.summary: Edema resulting from blocked lymphatic drainage is termed lymphedema.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick lists lymphedema among the clinical manifestations of edema and explains that movement of fluid from the interstitial space into lymphatic vessels can be blocked by conditions including trauma, fibrosis, invasive tumors, and filariasis. A tumor encasing the lymphatics of one limb produces lymphedema of that limb.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Anasarca is generalized edema, whereas this swelling is confined to one leg.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Congestion is a passive increase in blood volume from reduced venous outflow; here the lymphatic vessels, not veins, are obstructed.
whyWrongByChoice.C: An effusion is fluid within a body cavity, not swelling of the tissues of a limb.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hyperemia is an active increase in blood volume from arteriolar dilation, not tissue fluid accumulation from blocked lymphatics.

questions.topicName: Hemodynamics and Shock: Foundations and Frameworks

questions.stem: A 62-year-old man with a history of tuberculosis develops a thickened, rigid pericardium that prevents the heart from filling normally. He presents with widespread edema. Which pathophysiologic category of edema best explains his findings?

explanation.summary: Constrictive pericarditis impairs venous return and raises hydrostatic pressure, producing widespread edema.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that increases in hydrostatic pressure are predominantly due to disorders that impair venous return and lists constrictive pericarditis alongside congestive heart failure and liver cirrhosis as examples. Its clinical correlation notes that these disorders cause a more systemic increase in venous pressure and lead to more widespread edema.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Leaky angiogenic vessels are a cause of increased vascular permeability, unrelated to pericardial constriction.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Increased vascular permeability is driven by inflammatory cytokines acting on vessel walls, not by impaired cardiac filling.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lymphatic obstruction is caused by trauma, fibrosis, tumors, or filariasis blocking lymphatic drainage, not by a rigid pericardium.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Reduced colloid osmotic pressure results from albumin loss, as in cirrhosis, nephrotic syndrome, or protein-losing enteropathies.

questions.topicName: Hemodynamics and Shock: Foundations and Frameworks

questions.stem: A 50-year-old man with alcoholic cirrhosis asks why fluid has collected in his abdomen. His physician explains that scar tissue in the liver makes it hard for blood to flow through, so blood backs up in his bloodstream and pushes fluid out of his vessels. Which pathophysiologic mechanism of edema is the physician describing?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increased hydrostatic pressure from obstruction of the portal vein

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increased vascular permeability from inflammatory cytokines in the liver

choices.label: C
choices.text: Obstruction of hepatic lymphatics by dense fibrous scar

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reduced synthesis of albumin by the diseased, scarred liver

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sodium retention from renal hypoperfusion in cirrhosis

explanation.summary: Cirrhosis obstructs the portal vein, impairing venous return and raising hydrostatic pressure.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick lists liver cirrhosis among the disorders that increase hydrostatic pressure because it obstructs the portal vein. In the case connection, the explanation that blood does not flow easily through the scar and backs up, pushing more fluid out of the vessels, describes this hydrostatic mechanism.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Increased vascular permeability occurs during inflammation, not from scarring that obstructs hepatic blood flow.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The brick describes cirrhosis as obstructing the portal vein, a blood vessel, not the lymphatic vessels.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Reduced albumin synthesis is the other contributor in cirrhosis, but it lowers colloid osmotic pressure rather than causing blood to back up and push fluid out.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sodium retention from renal hypoperfusion is described in the setting of kidney dysfunction or heart failure, not as the mechanism of blood backing up behind hepatic scar.

questions.topicName: Hemodynamics and Shock: Foundations and Frameworks

questions.stem: Two patients present with edema from increased hydrostatic pressure. Patient 1 has a deep venous thrombosis of the left leg; Patient 2 has congestive heart failure. Which of the following best describes the expected difference in the distribution of their edema?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Both patients develop edema confined to the lower extremities only

choices.label: B
choices.text: Both patients develop the same widespread edema pattern

choices.label: C
choices.text: Patient 1 has edema confined to the left leg; Patient 2 has more widespread edema

choices.label: D
choices.text: Patient 1 has generalized anasarca; Patient 2 has edema of one leg

choices.label: E
choices.text: Patient 1 has pleural effusions; Patient 2 has no edema of the extremities

explanation.summary: Localized venous impairment produces edema confined to that body part, whereas systemic venous pressure increases cause widespread edema.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick's clinical correlation states that if the impairment is localized, such as a DVT in the leg, the resultant edema is usually confined to that body part, while disorders such as congestive heart failure cause a more systemic increase in venous pressure and lead to more widespread edema.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Heart failure raises venous pressure systemically and produces more widespread edema, not edema confined to the legs.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The distribution differs because one impairment is localized and the other is systemic.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This reverses the pattern; the localized DVT produces localized edema and heart failure produces widespread edema.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A DVT produces localized limb edema, not pleural effusions, and heart failure does cause extremity edema.

questions.topicName: Hemodynamics and Shock: Foundations and Frameworks

questions.stem: A student is asked why albumin, rather than other plasma proteins, is the main determinant of plasma colloid osmotic pressure. Which of the following statements best supports the answer?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Albumin actively transports sodium out of the interstitium

choices.label: B
choices.text: Albumin is released by inflammatory cells during inflammation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Albumin is synthesized by the kidney in response to hypoperfusion

choices.label: D
choices.text: Albumin is the only plasma protein that cannot cross the capillary wall

choices.label: E
choices.text: Albumin makes up almost 50% of total plasma protein

explanation.summary: Albumin is the predominant plasma protein contributing to osmotic pressure because it constitutes almost half of total plasma protein.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that the predominant plasma protein contributing to osmotic pressure is albumin, which makes up almost 50% of total plasma protein; therefore conditions in which there is a loss of albumin cause a reduced osmotic pressure.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Albumin exerts an osmotic pull on fluid; it does not actively transport sodium.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Albumin is not an inflammatory product; inflammatory cytokines act on vessel walls to increase permeability.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The brick attributes albumin production to the liver, not the kidney; severe liver disease reduces albumin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The brick does not claim albumin is uniquely unable to cross the capillary wall; its importance is its large share of plasma protein.

questions.topicName: Hemodynamics and Shock: Foundations and Frameworks

questions.stem: A 70-year-old woman with chronic kidney disease retains sodium and develops progressive edema. Which of the following best describes how sodium retention alters the Starling forces to produce her edema?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increases vascular permeability by cytokine release

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lowers colloid osmotic pressure only, with hydrostatic pressure unchanged

choices.label: C
choices.text: Raises colloid osmotic pressure and lowers hydrostatic pressure

choices.label: D
choices.text: Raises hydrostatic pressure and lowers colloid osmotic pressure

choices.label: E
choices.text: Raises hydrostatic pressure only, with colloid osmotic pressure unchanged

explanation.summary: Sodium retention expands intravascular volume, increasing hydrostatic pressure, and dilutes plasma proteins, diminishing osmotic pressure.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick explains that sodium retention leads to water retention because water follows sodium. This leads to an increased hydrostatic pressure due to intravascular fluid volume expansion and a diminished osmotic pressure due to dilution, and it mainly occurs when kidney function is compromised.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Increased vascular permeability is the mechanism of inflammatory edema, not of sodium and water retention.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Intravascular volume expansion also raises hydrostatic pressure, so it is not unchanged.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Both directions are reversed; volume expansion raises hydrostatic pressure and dilution lowers osmotic pressure.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sodium and water retention also dilutes plasma proteins, so colloid osmotic pressure falls rather than staying unchanged.

questions.topicName: Hemodynamics and Shock: Foundations and Frameworks

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man with severe heart failure has worsening edema despite no primary kidney disease. His physician notes that his failing heart is causing the kidneys to retain sodium. Which of the following best explains why heart failure produces sodium and water retention?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Inflammatory cytokines acting on the glomerulus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Loss of albumin into the urine

choices.label: C
choices.text: Obstruction of lymphatic drainage from the kidney

choices.label: D
choices.text: Portal vein obstruction reducing hepatic clearance

choices.label: E
choices.text: Renal hypoperfusion from low cardiac output

explanation.summary: Heart failure causes renal hypoperfusion, which triggers sodium retention and water retention.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that sodium and water retention mainly occurs when kidney function is compromised, either due to a primary kidney disorder or a cardiovascular disorder such as heart failure that causes renal hypoperfusion. Because water follows sodium, this expands intravascular volume and promotes edema.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Inflammatory cytokines increase vascular permeability in inflammation; they are not the link between heart failure and sodium retention.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Urinary albumin loss is the mechanism of nephrotic syndrome, lowering colloid osmotic pressure rather than causing sodium retention.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Lymphatic obstruction causes lymphedema in the drained tissue; it is not how heart failure affects the kidney.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Portal vein obstruction is the mechanism by which cirrhosis raises hydrostatic pressure, not a consequence of heart failure acting on the kidney.

questions.topicName: Hemodynamics and Shock: Foundations and Frameworks

questions.stem: A 35-year-old man develops a red, hot, swollen area of skin around an infected cut on his forearm. The swelling results from fluid leaving the vessels into the surrounding tissue. Which of the following best explains the increased fluid efflux at this site?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blockage of the lymphatic channels of the forearm by fibrosis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Inflammatory cytokines increasing vessel wall permeability

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reduced synthesis of albumin by the diseased liver

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reduced venous outflow from the veins of the forearm

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sodium and water retention from renal hypoperfusion

explanation.summary: During inflammation, cytokines act on vessel walls to increase permeability and allow more fluid efflux into the interstitium.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that during times of inflammation, the effect of inflammatory cytokines on vessel walls causes them to have increased permeability and allow more efflux of fluid into the interstitium. Localized inflammatory edema around an infected wound is produced by this mechanism.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Lymphatic blockage by fibrosis causes lymphedema, not the acute inflammatory swelling around an infected cut.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Reduced albumin synthesis lowers colloid osmotic pressure systemically and would not explain localized swelling at an infected site.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Reduced venous outflow describes congestion and hydrostatic edema, not the cytokine-driven leak of inflammation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sodium retention produces generalized edema when kidney function is compromised, not a localized inflammatory reaction.

questions.topicName: Hemodynamics and Shock: Foundations and Frameworks

questions.stem: A researcher studies newly formed blood vessels growing into a healing wound and notes that they leak considerably more fluid than mature vessels. Which of the following best explains this increased permeability?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Absence of lymphatic channels in the new tissue

choices.label: B
choices.text: Accumulation of deoxygenated hemoglobin in the vessels

choices.label: C
choices.text: Deposition of albumin within the new vessel walls

choices.label: D
choices.text: High hydrostatic pressure from arteriolar dilation in the wound

choices.label: E
choices.text: Incomplete interendothelial junctions and the action of VEGF

explanation.summary: Angiogenic vessels are leakier than mature vessels because of incomplete interendothelial junctions and VEGF.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that new vessels formed in a process known as angiogenesis are leakier than mature vessels due to incomplete interendothelial junctions and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) causing more vascular permeability.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The brick attributes the leak to the vessels themselves, not to a lack of lymphatic drainage.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Accumulation of deoxygenated hemoglobin is what gives congested tissue a cyanotic appearance; it does not increase permeability.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Albumin is a plasma protein that maintains colloid osmotic pressure; it does not deposit in vessel walls to cause leak.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Arteriolar dilation produces hyperemia; the brick attributes the leakiness of new vessels to their junctions and VEGF, not to hydrostatic pressure.

questions.topicName: Hemodynamics and Shock: Foundations and Frameworks

questions.stem: A 75-year-old woman with congestive heart failure develops fluid accumulation in her lungs. Over the next several days she becomes hypoxemic and then develops fever and a productive cough. Which of the following best explains the sequence of her complications?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Pulmonary edema causes herniation of tissue that compresses respiratory centers

choices.label: B
choices.text: Pulmonary edema converts a transudate into an exudate by protein loss

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pulmonary edema impairs gas exchange and provides a fertile ground for infection

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pulmonary edema impairs venous return and raises hydrostatic pressure

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pulmonary edema triggers angiogenesis and leaky new vessels

explanation.summary: Pulmonary edema impairs gas exchange, leading to hypoxemia, and creates a fertile ground for pneumonia.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick's clinical correlation states that pulmonary edema impairs gas exchange, leading to hypoxemia, and provides a fertile ground for infection (pneumonia). Her hypoxemia followed by fever and productive cough reflects both consequences.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Herniation compressing brainstem centers is the consequence of brain edema within the limited space of the skull, not of pulmonary edema.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The brick does not describe edema fluid converting from transudate to exudate by protein loss; its consequences are hypoxemia and infection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Impaired venous return is a cause of edema, not the consequence of pulmonary edema described here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Angiogenesis with leaky vessels is a mechanism of increased permeability, not a stated consequence of pulmonary edema.

questions.topicName: Hemodynamics and Shock: Foundations and Frameworks

questions.stem: A 22-year-old man sustains severe head trauma and develops massive cerebral edema. His physicians warn that this edema is immediately life threatening. Which of the following best explains why brain edema is so dangerous?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It impairs alveolar gas exchange and causes life-threatening hypoxemia

choices.label: B
choices.text: It indicates an underlying cardiac or renal dysfunction requiring urgent treatment

choices.label: C
choices.text: It provides a fertile ground for bacterial infection and abscess formation

choices.label: D
choices.text: It reduces the plasma albumin concentration and lowers colloid osmotic pressure

choices.label: E
choices.text: The rigid skull forces brain tissue to herniate and compress brainstem centers

explanation.summary: Because the skull is a limited space, brain edema can cause herniation through the foramen magnum and compress brainstem cardiac and respiratory centers.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that edema in the brain is life threatening because the skull is a limited physical space; severe brain edema can cause herniation of brain tissue through spaces like the foramen magnum, which can press on centers in the brainstem that control cardiac and respiratory function.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Impaired gas exchange and hypoxemia are consequences of pulmonary edema, not brain edema.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Being a sign of cardiac or renal dysfunction describes subcutaneous edema, which the brick notes is not immediately life-threatening.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A fertile ground for infection describes the risk of pneumonia with pulmonary edema.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Brain edema does not lower plasma albumin; reduced colloid osmotic pressure is a cause of edema, not a result of brain swelling.

questions.topicName: Hemodynamics and Shock: Foundations and Frameworks

questions.stem: A 66-year-old man presents with new bilateral pitting swelling of his ankles and shins. He has no pain, redness, or shortness of breath. Which of the following best describes the clinical significance of this subcutaneous edema?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It confirms an inflammatory exudate in the soft tissue and therefore signals an underlying cellulitis or abscess

choices.label: B
choices.text: It indicates an active IgE-mediated hypersensitivity reaction that requires urgent epinephrine administration

choices.label: C
choices.text: It indicates that pulmonary gas exchange is impaired and that respiratory failure is imminent

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is immediately life-threatening because the swelling can cause herniation of soft tissue through fascial planes

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is not immediately life-threatening but may signal underlying cardiac or renal dysfunction

explanation.summary: Subcutaneous edema is not immediately life-threatening but may be a sign of underlying cardiac or renal disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick's clinical correlation states that clinical consequences of edema depend on its extent and location, and that subcutaneous edema, though not immediately life-threatening, may be a sign of underlying cardiac or renal dysfunction.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Without pain, redness, or infection there is no basis to call this an inflammatory exudate; it is far more consistent with non-inflammatory edema.
whyWrongByChoice.B: An IgE-mediated hypersensitivity reaction describes anaphylactic shock; painless bilateral ankle edema does not indicate this.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Impaired gas exchange is a consequence of pulmonary edema, not subcutaneous edema.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Herniation is the life-threatening consequence of brain edema within the rigid skull, not of subcutaneous edema.

questions.topicName: Hemodynamics and Shock: Foundations and Frameworks

questions.stem: A 55-year-old woman with long-standing rheumatoid arthritis develops a pleural effusion. No infection is identified. Which of the following best characterizes the fluid that would be expected on thoracentesis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A transudate, because rheumatoid arthritis impairs venous return

choices.label: B
choices.text: A transudate, because the effusion is not caused by infection

choices.label: C
choices.text: An exudate, because rheumatoid arthritis causes albumin loss

choices.label: D
choices.text: An exudate, because rheumatoid arthritis is an inflammatory disorder

choices.label: E
choices.text: An ultrafiltrate of plasma with low specific gravity

explanation.summary: Inflammatory disorders such as lupus and rheumatoid arthritis produce exudative effusions.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick lists the common disorders associated with exudates as infections (pneumonia, tuberculosis), inflammatory disorders (lupus, rheumatoid arthritis), and malignancy. Exudates arise from increased vascular permeability caused by inflammatory mediators and are protein-rich with higher cellularity and specific gravity.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Rheumatoid arthritis is an inflammatory disorder, not a cause of impaired venous return, so it does not produce a transudate.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Infection is only one cause of exudates; inflammatory disorders and malignancy also produce exudates without infection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Albumin loss produces transudates by lowering colloid osmotic pressure; exudates form from inflammatory vascular permeability, not albumin loss.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A plasma ultrafiltrate with low specific gravity describes a transudate, which occurs with heart failure, liver failure, renal disease, and malnutrition.

questions.topicName: Hemodynamics and Shock: Foundations and Frameworks

questions.stem: A diagram compares a normal capillary with vessels in exudative and transudative states. In the exudate panel, the vessel shows vasodilation and stasis with leakage of both fluid and protein. Which of the following vessel changes accounts for the protein leakage in an exudate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blockage of lymphatic uptake of interstitial protein

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decreased colloid osmotic pressure from reduced protein synthesis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Dilution of plasma proteins by sodium and water retention

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased hydrostatic pressure from venous outflow obstruction

choices.label: E
choices.text: Increased interendothelial spaces caused by inflammation

explanation.summary: Exudates form when inflammation widens interendothelial spaces, allowing fluid and protein to leak out.
explanation.whyCorrect: Figure 3 in the brick labels the exudate panel with vasodilation and stasis and increased interendothelial spaces, both bracketed as effects of inflammation, resulting in fluid and protein leakage. This is why exudates have a high protein content and may contain white and red cells.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Lymphatic obstruction causes lymphedema; the figure attributes exudate formation to changes in the vessel wall itself.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Decreased colloid osmotic pressure from decreased protein synthesis, as in liver disease, is a transudate mechanism.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Dilution of plasma proteins by sodium and water retention lowers osmotic pressure and favors transudate, not protein-rich exudate.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Increased hydrostatic pressure from venous outflow obstruction, such as congestive heart failure, is shown in the transudate panel and produces low-protein fluid.

questions.topicName: Hemodynamics and Shock: Foundations and Frameworks

questions.stem: A 4-year-old child with severe protein-calorie malnutrition develops generalized edema and abdominal fluid. Aspiration of the abdominal fluid is most likely to show which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bacteria consistent with an infectious exudate

choices.label: B
choices.text: High protein content with numerous white cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: High specific gravity from inflammatory mediators

choices.label: D
choices.text: Low protein and low cellularity consistent with a transudate

choices.label: E
choices.text: Protein-rich fluid from increased vascular permeability

explanation.summary: Malnutrition produces non-inflammatory transudates that are ultrafiltrates of plasma with low protein and cellularity.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick lists malnutrition together with heart failure, liver failure, and renal disease as disorders in which transudates are common. Transudates are non-inflammatory, essentially ultrafiltrates of plasma with low levels of protein, cellularity, and specific gravity; in malnutrition the underlying driver is reduced plasma protein lowering colloid osmotic pressure.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bacteria indicate an infectious exudate such as from pneumonia or tuberculosis, which is not the process in uncomplicated malnutrition.
whyWrongByChoice.B: High protein content with many white cells characterizes an exudate from infection or inflammation, not malnutrition.
whyWrongByChoice.C: High specific gravity is a feature of exudates, whereas transudates have low specific gravity.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Increased vascular permeability from inflammatory mediators produces exudates; malnutrition causes a non-inflammatory transudate.

questions.topicName: Hemodynamics and Shock: Foundations and Frameworks

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man with long-standing congestive heart failure has had passive congestion of his liver for many years. Which of the following is the most likely long-term consequence of this chronic congestion?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased oxygenated blood flow to the liver

explanation.summary: Over time, chronic congestion can lead to ischemic tissue injury and fibrosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that chronic congestion, a passive process from reduced venous outflow, can over time lead to ischemic tissue injury and fibrosis. It cites chronic pulmonary and hepatic congestion secondary to congestive heart failure as examples of congestion.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Arteriolar dilation producing erythema is hyperemia, an active process, not a consequence of passive congestion.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A protein-rich exudate results from inflammatory vascular permeability, not from chronic venous congestion.
whyWrongByChoice.C: IgE-mediated hypersensitivity is the mechanism of anaphylactic shock and is unrelated to congestion.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Congested tissue accumulates deoxygenated hemoglobin from reduced outflow; it does not receive increased oxygenated inflow.

questions.topicName: Hemodynamics and Shock: Foundations and Frameworks

questions.stem: A 74-year-old woman with cardiac failure is found to have both chronic pulmonary congestion and chronic hepatic congestion. Which of the following best explains why multiple organs are congested in this patient?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cardiac failure blocks lymphatic drainage from the lungs and liver

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cardiac failure causes localized congestion from isolated venous obstruction

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cardiac failure causes systemic congestion from reduced venous outflow

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cardiac failure produces exudates in the lungs and liver

choices.label: E
choices.text: Cardiac failure triggers hyperemia from arteriolar dilation in each organ

explanation.summary: Congestion can be systemic, as in cardiac failure, or localized, as in isolated venous obstruction.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick describes congestion as a passive process resulting from reduced venous outflow and states that it can be systemic, as in cardiac failure, or localized, as in isolated venous obstruction. The summary gives chronic pulmonary and hepatic congestion secondary to congestive heart failure as examples of systemic congestion.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Lymphatic obstruction is caused by trauma, fibrosis, tumors, or filariasis; cardiac failure congests organs by reducing venous outflow.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Localized congestion from isolated venous obstruction affects one region, such as a leg with a popliteal clot, not multiple organs.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cardiac failure produces non-inflammatory transudates, and congestion refers to increased blood volume, not fluid collections.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Hyperemia is an active process from arteriolar dilation seen with exercise, blushing, and inflammation, not with cardiac failure.

questions.topicName: Hemodynamics and Shock: Foundations and Frameworks

questions.stem: A medical student is asked to define shock in physiologic terms. Which of the following best captures the definition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A passive increase in the volume of blood within a tissue resulting from reduced venous outflow

choices.label: B
choices.text: A state of circulatory failure with inability to supply blood and oxygen to organs and tissues

choices.label: C
choices.text: Accumulation of fluid within a body cavity caused by increased vascular permeability

choices.label: D
choices.text: An active increase in blood volume within the tissues from arteriolar dilation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Loss of plasma albumin leading to a reduction in colloid osmotic pressure

explanation.summary: Shock is a state of circulatory failure in which blood and oxygen cannot be supplied to organs and tissues.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick defines shock as a state of circulatory failure in which there is an inability to supply blood and oxygen to organs and tissues, and notes that the cellular injury may become irreversible and even fatal if the process is prolonged.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A passive increase in tissue blood volume from reduced venous outflow is congestion.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fluid accumulation within a body cavity is an effusion, not shock.
whyWrongByChoice.D: An active increase in tissue blood volume from arteriolar dilation is hyperemia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Loss of albumin lowering colloid osmotic pressure is a mechanism of edema, not the definition of shock.

questions.topicName: Hemodynamics and Shock: Foundations and Frameworks

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after a diving accident with a cervical spinal cord injury. He is hypotensive with evidence of tissue hypoperfusion, but he has no bleeding, no signs of infection, and no history of allergen exposure. Which of the following best explains his hypotension?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acute vasodilation resulting from spinal cord injury

choices.label: B
choices.text: IgE-mediated release of mediators causing vasodilation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Low cardiac output from heart pump failure

choices.label: D
choices.text: Low cardiac output from reduced blood volume

explanation.summary: Neurogenic shock results from spinal cord injury, in which acute vasodilation leads to hypotension and tissue hypoperfusion.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick defines neurogenic shock as resulting from spinal cord injury, where acute vasodilation leads to hypotension and tissue hypoperfusion. A cervical cord injury with hypotension in the absence of hemorrhage, infection, or allergen fits this type.

whyWrongByChoice.B: IgE-mediated vasodilation is the mechanism of anaphylactic shock, which requires exposure to an allergen.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Heart pump failure causes cardiogenic shock, as in myocardial infarction or arrhythmias, which are not present here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Reduced blood volume causes hypovolemic shock from massive hemorrhage or burns, but he has no bleeding.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Systemic inflammation from overwhelming infection causes septic shock, but there are no signs of infection.

questions.topicName: Hemodynamics and Shock: Foundations and Frameworks

questions.stem: A 21-year-old woman develops high fever, a diffuse rash, and profound hypotension; she is diagnosed with toxic shock syndrome. Under which category of shock does her condition fall?

explanation.summary: Toxic shock syndrome is one of the states of systemic inflammation that produce septic shock.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that septic shock results from states of systemic inflammation and specifically lists overwhelming bacterial or fungal infections, toxic shock syndrome, burns, and pancreatitis as examples.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Anaphylactic shock is an IgE-mediated hypersensitivity reaction to an allergen, not a systemic inflammatory state from infection.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cardiogenic shock results from heart pump failure such as myocardial infarction or arrhythmias.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hypovolemic shock results from low blood volume such as massive hemorrhage or fluid loss from severe burns, not from systemic inflammation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Neurogenic shock results from spinal cord injury causing acute vasodilation.

questions.topicName: Hemodynamics and Shock: Foundations and Frameworks

questions.stem: Two patients are in shock. One was stung by a wasp and developed an IgE-mediated reaction; the other suffered a thoracic spinal cord transection. Both are hypotensive with tissue hypoperfusion. Which of the following mechanisms is shared by both patients' shock states?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Low cardiac output from heart pump failure

choices.label: C
choices.text: Low cardiac output from reduced blood volume

choices.label: D
choices.text: Peripheral vasodilation causing warm, flushed skin from sepsis

explanation.summary: Both neurogenic and anaphylactic shock produce hypotension and tissue hypoperfusion through acute vasodilation.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick describes neurogenic shock as resulting from spinal cord injury in which acute vasodilation leads to hypotension and tissue hypoperfusion, and anaphylactic shock as an IgE-mediated hypersensitivity reaction to an allergen in which acute vasodilation likewise leads to hypotension and tissue hypoperfusion. The triggers differ, but the vasodilatory mechanism is shared.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Heart pump failure is the mechanism of cardiogenic shock, not of neurogenic or anaphylactic shock.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Reduced blood volume is the mechanism of hypovolemic shock from hemorrhage or burns; neither patient has lost volume.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Warm, flushed skin from peripheral vasodilation is described for septic shock; neither patient has sepsis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Systemic inflammation from overwhelming infection is the mechanism of septic shock, which neither patient has.

questions.topicName: Hemodynamics and Shock: Foundations and Frameworks

questions.stem: A 62-year-old man with severe gram-negative sepsis develops oozing of blood from his gums and around his intravenous catheter sites. At the same time, the tips of several fingers become cold and dusky blue. Laboratory studies show thrombocytopenia and prolonged clotting times.
