whyWrongByChoice.C: Sterile collection via catheter is a method for urine.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Bronchoscopy is a method for collecting sputum.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Clinical Pathology for Patient Care

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman undergoes a procedure in which her blood is passed through a machine that removes one specific component and then returns the remainder of the blood to her body. This procedure is best described as which of the following, and it is overseen by which laboratory section?

choices.label: D
choices.text: HLA typing; Immunology and Serology Laboratory

explanation.summary: Apheresis, a process in which a machine removes a component of the blood and returns the rest to the body, is a function of the transfusion medicine laboratory.
explanation.whyCorrect: The transfusion medicine laboratory is concerned with all aspects of blood transfusion, cellular therapies, and apheresis. Apheresis is defined as a process in which a machine removes a component of the blood and then returns the rest to the body.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Centrifugation spins a collected tube to separate plasma from cells; it does not return blood to the patient.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Disk diffusion is an antimicrobial susceptibility test performed on a culture plate.
whyWrongByChoice.D: HLA typing is a compatibility test for transplantation, not a procedure that removes a blood component.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Venipuncture is simply drawing blood from a vein with a needle; nothing is returned to the patient.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Clinical Pathology for Patient Care

questions.stem: Before a transfusion, the blood bank runs a test on a 29-year-old woman's specimen specifically to determine whether she is positive or negative for a particular red cell antigen, separate from confirming whether she is group A, B, AB, or O. Which of the following tests is being described?

explanation.summary: Rh typing confirms whether a patient is Rh positive or Rh negative.
explanation.whyCorrect: The most common tests in the transfusion medicine laboratory include blood typing (confirming type A, B, AB, or O), Rh typing (confirming if the patient is Rh positive or negative), screening for unexpected red blood cell antibodies, and screening for current or past infections. Determining positive versus negative status distinct from ABO group is Rh typing.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Antibody screening looks for unexpected red blood cell antibodies, not an antigen positive/negative status.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Blood typing confirms the ABO group (A, B, AB, or O), which the stem explicitly sets apart from this test.
whyWrongByChoice.C: HLA typing is performed by immunology and serology for transplantation compatibility.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Infection screening detects current or past infections, not red cell antigen status.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Clinical Pathology for Patient Care

questions.stem: A 47-year-old woman who received multiple transfusions years ago is scheduled for surgery. Her blood is tested for the presence of unexpected antibodies directed against red blood cells so that compatible units can be selected. Which section of the clinical laboratory performs this test?

explanation.summary: Screening a patient's blood for unexpected red blood cell antibodies is a transfusion medicine (blood bank) test.
explanation.whyCorrect: Screening the patient's blood for any unexpected red blood cell antibodies is one of the most common tests performed in the transfusion medicine laboratory, alongside blood typing, Rh typing, and screening for current or past infections. These tests are part of the process of blood product donation and transfusion.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Clinical chemistry measures analytes such as electrolytes, lipids, and hormones.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hematology performs the CBC, body fluid cell counts, and coagulation testing, not transfusion antibody screening.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Immunology and serology identifies antibodies to establish current or past infection or immunity (for example, COVID-19 IgG or Hepatitis B antibodies), not red cell antibodies for transfusion compatibility.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Microbiology identifies micro-organisms and their antibiotic susceptibilities.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Clinical Pathology for Patient Care

questions.stem: A 44-year-old man with end-stage kidney disease is being evaluated as a potential transplant recipient. To determine whether a donor organ would be compatible, his human leukocyte antigen (HLA) type is tested. Which section of the clinical laboratory performs this testing?

explanation.summary: HLA typing to determine transplant compatibility is performed by the immunology and serology laboratory.
explanation.whyCorrect: One of the stated focuses of the immunology and serology laboratory is determining organ, tissue, and fluid compatibility for transplantation by testing a patient for their HLA (human leukocyte antigen) type.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The blood bank determines ABO and Rh type and screens for red cell antibodies for transfusion, not HLA type for organ transplantation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Clinical chemistry runs biochemical tests such as routine chemistries and hormone levels.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hematology performs the CBC, body fluid cell counts, and coagulation testing.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Microbiology identifies micro-organisms and tests antimicrobial susceptibility.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Clinical Pathology for Patient Care

questions.stem: A 4-year-old boy has had repeated serious bacterial infections since infancy. His physician suspects an underactive immune system and orders quantitative immunoglobulin levels. Which section of the clinical laboratory investigates this type of problem?

explanation.summary: Investigating overactive (autoimmune) or underactive (immunodeficiency) immune systems, using tests such as immunoglobulins and rheumatoid factor, is the role of immunology and serology.
explanation.whyCorrect: The immunology and serology laboratory investigates problems with the immune system, whether overactive (autoimmune) or underactive (immunodeficiency disorders). Example testing includes immunoglobulins and rheumatoid factor, so a workup for suspected immunodeficiency with immunoglobulin levels belongs to this section.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The blood bank types blood and prepares transfusion products.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Clinical chemistry measures analytes such as electrolytes, glucose, and hormones.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hematology counts blood cells and evaluates clotting; it does not assess immunoglobulin levels for immune function.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Microbiology would culture the organisms causing his infections but does not evaluate the immune system itself.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Clinical Pathology for Patient Care

questions.stem: A hospital laboratory director reviews the annual test volume from each section. One section is noted to produce more patient results than any other, reflecting that its tests are among the most commonly ordered by healthcare providers. Which section is this most likely to be?

explanation.summary: Clinical chemistry typically produces more patient results than other laboratory sections.
explanation.whyCorrect: The clinical chemistry laboratory uses biochemical and molecular techniques in the diagnosis and management of disease. It typically produces more patient results than other sections of the laboratory, and its tests, such as routine chemistries, lipid testing, and hormone levels, are some of the more commonly ordered tests by healthcare providers.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The blood bank's tests center on blood product donation and transfusion and are not described as the highest-volume section.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Immunology and serology focuses on antibodies, immune disorders, and HLA typing and is not identified as the highest-volume section.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Microbiology focuses on cultures and susceptibility testing and is not identified as the highest-volume section.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Urinalysis evaluates urine only and is not identified as the section producing the most results.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Clinical Pathology for Patient Care

questions.stem: A 33-year-old man with a seizure disorder has a blood level of his anticonvulsant measured to ensure the dose is in the appropriate range. Under which category of testing, and in which section, is this test performed?

explanation.summary: Therapeutic drug monitoring is a toxicology test performed by the clinical chemistry laboratory.
explanation.whyCorrect: Among the most common clinical chemistry tests is toxicology, which includes therapeutic drug monitoring and drugs of abuse testing. Measuring an anticonvulsant level to guide dosing is therapeutic drug monitoring.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Antibody identification confirms infection or immunity, not drug concentrations.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Coagulation testing (PT and PTT) evaluates clotting, not drug levels.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The urinalysis dipstick assesses urine pH, bilirubin, blood, glucose, ketones, leukocyte esterase, nitrites, and protein, not drug levels.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Susceptibility testing determines which antibiotics work against an organism.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Clinical Pathology for Patient Care

questions.stem: A 72-year-old woman taking a blood thinner has a prothrombin time (PT) and partial thromboplastin time (PTT) ordered to evaluate her clotting. Which section of the clinical laboratory may perform these routine coagulation tests?

explanation.summary: Routine coagulation testing such as PT and PTT may be performed by the hematology laboratory.
explanation.whyCorrect: In addition to the complete blood count with differential and body fluid cell counts, the hematology laboratory may also perform routine coagulation testing, with the prothrombin time (PT) and partial thromboplastin time (PTT) given as examples. These help in the diagnosis of clotting disorders.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The blood bank would supply plasma or other products if needed but does not perform routine coagulation testing.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Clinical chemistry runs routine chemistries, lipids, blood gases, toxicology, tumor markers, and hormones, not PT/PTT.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Immunology and serology identifies antibodies and immune disorders.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Urinalysis tests urine only.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Clinical Pathology for Patient Care

questions.stem: A 19-year-old man with fever and neck stiffness undergoes lumbar puncture. One tube of spinal fluid is sent for a cell count and differential to help assess for an inflammatory process. Which section of the clinical laboratory performs this particular analysis?

explanation.summary: Body fluid analysis consisting of a cell count and differential is performed by the hematology laboratory.
explanation.whyCorrect: The hematology laboratory performs routine hematologic testing (CBC with differential) as well as body fluid analysis, specifically cell count and differential, to aid in the diagnosis of hematologic, inflammatory, and clotting disorders. Hematology accepts both blood and body fluids as specimens.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The blood bank accepts only blood, for transfusion-related testing.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Clinical chemistry accepts body fluids for biochemical analysis, not cell counting with a differential.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Microbiology would culture the spinal fluid to identify an organism, but it does not perform the cell count and differential.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Urinalysis accepts only urine.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Clinical Pathology for Patient Care

questions.stem: A 61-year-old man with diabetes undergoes surgical debridement of an infected foot ulcer. A piece of the debrided tissue is sent to the clinical laboratory so that the organism responsible can be identified. Of the sections listed, tissue is an accepted specimen type for which one?

explanation.summary: Microbiology accepts the widest range of specimens, including tissue, to identify infecting micro-organisms.
explanation.whyCorrect: The microbiology laboratory accepts blood, urine, sputum, body fluids, tissue, and stool. It uses chemical, immunologic, and genetic tests, microscopic examination, and staining to identify micro-organisms, making it the destination for tissue sent to identify an infecting organism.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The blood bank accepts only blood.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hematology accepts blood and body fluids, not tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Immunology and serology accepts blood (serum), body fluids, and urine, not tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Urinalysis accepts only urine.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Clinical Pathology for Patient Care

questions.stem: A disk diffusion test is performed on a bacterial isolate from a 55-year-old woman's wound. After incubation, the disk for drug W has no surrounding clear area, drug X has a small clear circle, drug Y has a very large clear circle of inhibited growth, and drug Z has a moderate circle. Based on this test alone, which drug is most likely to be effective against this organism?

choices.label: E
choices.text: None of the drugs, because growth is present on the plate

explanation.summary: In disk diffusion testing, a significant circle of inhibited growth around a disk indicates the antibiotic works against the organism.
explanation.whyCorrect: Disks containing different antibiotics are placed on a plate of the growing organism. A significant circle of inhibited growth around a disk indicates that the antibiotic works against the organism, whereas no circle indicates resistance. Drug Y, with the largest zone of inhibited growth, shows the clearest evidence of activity.

whyWrongByChoice.A: No clear area around drug W indicates the organism is resistant to that medication.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Drug X produced only a small zone, far less inhibition than drug Y.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Drug Z produced a moderate zone, still less inhibition than drug Y.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Growth across the plate is expected; it is the zone of inhibition around each disk that shows drug activity.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Clinical Pathology for Patient Care

questions.stem: A urine specimen from a 30-year-old woman is evaluated in the urinalysis laboratory. The technologist first notes the sample's appearance, then dips a chemical reagent strip into it, and finally examines it under the microscope. Which of the following is assessed by the reagent strip portion of this evaluation?

explanation.summary: The urinalysis dipstick chemical test assesses urine pH, bilirubin, blood, glucose, ketones, leukocyte esterase, nitrites, and protein.
explanation.whyCorrect: The urinalysis laboratory uses a set of tests: a visual exam of appearance, a dipstick chemical test, and a microscopic exam. The dipstick tests include assessments for urine pH, bilirubin, blood, glucose, ketones, leukocyte esterase, nitrites, and protein.

whyWrongByChoice.A: ABO and Rh typing are blood bank tests performed on blood.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A cell count and differential is a hematology body fluid analysis, not a dipstick result.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Organism identification and susceptibility testing are performed by microbiology on a urine culture.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Rheumatoid factor and immunoglobulins are immunology and serology tests.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Clinical Pathology for Patient Care

questions.stem: A medical student mistakenly routes a urine specimen to a laboratory section that accepts only blood and cannot process urine at all. Which of the following sections is this most likely to be?

explanation.summary: The blood bank / transfusion medicine laboratory accepts only blood; urine is accepted by clinical chemistry, immunology/serology, microbiology, and urinalysis.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the summary of specimens accepted by each section, blood bank / transfusion medicine accepts only blood, since its testing centers on blood product donation and transfusion. Urine is an accepted specimen type in the clinical chemistry, immunology/serology, microbiology, and urinalysis laboratories, while hematology accepts blood and body fluids.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Clinical chemistry accepts blood, urine, and body fluids.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Immunology and serology accepts blood (serum), body fluids, and urine.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Microbiology accepts blood, urine, sputum, body fluids, tissue, and stool.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Urinalysis accepts urine exclusively, so it certainly processes urine.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Clinical Pathology for Patient Care
